8.18.9.a.s: api vā mūtayoḥ samopya vivadhaṃ kṛtvā śuṣke sthāṇau valmīkavapāyāṃ vāvadhāyāvatatadhanvā pinākahastaḥ kṛttivāsomiti triravatāmyanti
8.18.9.a.d: अपि वा मूतयोः समोप्य विवधं कृत्वा शुष्के स्थाणौ वल्मीकवपायां वावधायावततधन्वा पिनाकहस्तः कृत्तिवासोमिति त्रिरवताम्यन्ति
8.18.9.a.m: Or having poured them into two woven baskets, having made a carrying-pole, and having placed them on a dry stump or on the crest of an anthill, they hold their breath three times with the formula: 'With unstrung bow, holding the pināka bow in hand, clad in a hide...'

8.18.10.a.d: अपः परिषिच्याप्रतीक्षास्तूष्णीमेत्यैधो ऽस्येधिषीमहीत्याहवनीये समिध आधायापो अन्वचारिषमित्युपतिष्ठन्ते
8.18.10.a.m: Having sprinkled water around, returning silently without looking back, and having placed kindling on the āhavanīya with the formula 'You are kindling; may we kindle,' they worship with the formula 'I have followed the waters.'

8.19.1.a.m: He portions out a mess of boiled rice (caru) in ghee for the Ādityas as before.

8.19.3.a.m: Or a white bull, or one with white lower marks.

8.19.4.a.m: The sacrifice is concluded according to the established procedure.

8.19.5.a.s: āgnāvaiṣṇavamekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapeccakṣuṣkāmo bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ brahmavarcasakāma aindraṃ paśukāmaḥ sārsavataṃ prajākāmaḥ pauṣṇaṃ pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ
8.19.5.a.d: आग्नावैष्णवमेकादशकपालं निर्वपेच्चक्षुष्कामो बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं ब्रह्मवर्चसकाम ऐन्द्रं पशुकामः सार्सवतं प्रजाकामः पौष्णं प्रतिष्ठाकामः
8.19.5.a.m: One who desires sight should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni-and-Viṣṇu; one who desires spiritual luster, a caru to Bṛhaspati; one who desires cattle, [a cake] to Indra; one who desires offspring, [a caru] to Sarasvatī; one who desires stability, [a caru] to Pūṣan.

8.19.6.a.m: Whichever of these he might desire, that one he should offer additionally.

8.19.7.a.m: The offering is completed in the established manner.

8.19.9.a.m: Here, having sacrificed on the full-moon day, the moistening and the rest, up to the shaving, are performed as before,

8.19.9.d.m: “He who makes the plants turn back upon the skin of this earth,

8.19.9.e.m: Agni the ruler through might, Varuṇa along with thoughts,

8.19.9.f.m: Indra together with the Maruts as comrades.”

8.20.1.a.s: tato dvyahe tryahe caturahe 'rdhamāse māsi caturṣu vā māseṣu śunāsīrīyeṇa yajate
8.20.1.a.d: ततो द्व्यहे त्र्यहे चतुरहे ऽर्धमासे मासि चतुर्षु वा मासेषु शुनासीरीयेण यजते
8.20.1.a.m: Then after two days, after three days, after four days, after half a month, after a month, or after four months, he sacrifices with the Śunāsīrīya.

8.20.2.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the Vaiśvadeva.

8.20.3.a.m: At the time of the apportioning, he parcels out the ten subsequent sacrificial substances beginning with the eight-pot-sherd cake for Agni.

8.20.4.a.m: The milk for Vāyu is prepared according to the rule of the morning milking.

8.20.5.b.s: pañca saṃcarāṇi nirupya vāyavyā yavāgūḥ pratidhugvendrāya śunāsīrāya puroḍāśo dvādaśakapālaḥ //
8.20.5.b.d: पञ्च संचराणि निरुप्य वायव्या यवागूः प्रतिधुग्वेन्द्राय शुनासीराय पुरोडाशो द्वादशकपालः ॥
8.20.5.b.m: Having apportioned the five common offerings, there is barley gruel or fresh warm milk for Vāyu, and a twelve-pot-sherd sacrificial cake for Indra Śunāsīra.

8.20.5.c.s: indrāya śunāsīrāya srucā uhuta no haviḥ /
8.20.5.c.d: इन्द्राय शुनासीराय स्रुचा उहुत नो हविः ।
8.20.5.c.m: “For Indra Śunāsīra our sacrificial substance has been offered with the ladle;

8.20.5.d.m: let the wise one accept it!”

8.20.5.e.s: pra havyāni ghṛtavantyasmai haryaśvāya bharatā sajoṣāḥ /
8.20.5.e.d: प्र हव्यानि घृतवन्त्यस्मै हर्यश्वाय भरता सजोषाः ।
8.20.5.e.m: “Offer the ghee-rich sacrificial substances to this driver of bay steeds, united in mind!

8.20.5.f.s: indrartubhirbrahmaṇā vāvṛdhānaḥ śunāsīrī haviridaṃ juṣasveti śunāsīrīyasya yājyānuvākye //
8.20.5.f.d: इन्द्रर्तुभिर्ब्रह्मणा वावृधानः शुनासीरी हविरिदं जुषस्वेति शुनासीरीयस्य याज्यानुवाक्ये ॥
8.20.5.f.m: O Indra, grown great through the seasons by sacred speech, O Śunāsīrī, enjoy this offering!”—these are the yājyā and anuvākyā verses for the Śunāsīrīya offering.

8.20.7.a.m: It has five fore-offerings and three after-offerings, say some.

8.20.8.a.m: With the month-name, “Thou art Saṃsarpa; for Aṃhaspatya thee,” he makes an offering over the one-pot-sherd cake.

8.20.9.a.m: A plow with a team of twelve oxen is the sacrificial gift,

8.20.13.a.m: a white horse, or a white cow for the one-pot-sherd cake.

8.21.1.a.m: “He prays for well-being for the coming year;

8.21.1.b.m: he prays for the heavenly realm,” thus the hotṛ inserts into the blessings of the sūktavāka recitation.

8.21.1.e.m: The offering is completed in the established manner.

8.21.1.g.m: Here, having sacrificed on the full-moon day, the moistening and the rest, up to the shaving, are performed as before,

8.21.1.j.m: “Parameṣṭhin released one month for living beings;

8.21.1.k.m: thereby he brought great immortality to mortals.

8.21.1.l.m: After offspring thou art born; that indeed is thine immortality, O mortal.

8.21.1.m.m: Whereby the months, the half-months, the seasons, the full years [are ordered],

8.21.1.n.s: yena te te prajāpata ījānasya nyavartayan /
8.21.1.n.d: येन ते ते प्रजापत ईजानस्य न्यवर्तयन् ।
8.21.1.n.m: whereby they shaved thine [hair], O Prajāpati, when thou didst sacrifice,

8.21.1.o.m: thereby, by his sacred word, I shave this one for life.”

8.21.2.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Seasonal Sacrifices, he sacrifices with soma or with an animal sacrifice.

8.21.3.a.m: When the Phālguna full moon becomes visible, he undergoes initiation for soma.

8.21.4.a.m: After that, another Phālguna full moon should not pass by him without having sacrificed.

8.21.5.a.m: This is indeed for one who is concluding [the cycle].

8.21.6.a.m: Now for one who is undertaking it again: having sacrificed with the Śunāsīrīya on the fourteenth day of the Phālguna [fortnight],

8.22.1.a.m: he sacrifices with the Vaiśvadeva on the fifteenth.

8.22.2.a.s: etenaiva paśukāmo yajeta yasminnasyartau bhuyiṣṭhaṃ goṣu payaḥ syāt
8.22.2.a.d: एतेनैव पशुकामो यजेत यस्मिन्नस्यर्तौ भुयिष्ठं गोषु पयः स्यात्
8.22.2.a.m: One desiring cattle should sacrifice with this very [rite] in whichever season the milk in his cows would be most abundant.

8.22.3.a.m: One desiring offspring or desiring cattle should sacrifice with this very [rite].

8.22.4.b.s: vaiśvadevenetareṣāṃ parvaṇāṃ sthāne paśukāmo yajeta yāvatsahasraṃ paśūnprāpnuyāt /
8.22.4.b.d: वैश्वदेवेनेतरेषां पर्वणां स्थाने पशुकामो यजेत यावत्सहस्रं पशून्प्राप्नुयात् ।
8.22.4.b.m: One desiring cattle should sacrifice with the Vaiśvadeva in place of the other seasonal offerings until he attains a thousand cattle;

8.22.4.c.m: then he should sacrifice with the other [rites] at their prescribed times.

8.22.5.a.m: One desiring a village should sacrifice with the Śunāsīrīya using rainwater.

8.22.6.a.m: Having collected rainwater, he performs the water-duties with it.

8.22.7.a.s: etenaiva prajākāmaḥ paśukāmaḥ puṣṭikāmo brahmavarcasakāmo 'nnādyakāmo vā yajeta
8.22.7.a.d: एतेनैव प्रजाकामः पशुकामः पुष्टिकामो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामो ऽन्नाद्यकामो वा यजेत
8.22.7.a.m: One desiring offspring, desiring cattle, desiring prosperity, desiring spiritual lustre, or desiring food should sacrifice with this very [rite].

8.22.8.a.m: Through the seasonal offerings, he counts the months in the Seasonal Sacrifices.

8.22.9.a.m: We shall explain the five-year rituals.

8.22.10.a.m: Having sacrificed for three seasonal years, he does not sacrifice for a month;

8.22.10.b.m: having sacrificed for the subsequent two, he desists.

8.22.11.a.s: caitryāṃ tūpakramya dvāviṣṭvā māsamaniṣṭvā trīnparāniṣṭvā viramati
8.22.11.a.d: चैत्र्यां तूपक्रम्य द्वाविष्ट्वा मासमनिष्ट्वा त्रीन्परानिष्ट्वा विरमति
8.22.11.a.m: Having begun, however, on the full moon of Caitra, having sacrificed for two [years], not having sacrificed for a month, and having sacrificed for the subsequent three, he desists.

8.22.14.a.m: or he should repeat them thrice, or indefinitely.

8.22.15.a.s: vijñāyate ca sa triṣutriṣu saṃvatsareṣu māsaṃ na yajata ityetadvacano 'bhyāsaḥ
8.22.15.a.d: विज्ञायते च स त्रिषुत्रिषु संवत्सरेषु मासं न यजत इत्येतद्वचनो ऽभ्यासः
8.22.15.a.m: And it is learned [in the Brāhmaṇa]: 'He does not sacrifice for a month every three years'—such a text indicates repetition.

8.22.16.a.m: In the five-year rituals, the offering to Vaiśvānara and Parjanya and the Pañcahotṛ formula should not recur,

8.22.18.a.m: just like the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice, just like the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice.

9.1.1.a.m: An expiation having scripture as its authority is prescribed upon a transgression of a rule.

9.1.2.a.m: When multiple expiations are taught for a single flaw, they should be combined, because they serve distinct purposes.

9.1.4.a.m: these serve to eliminate the flaw.

9.1.5.a.m: They are to be performed immediately after the flaw.

9.1.6.a.m: Once the flaw is eliminated, the entire rite [is performed] again.

9.1.7.a.m: There is no repetition of it without an explicit injunction.

9.1.8.a.m: One who has added fuel to his fires, when about to set out on a journey, should offer [a libation] with: 'To thee, O greatest of the Aṅgirases…'

9.1.9.a.m: Having mounted the fires separately onto churning sticks, he sets out.

9.1.10.a.m: Where he resides, there he should conclude that sacrifice.

9.1.11.a.s: yadyanvāhitāgnerāhavanīyo 'nugacchedanvagniruṣasāmagramakhyadityanyaṃ praṇīya bhūrityupasthāya yo agniṃ devavītaye haviṣmām̐ āvivāsati /
9.1.11.a.d: यद्यन्वाहिताग्नेराहवनीयो ऽनुगच्छेदन्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यदित्यन्यं प्रणीय भूरित्युपस्थाय यो अग्निं देववीतये हविष्माम्̐ आविवासति ।
9.1.11.a.m: If the āhavanīya fire of one who has added fuel to the fires should go out, having brought forward another with: 'Agni has followed the morning glows…', having attended upon it with: 'Bhūḥ', [and with]: 'He who strives to serve Agni for the feast of the gods with an oblation,

9.1.11.b.m: to him, O Purifier, be gracious, svāhā!'—

9.1.11.c.s: pūrṇaṃ sruvaṃ sarvaprāyaścittaṃ hutvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ity āhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.1.11.c.d: पूर्णं स्रुवं सर्वप्रायश्चित्तं हुत्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्य् आहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.1.11.c.m: having offered a full dipping-spoon as a universal expiation, he should offer an oblation with: 'Viṣṇu strode across this…'

9.1.13.a.m: He should mutter the yajus formula for undertaking the vow mentally.

9.1.14.a.m: Whichever fire should go out, this same [procedure] should be repeated, with the exception of bringing forward [the fire].

9.1.16.a.m: [The fire to be churned or brought for the anvāhāryapacana is] whatever is the origin of the southern fire.

9.1.17.a.s: yadyāhitāgneragnirapakṣāyedā śamyāparāsātpari vājapatiḥ kaviragniriti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ parikramya taṃ saṃbharedidaṃ ta ekaṃ para uta ekaṃ tṛtīyena jyotiṣā saṃviśasva /
9.1.17.a.d: यद्याहिताग्नेरग्निरपक्षायेदा शम्यापरासात्परि वाजपतिः कविरग्निरिति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं परिक्रम्य तं संभरेदिदं त एकं पर उत एकं तृतीयेन ज्योतिषा संविशस्व ।
9.1.17.a.m: If the fire of one who has set up his fires should burn beyond [its hearth] up to a yoke-pin's throw, having walked thrice around it clockwise with: 'Agni, the ruler of spoils, the sage…', he should gather it with: 'This is one of yours, and that other is one; enter together with the third light!

9.1.17.b.s: saṃveśanastanuvai cāruredhi priye devānāṃ parame janitra iti
9.1.17.b.d: संवेशनस्तनुवै चारुरेधि प्रिये देवानां परमे जनित्र इति
9.1.17.b.m: As a gatherer of bodies, be lovely in the dear, highest birthplace of the gods!'

9.1.18.a.m: If it should burn beyond further than that, he should pursue it and pitch camp.

9.1.19.a.m: There he should set apart an eight-potsherd cake for Agni the Path-Maker.

9.1.20.a.m: He should fetch sacrificial grass from near the path.

9.1.21.b.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

9.1.22.a.m: Then, on the next day, he moves back home.

9.1.23.a.s: yasya haviṣe vatsā apākṛtā dhayeyustatsthāne vāyavyāṃ yavāgūṃ nirvapet
9.1.23.a.d: यस्य हविषे वत्सा अपाकृता धयेयुस्तत्स्थाने वायव्यां यवागूं निर्वपेत्
9.1.23.a.m: If calves separated for the oblation should suckle [their mothers], in their place he should set apart barley gruel for Vāyu.

9.1.24.a.m: Then, having separated the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.

9.1.25.a.m: For whom the oblation milked in the evening meets with mishap, having set apart rice grains for Indra, he should observe the fast.

9.1.26.a.m: Whatever [milk] there is in the morning, he should cook it.

9.1.27.a.m: Then the other [offering] should be a cake for Indra.

9.1.28.a.m: Cutting portions from it together with the morning milking, he should proceed.

9.1.29.a.m: This very same is the expiation when the morning milking meets with mishap.

9.1.30.a.m: Cutting portions from it together with the evening milking, he should proceed.

9.1.31.a.m: If both milkings of his should meet with mishap, he should set apart an eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni and a five-cup mess of cooked rice for Indra.

9.1.32.a.m: He should worship Agni with the cake

9.1.33.a.m: Or he should worship both deities with the five-cup mess.

9.1.34.a.m: Then, having separated the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.

9.2.1.a.m: Whose wife should be menstruating on the day of the vow, he should sacrifice having secluded her.

9.2.2.a.m: Behind the altar ground or inside the altar ground, he should spread out her girdle with its cord pointing north.

9.2.3.a.s: yadā trirātrīṇā syādathaināmupahvayetāmūhamasmi sā tvaṃ dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ sāmāhamṛktvaṃ tāvehi saṃbhavāva saha reto dadhāvahai puṃse putrāya vettavai rāyaspoṣāya suprajāstvāya suvīryāyeti
9.2.3.a.d: यदा त्रिरात्रीणा स्यादथैनामुपह्वयेतामूहमस्मि सा त्वं द्यौरहं पृथिवी त्वं सामाहमृक्त्वं तावेहि संभवाव सह रेतो दधावहै पुंसे पुत्राय वेत्तवै रायस्पोषाय सुप्रजास्त्वाय सुवीर्यायेति
9.2.3.a.m: When three nights have passed for her, he should then summon her: 'I am he, you are she; I am the sky, you are the earth; I am the Sāman, you are the Ṛc. Come, let us unite, let us place our seed together, for a male child to be born, for wealth and prosperity, for good offspring, for heroic strength.'

9.2.4.a.s: yasyāgnihotraṃ sāmnāyyaṃ vā viṣyandetodaṅparetya valmīkavapāmuddhṛtya prajāpate na tvadetānīti prājāpatyayarcā valmīkavapāyāmavanīya bhūrityupasthāyānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt /
9.2.4.a.d: यस्याग्निहोत्रं साम्नाय्यं वा विष्यन्देतोदङ्परेत्य वल्मीकवपामुद्धृत्य प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति प्राजापत्ययर्चा वल्मीकवपायामवनीय भूरित्युपस्थायान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात् ।
9.2.4.a.m: If his agnihotra or curd-and-milk oblation should overflow, having gone away to the north, having extracted the interior of an ant-hill, having poured [the spilled liquid] into the ant-hill interior with the verse addressed to Prajāpati: 'O Prajāpati, none other than you…', having attended upon it with 'Bhūḥ', and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.

9.2.4.b.m: If it is the curd-and-milk oblation, he should bring another [portion].

9.2.5.a.s: yadi kīṭo 'vapadyeta madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇena mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivyayarcāntaḥparidhi ninīyānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt /
9.2.5.a.d: यदि कीटो ऽवपद्येत मध्यमेनान्तमेन वा पलाशपर्णेन मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिव्ययर्चान्तःपरिधि निनीयान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात् ।
9.2.5.a.m: If an insect should fall into it, having poured it out inside the enclosing sticks with the middle or outer leaf of a palāśa tree, accompanied by the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth: 'May the great Heaven and Earth for us…', and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.

9.2.5.b.m: If [the milk intended for] the sāṃnāyya [is spoiled], he should fetch another.

9.2.6.a.s: yasyāgnihotramavavarṣenmitro janānkalpayati prajānanmitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyām /
9.2.6.a.d: यस्याग्निहोत्रमववर्षेन्मित्रो जनान्कल्पयति प्रजानन्मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् ।
9.2.6.a.m: If rain falls upon a sacrificer's agnihotra [offering, with the verses]: "Mitra arranges the peoples, knowing well; Mitra sustains the earth and also heaven;

9.2.6.b.s: mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhicaṣṭe satyāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhoteti tatkṛtvānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt
9.2.6.b.d: मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभिचष्टे सत्याय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोतेति तत्कृत्वान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात्
9.2.6.b.m: Mitra looks upon the communities with unwinking eye; offer the oblation rich in clarified butter to Truth"—having performed that [rite] and milked another [cow], he should offer again.

9.2.7.a.s: yadi pūrvasyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmuttarāhutiḥ skandedyadi vottarayā pūrvāmabhijuhuyādyatra vettha vanaspate devānāṃ guhyā nāmāni /
9.2.7.a.d: यदि पूर्वस्यामाहुत्यां हुतायामुत्तराहुतिः स्कन्देद्यदि वोत्तरया पूर्वामभिजुहुयाद्यत्र वेत्थ वनस्पते देवानां गुह्या नामानि ।
9.2.7.a.m: If, after the first offering is offered, the subsequent offering spills, or if he offers over the first with the subsequent one, with [the verse]: "Where thou knowest, O lord of the forest, the secret names of the gods,

9.2.7.b.s: tatra havyāni gāmayoṃta vānaspatyayarcā samidhamādhāya tata eva tūṣṇīṃ hutvānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt
9.2.7.b.d: तत्र हव्यानि गामयोंत वानस्पत्ययर्चा समिधमाधाय तत एव तूष्णीं हुत्वान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात्
9.2.7.b.m: There send the oblations," with this verse addressed to the lord of the forest, having placed a piece of firewood [on the fire], having offered silently right from there, and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.

9.2.8.a.s: yadi pūrvasyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmāhavanīyo 'nugacchedagnirdārau dārāvagniriti vadannanantare śakale hiraṇye vā juhuyāt
9.2.8.a.d: यदि पूर्वस्यामाहुत्यां हुतायामाहवनीयो ऽनुगच्छेदग्निर्दारौ दारावग्निरिति वदन्ननन्तरे शकले हिरण्ये वा जुहुयात्
9.2.8.a.m: If, after the first offering has been offered, the āhavanīya goes out, he should offer upon an unbroken chip of wood or upon gold, reciting: "Agni is in the wood, in the wood is Agni."

9.2.9.a.s: yadi purā prayājebhyo bahiḥparidhyaṅgāraḥ skandettaṃ sruvasya budhnenābhinidadhyānmā tamo mā yajñastamanmā yajamānasyamannamaste astvāyate namo rudra parāyate namo yatra niṣīdasi /
9.2.9.a.d: यदि पुरा प्रयाजेभ्यो बहिःपरिध्यङ्गारः स्कन्देत्तं स्रुवस्य बुध्नेनाभिनिदध्यान्मा तमो मा यज्ञस्तमन्मा यजमानस्यमन्नमस्ते अस्त्वायते नमो रुद्र परायते नमो यत्र निषीदसि ।
9.2.9.a.m: If before the preliminary offerings an ember falls outside the enclosing sticks, he should press it down with the bottom of the sruva, [saying]: "May darkness not [fall upon us], may the sacrifice not faint, may the sacrificer's food not fail; homage be to thee as thou comest, homage, O Rudra, as thou goest away, homage to where thou sittest!

9.2.9.b.s: adhvaryuṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi purastāt /
9.2.9.b.d: अध्वर्युं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि पुरस्तात् ।
9.2.9.b.m: Do not harm the adhvaryu; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the east.

9.2.9.c.s: brahmāṇaṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi dakṣiṇataḥ /
9.2.9.c.d: ब्रह्माणं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि दक्षिणतः ।
9.2.9.c.m: "Do not harm the brahman; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the south.

9.2.9.d.s: hotāraṃ mā hiṃsīḥ patnīṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi paścāt /
9.2.9.d.d: होतारं मा हिंसीः पत्नीं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि पश्चात् ।
9.2.9.d.m: "Do not harm the hotṛ; do not harm the wife; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the west.

9.2.9.e.s: āgnīdhraṃ mā hiṃṣīḥ paśūnmā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadyuttarataḥ
9.2.9.e.d: आग्नीध्रं मा हिंषीः पशून्मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यद्युत्तरतः
9.2.9.e.m: "Do not harm the agnīdh; do not harm the cattle; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the north.

9.2.10.a.s: āhaṃ yajñaṃ dadhe nirṛterupasthāttaṃ devebhyaḥ paridadāmītyenamādāya
9.2.10.a.d: आहं यज्ञं दधे निरृतेरुपस्थात्तं देवेभ्यः परिददामीत्येनमादाय
9.2.10.a.m: Having taken it with [the verse]: "I take up the sacrifice from the lap of Nirṛti; I deliver it to the gods,"

9.3.1.a.m: With [the verse]: "The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, chant-backed, rich in clarified butter, fair-faced;

9.3.1.b.s: mā no hāsīnmetthito nettvā jahāma gopoṣaṃ no vīrapoṣaṃ ca yacchetyenamagnau praharati
9.3.1.b.d: मा नो हासीन्मेत्थितो नेत्त्वा जहाम गोपोषं नो वीरपोषं च यच्छेत्येनमग्नौ प्रहरति
9.3.1.b.m: May he not forsake us, nor may we, united, forsake thee; grant us abundance in cattle and abundance in men," he casts it into the fire.

9.3.2.a.m: Or, having cast it [into the fire], he may offer [an oblation] upon it.

9.3.3.a.s: yadi kālasaṃnikarṣe 'gnirmathyamāno na jāyeta yatrānyaṃ paśyettata āhṛtya juhuyāt
9.3.3.a.d: यदि कालसंनिकर्षे ऽग्निर्मथ्यमानो न जायेत यत्रान्यं पश्येत्तत आहृत्य जुहुयात्
9.3.3.a.m: If at the arrival of the time [of offering], fire being churned is not produced, he should bring [fire] from wherever he sees another and offer.

9.3.4.a.m: Then, not hurrying, he should churn again.

9.3.5.a.s: yadyanyaṃ na vindedajāyai dakṣiṇe karṇe hotavyam
9.3.5.a.d: यद्यन्यं न विन्देदजायै दक्षिणे कर्णे होतव्यम्
9.3.5.a.m: If he cannot find another [fire], the offering should be made in the right ear of a she-goat.

9.3.6.a.m: Thereafter, however, he should not eat [the meat] of a goat.

9.3.7.a.s: yadyajāṃ na vindedbrāhmaṇasya dakṣiṇe haste hotavyam
9.3.7.a.d: यद्यजां न विन्देद्ब्राह्मणस्य दक्षिणे हस्ते होतव्यम्
9.3.7.a.m: If he does not find a she-goat, the offering should be made in the right hand of a brāhmaṇa.

9.3.8.a.m: However, he should not deny shelter to a brāhmaṇa.

9.3.9.a.m: If he does not find a brāhmaṇa, the offering should be made on a clump of darbha grass.

9.3.10.a.m: However, he should not sit upon darbha grass.

9.3.11.a.m: If he does not find darbha grass, the offering should be made in water.

9.3.12.a.s: āpastu na paricakṣītemā bhojanīyā imā abhojanīyā iti
9.3.12.a.d: आपस्तु न परिचक्षीतेमा भोजनीया इमा अभोजनीया इति
9.3.12.a.m: However, he should not disparage waters, saying: "These are fit for consumption, these are unfit for consumption."

9.3.13.a.m: Even [from someone] whose [food] is unfit for consumption, he must accept waters throughout this year.

9.3.14.a.m: However, he should not wash his feet with water.

9.3.15.a.m: "These observances are for one year," says Āśmarathya;

9.3.16.a.m: After a year, he should offer a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati.

9.3.17.a.s: agnaye kṣamavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ yeṣāṃ pūrvāparā anvañcaḥ pramīyeran /
9.3.17.a.d: अग्नये क्षमवते ऽष्टाकपालं येषां पूर्वापरा अन्वञ्चः प्रमीयेरन् ।
9.3.17.a.m: To Agni Kṣāmavat [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if those related senior or junior to him should die in succession,

9.3.18.a.d: अग्नये विविचये ऽष्टाकपालं यस्याहिताग्नेरन्यैरग्निभिरग्नयः संसृजेरन्मिथो वा
9.3.18.a.m: To Agni Vivici [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the fires of an āhitāgni should become commingled with other fires, or with each other.

9.3.19.a.m: To Agni Vipṛc [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the gārhapatya and the āhavanīya [become commingled].

9.3.20.a.s: agninā vipṛcā vayaṃ gīrbhiḥ stomaṃ manāmahe /
9.3.20.a.d: अग्निना विपृचा वयं गीर्भिः स्तोमं मनामहे ।
9.3.20.a.m: "With Agni the separator, we think of a chant with hymns;

9.3.20.c.m: "Agni the sage is kindled, the wise accomplisher of the sacrifice;

9.3.20.d.m: Separating, grant us wealth"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

9.3.21.a.s: agnaye vītaye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ yadi gārhapatyadakṣiṇāgnī dakṣiṇāgnyāhavanīyau vā
9.3.21.a.d: अग्नये वीतये ऽष्टाकपालं यदि गार्हपत्यदक्षिणाग्नी दक्षिणाग्न्याहवनीयौ वा
9.3.21.a.m: To Agni Vīti [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the gārhapatya and the dakṣiṇāgni, or the dakṣiṇāgni and the āhavanīya [become commingled].

9.3.22.a.s: agnaye śucaye 'ṣṭakapālaṃ yadi pradāvyenābhyādāhyena śavāgninā vā //
9.3.22.a.d: अग्नये शुचये ऽष्टकपालं यदि प्रदाव्येनाभ्यादाह्येन शवाग्निना वा ॥
9.3.22.a.m: To Agni Śuci [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [a fire becomes commingled] with a conflagration, with a cremation fire, or with a corpse fire.

9.3.22.b.m: To Agni Saṃkusuka [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [it becomes commingled] with the fire of a lying-in room.

9.3.22.d.m: With beans and clarified butter, with reed firewood, we appease the flesh-consuming fire.

9.3.22.e.m: In this Saṃkusuka fire we wipe away our impurities;

9.3.22.f.s: abhūma yajñiyāḥ śuddhāḥ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣāditi yājyānuvākye //
9.3.22.f.d: अभूम यज्ञियाः शुद्धाः प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषादिति याज्यानुवाक्ये ॥
9.3.22.f.m: We have become worthy of sacrifice, purified; may he prolong our spans of life"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

9.3.22.g.m: To Agni Apsumat [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [it becomes commingled] with fire from lightning.

9.3.23.a.s: yadi sarvāḥ saṃnipateranvivicaye nirupya śucaye nirvapedvrātabhṛtīṃ tṛtīyāmapsumatīṃ caturthīṃ kṣāmavatīmantaṃ parikramayet
9.3.23.a.d: यदि सर्वाः संनिपतेरन्विविचये निरुप्य शुचये निर्वपेद्व्रातभृतीं तृतीयामप्सुमतीं चतुर्थीं क्षामवतीमन्तं परिक्रमयेत्
9.3.23.a.m: If all [types of fires] meet together, having offered to [Agni] Vivici, he should offer to [Agni] Śuci, the [offering] to [Agni] Vrātabhṛt as the third, the [offering] to [Agni] Apsumat as the fourth, and conclude with the [offering] to [Agni] Kṣāmavat.

9.3.24.a.m: Some hand down the offering to [Agni] Vrātabhṛt as the second,

9.4.1.a.m: "Agni, Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Bṛhaspati have cured the leaking womb;

9.4.1.b.s: pṛthivyāmavacuścotaitannābhiprāpnoti nirṛtiṃ parācairityagnihotrasthālīṃ sravantīmabhimantrya vidhuṃ dadrāṇamiti saṃdadhyāt
9.4.1.b.d: पृथिव्यामवचुश्चोतैतन्नाभिप्राप्नोति निरृतिं पराचैरित्यग्निहोत्रस्थालीं स्रवन्तीमभिमन्त्र्य विधुं दद्राणमिति संदध्यात्
9.4.1.b.m: What has dripped upon the earth does not reach Nirṛti below"—addressing the leaking agnihotra pot with this verse, he should join [the crack] with [the formula]: "The moon wandering...."

9.4.2.a.m: It has been stated: "He who offers the New and Full Moon sacrifices should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt."

9.4.3.a.m: Or, [this offering] should be made as the principal rite within the same ritual procedure.

9.4.4.b.s: vi vā etasya yajñaśchidyate yasya yajñe pratate 'ntaretāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapanti /
9.4.4.b.d: वि वा एतस्य यज्ञश्छिद्यते यस्य यज्ञे प्रतते ऽन्तरेतामिष्टिं निर्वपन्ति ।
9.4.4.b.m: "The sacrifice of him in whose extended sacrifice they offer this intermediate offering is indeed severed;

9.4.4.c.s: ya evāsāvāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ yo 'māvāsyāyāṃ tamagnaye pathikṛte kuryāt /
9.4.4.c.d: य एवासावाग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः पौर्णमास्यां यो ऽमावास्यायां तमग्नये पथिकृते कुर्यात् ।
9.4.4.c.m: That cake on eight potsherds for Agni which belongs to the Full Moon, or that which belongs to the New Moon, he should make that one for Agni Pathikṛt;

9.4.4.d.s: tenaiva punaḥ panthāmavaiti na yajñaṃ vicchinattīti vijñāyate
9.4.4.d.d: तेनैव पुनः पन्थामवैति न यज्ञं विच्छिनत्तीति विज्ञायते
9.4.4.d.m: By that very means he finds the path again and does not sever the sacrifice"—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.4.5.a.m: Another [view] is that the two saṃyājyā verses should be those addressed to Agni Pathikṛt.

9.4.6.a.m: It has been stated: "If the moon rises in the east over one whose oblation has been set apart..."

9.4.7.a.m: "If [the moon] rises when it has not yet been set apart, he should set apart [the oblations] for the regular deities," says Āśmarathya.

9.4.8.a.m: When they have become husked rice grains, he should lead [the calves] away.

9.4.9.a.m: 'For the deities whose portions have become altered,' says Ālekhana.

9.4.10.a.m: If [the moon] rises when [the oblation] has been portioned out, the remainder is for the original [deities].

9.4.11.a.m: When they have become husked rice grains, he should lead [the calves] away.

9.4.12.a.m: If [the moon] should rise when his oblation has not yet been taken, or if he should intend the performance of the vow,

9.4.12.b.m: [he should divide] the rice grains into three parts, as before.

9.4.12.c.m: Then, having driven away the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.

9.4.13.a.s: atha yasya gṛhītaṃ havirabhyudiyātsaiva prāyaścittiḥ sā vratacaryā
9.4.13.a.d: अथ यस्य गृहीतं हविरभ्युदियात्सैव प्रायश्चित्तिः सा व्रतचर्या
9.4.13.a.m: Then, if [the moon] should rise when his oblation has been taken, that very expiation [applies], that [same] performance of the vow.

9.4.14.a.s: vatsānmātṛbhiḥ saṃsṛjya punarapākṛtya pūrvedyurdugdhaṃ dadhi havirātañcanārthaṃ nidadhyāt
9.4.14.a.d: वत्सान्मातृभिः संसृज्य पुनरपाकृत्य पूर्वेद्युर्दुग्धं दधि हविरातञ्चनार्थं निदध्यात्
9.4.14.a.m: Having united the calves with their mothers and driven them away again, he should set aside the curd milked on the previous day for the sake of curdling the oblation.

9.4.15.a.s: agnaye vratapataye puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedya āhitāgniḥ sannavratyamiva caretpravasedvā vratye 'hani māṃsaṃ vāśnāti striyaṃ vopaiti
9.4.15.a.d: अग्नये व्रतपतये पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद्य आहिताग्निः सन्नव्रत्यमिव चरेत्प्रवसेद्वा व्रत्ये ऽहनि मांसं वाश्नाति स्त्रियं वोपैति
9.4.15.a.m: He should portion out an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni Vratapati if he, being an āhitāgni, should act as if breaking a vow, or if he should go on a journey, or if on the day of a vow he eats meat or approaches a woman.

9.4.16.a.m: [He should portion out] an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni Vratabhṛt if he should shed tears born of distress.

9.4.17.a.m: 'You, O pure Agni, bearer of vows, seat the gods here,

9.4.17.c.s: vratānubibhradvratapā adābhyo yajā no devām̐ ajaraḥ suvīraḥ /
9.4.17.c.d: व्रतानुबिभ्रद्व्रतपा अदाभ्यो यजा नो देवाम्̐ अजरः सुवीरः ।
9.4.17.c.m: 'Bearing the vows, protector of vows, undeceived, sacrifice to the gods for us, ageless, rich in heroic sons;

9.4.17.d.s: dadhadratnāni suvidāno agne gopāya no jīvase jātaveda iti yājyānuvākye //
9.4.17.d.d: दधद्रत्नानि सुविदानो अग्ने गोपाय नो जीवसे जातवेद इति याज्यानुवाक्ये ॥
9.4.17.d.m: bestowing treasures, well-knowing, O Agni Jātavedas, protect us so that we may live'—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

9.4.17.e.m: Some prescribe the [cake] to Vratabhṛt in case of a journey, and the [cake] to Vratapati in the act of shedding tears.

9.5.1.a.s: yadyagnihotryupasṛṣṭā vāśyeta yasmādbhīṣāvāśiṣṭhāstato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi /
9.5.1.a.d: यद्यग्निहोत्र्युपसृष्टा वाश्येत यस्माद्भीषावाशिष्ठास्ततो नो अभयं कृधि ।
9.5.1.a.m: If the agnihotra-cow, having been brought near, should low: 'From whatever terror you have lowed, make fearlessness for us therefrom;

9.5.1.b.s: abhayaṃ naḥ paśubhyo namo rudrāya mīḍhuṣa iti juhuyādabhi vā mantrayeta
9.5.1.b.d: अभयं नः पशुभ्यो नमो रुद्राय मीढुष इति जुहुयादभि वा मन्त्रयेत
9.5.1.b.m: fearlessness for our animals! Homage to bounteous Rudra!'—with this he should make an oblation or address [the cow].

9.5.2.a.m: And if she should sit down, having addressed her with this same [verse, substituting:] 'From whatever terror you have sat down', and having made her stand up with: 'The divine Aditi, having all forms, has stood up; she has placed life in the lord of the sacrifice;

9.5.2.b.s: indrāya kṛṇvatī bhāgaṃ mitrāya varuṇāya cetyupasthāpya tāṃ dugdhvā brāhmaṇāya dadyādyasyānnaṃ nādyāt /
9.5.2.b.d: इन्द्राय कृण्वती भागं मित्राय वरुणाय चेत्युपस्थाप्य तां दुग्ध्वा ब्राह्मणाय दद्याद्यस्यान्नं नाद्यात् ।
9.5.2.b.m: making a portion for Indra, for Mitra, and for Varuṇa'—and having milked her, he should give [the milk] to a brahmin whose food he would not eat.

9.5.2.c.m: 'He attaches misfortune and evil to him,' it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.5.3.a.m: Or, having driven [her] away or made [her] rise with a stick, beating or not beating, he should keep [her] for himself.

9.5.4.a.s: sūyavasādbhagavatī hi bhūyā atho vayaṃ bhagavantaḥ syāma /
9.5.4.a.d: सूयवसाद्भगवती हि भूया अथो वयं भगवन्तः स्याम ।
9.5.4.a.m: 'May you be fortunate with good pasture, and so may we be fortunate;

9.5.4.b.s: addhi tṛṇamadhnye viśvadānīṃ piba śuddhamudakamācarantīti darbhastambamālupya grāsayet
9.5.4.b.d: अद्धि तृणमध्न्ये विश्वदानीं पिब शुद्धमुदकमाचरन्तीति दर्भस्तम्बमालुप्य ग्रासयेत्
9.5.4.b.m: eat grass, O inviolable cow, at all times; drink pure water as you wander'—having pulled out a clump of darbha grass, he should feed it [to her].

9.5.5.a.s: yadyu vai lohitaṃ duhīta vyutkrāmatetyuktvā dakṣiṇamagniṃ pariśritya tasminnetacchrapayitvā tasminvyāhṛtībhistūṣṇīṃ vā hutvā tāṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyādyamanabhyāgamiṣyansyāt
9.5.5.a.d: यद्यु वै लोहितं दुहीत व्युत्क्रामतेत्युक्त्वा दक्षिणमग्निं परिश्रित्य तस्मिन्नेतच्छ्रपयित्वा तस्मिन्व्याहृतीभिस्तूष्णीं वा हुत्वा तां ब्राह्मणाय दद्याद्यमनभ्यागमिष्यन्स्यात्
9.5.5.a.m: And if she should yield blood, having said: 'Step apart!', having enclosed the southern fire, having boiled this [milk] on it, having offered [oblations] into it with the vyāhṛtis or silently, he should give that [cow] to a brahmin whom he does not intend to visit again.

9.5.6.a.s: yadi duhyamānaṃ skandedyadadya dugdhaṃ pṛthivīmasakta yadoṣadhīrapyasaradyadāpaḥ /
9.5.6.a.d: यदि दुह्यमानं स्कन्देद्यदद्य दुग्धं पृथिवीमसक्त यदोषधीरप्यसरद्यदापः ।
9.5.6.a.m: If [the milk] being milked should spill: 'What milk today has adhered to the earth, what has gone into the plants, what into the waters,

9.5.6.b.s: payo gṛheṣu payo aghniyāsu payo vatseṣu payo astu tanmayityenadabhimantrya samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomītyadbhirupasṛjet
9.5.6.b.d: पयो गृहेषु पयो अघ्नियासु पयो वत्सेषु पयो अस्तु तन्मयित्येनदभिमन्त्र्य समुद्रं वः प्रहिणोमीत्यद्भिरुपसृजेत्
9.5.6.b.m: may there be milk in our houses, milk in the inviolable cows, milk in the calves, milk in me!'—having addressed it with this [verse], he should pour water over it with: 'I send you to the ocean.'

9.5.7.a.m: If [the cow] being milked should break the pot, having washed another, he should milk into it, or into that very one.

9.5.8.a.s: yadi duhyamānaṃ dugdhaṃ hriyamāṇaṃ hṛtamadhiśrīyamāṇamadhiśritamudvāsyamānamudvāsitamunnīyamānamunnītaṃ vā skandettadeva yādṛkkīdṛkca hotavyamanyayā vābhidohyam
9.5.8.a.d: यदि दुह्यमानं दुग्धं ह्रियमाणं हृतमधिश्रीयमाणमधिश्रितमुद्वास्यमानमुद्वासितमुन्नीयमानमुन्नीतं वा स्कन्देत्तदेव यादृक्कीदृक्च होतव्यमन्यया वाभिदोह्यम्
9.5.8.a.m: If [the milk] being milked, having been milked, being carried, having been carried, being placed on [the fire], having been placed on [the fire], being taken off, having been taken off, being drawn up, or having been drawn up should spill, just whatever it is should be offered, or [the milk of] another [cow] should be milked into it.

9.5.9.a.m: If, having been drawn once, it should spill, or twice or thrice, he should not pay heed to that.

9.5.9.b.s: yadyu vai caturthamunnītaṃ skandetsthālyāṃ śeṣamavanīya caturabhyunnīya hotavyamanyayā vābhidohyam
9.5.9.b.d: यद्यु वै चतुर्थमुन्नीतं स्कन्देत्स्थाल्यां शेषमवनीय चतुरभ्युन्नीय होतव्यमन्यया वाभिदोह्यम्
9.5.9.b.m: And if, having been drawn a fourth time, it should spill, having poured the remainder into the pot and having drawn [it] four times, it should be offered, or [the milk of] another [cow] should be milked into it.

9.6.1.a.s: yadyuddrutasya skandettanniṣadya punargṛhītvā tadeva yādṛkkīdṛkca hotavyam /
9.6.1.a.d: यद्युद्द्रुतस्य स्कन्देत्तन्निषद्य पुनर्गृहीत्वा तदेव यादृक्कीदृक्च होतव्यम् ।
9.6.1.a.m: If it should spill of one who has run up, having sat down and taken it again, just whatever it is should be offered.

9.6.1.b.m: Then, having milked another [cow], an offering should be made again.

9.6.1.c.m: Then, having recited an invitatory verse addressed to Varuṇa, he should offer ghee with a consecratory verse addressed to Varuṇa.

9.6.2.a.s: yadi prācīnaṃ skandettadeva yādṛkkīdṛkca hotavyamanyayā vābhidohyam
9.6.2.a.d: यदि प्राचीनं स्कन्देत्तदेव यादृक्कीदृक्च होतव्यमन्यया वाभिदोह्यम्
9.6.2.a.m: If it should spill toward the east, just whatever it is should be offered, or [the milk of] another [cow] should be milked into it.

9.6.3.b.s: yadi prācīnaṃ hriyamāṇaṃ skandetprajāpaterviśvabhṛti tanvaṃ hutamasi svāhetyenadabhimantryaitadevāgnihotraṃ syādityāśmārathyaḥ /
9.6.3.b.d: यदि प्राचीनं ह्रियमाणं स्कन्देत्प्रजापतेर्विश्वभृति तन्वं हुतमसि स्वाहेत्येनदभिमन्त्र्यैतदेवाग्निहोत्रं स्यादित्याश्मारथ्यः ।
9.6.3.b.m: If it should spill while being carried toward the east, having addressed it with: 'You are offered as a body into Prajāpati's all-nourishing [fire], svāhā!', this alone should be the agnihotra, says Āśmarathya.

9.6.3.c.m: 'Having milked another [cow], an offering should be made again,' says Ālekhana.

9.6.4.a.s: yadi puraḥ parāhṛtaṃ skandedanūdāhṛtya caturabhyunnīya hotavyamanyayā vābhidohyam
9.6.4.a.d: यदि पुरः पराहृतं स्कन्देदनूदाहृत्य चतुरभ्युन्नीय होतव्यमन्यया वाभिदोह्यम्
9.6.4.a.m: If it should spill after being carried forward, having brought [more milk] after it and having drawn it four times, it should be offered, or [the milk of] another [cow] should be milked into it.

9.6.5.a.s: yadi pura upasannaṃ skandettadeva yādṛkkīdṛkca hotavyamanyayā vābhidohyam
9.6.5.a.d: यदि पुर उपसन्नं स्कन्देत्तदेव यादृक्कीदृक्च होतव्यमन्यया वाभिदोह्यम्
9.6.5.a.m: If it should spill when placed in front [of the fire], just whatever it is should be offered, or [the milk of] another [cow] should be milked into it.

9.6.6.b.s: yadi pura upasannamahutaṃ skandettadeva yādṛkkīdṛkca hotavyam /
9.6.6.b.d: यदि पुर उपसन्नमहुतं स्कन्देत्तदेव यादृक्कीदृक्च होतव्यम् ।
9.6.6.b.m: If it should spill unoffered when placed in front [of the fire], just whatever it is should be offered.

9.6.6.c.m: Then, having milked another [cow], an offering should be made again.

9.6.6.d.m: Then with ghee [he offers to] Varuṇa—the rest is the same.

9.6.7.a.m: 'The sky has spilled onto the earth; the youthful bull has spilled onto the cows;

9.6.7.b.s: skannemā viśvā bhuvanā skanno yañaḥ prajanayatu //
9.6.7.b.d: स्कन्नेमा विश्वा भुवना स्कन्नो यञः प्रजनयतु ॥
9.6.7.b.m: having spilled, [may it quicken] all these worlds; may the spilled sacrifice produce offspring!

9.6.7.c.m: It has spilled, it has been born, related to Prajāpati; from what has spilled a bull is born;

9.6.7.d.m: from what has spilled may we be born with offspring'—having addressed what has spilled with this [formula], he should pour water over it with: 'Make the earth swell!'

9.6.8.a.m: Whatever is not the measure of an oblation is merely a drop.

9.6.9.a.m: If it should spill in the evening, he should not eat until the morning offering.

9.6.9.b.m: If in the morning, he should not eat until the evening offering.

9.6.10.a.m: A divine thunderbolt indeed comes down upon him whose agnihotra [milk] hisses;

9.6.10.b.m: he should say: 'Burn so-and-so!', naming the one whom he hates.

9.6.11.a.s: yasyāgnihotre 'dhiśrite śvāntarāgnī dhāvedgārhapatyādbhasmādāyedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti vaiṣṇavyarcāhavanīyāddhvaṃsayannuddrutyaitayaiva bhasmanā śunaḥ padamapivapet
9.6.11.a.d: यस्याग्निहोत्रे ऽधिश्रिते श्वान्तराग्नी धावेद्गार्हपत्याद्भस्मादायेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति वैष्णव्यर्चाहवनीयाद्ध्वंसयन्नुद्द्रुत्यैतयैव भस्मना शुनः पदमपिवपेत्
9.6.11.a.m: If a dog should run between the fires while his agnihotra is placed on [the fire], having taken ashes from the gārhapatya, scattering them from the āhavanīya with the verse addressed to Viṣṇu: 'Through this Viṣṇu strode...', having run up, he should strew the dog's footprint with ashes with this very [verse].

9.6.12.a.s: yasyāgnimanāhṛtaṃ sūryo 'bhinimrocedyatra dīpyamānaṃ parāpaśyettata āhṛtyaitaṃ praviśānīti vaiṣa ādhīyate
9.6.12.a.d: यस्याग्निमनाहृतं सूर्यो ऽभिनिम्रोचेद्यत्र दीप्यमानं परापश्येत्तत आहृत्यैतं प्रविशानीति वैष आधीयते
9.6.12.a.m: If the sun should set while his fire has not been brought [forward], having fetched it from where he sees it burning in the distance, it is established with: 'May I enter this.'

9.6.13.a.m: Such is the procedure for establishing the dakṣiṇāgni when it has become extinguished.

9.6.14.a.m: If the sun should set while his fire has not been taken out [from the gārhapatya]:

9.7.1.a.m: Having tied gold with a blade of darbha grass, he should carry it in front.

9.7.1.b.m: Behind [it], an Ārṣeya brahmin of great learning should take out the fire.

9.7.1.c.m: Behind [him], he should run after with the agnihotra [milk].

9.7.1.d.s: āyatane hiraṇye 'gniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya nityamagnihotramupasādyā tamitoraprāṇannāsitvā samanya hutvā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarityupasthāya vāruṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapet
9.7.1.d.d: आयतने हिरण्ये ऽग्निं प्रतिष्ठाप्य नित्यमग्निहोत्रमुपसाद्या तमितोरप्राणन्नासित्वा समन्य हुत्वा भूर्भुवः सुवरित्युपस्थाय वारुणं चरुं निर्वपेत्
9.7.1.d.m: Having established the fire on gold in its proper place, having set down the regular agnihotra, having sat without exhaling until exhaustion, having breathed out and offered, and having attended upon [the fire] with 'Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ', he should set apart a cooked mess for Varuṇa.

9.7.2.a.m: Some teach a second [offering] dedicated to the Vrātabhṛts;

9.7.2.b.m: some teach that the bringing forward is done without gold.

9.7.3.a.s: yadi sāyamagnihotrakālo 'tipadyeta doṣā vastornamaḥ svāheti kālasamāpādanīyaṃ homaṃ hutvā nityamagnihotramupasādyā tamitoraprāṇannāsitvā samanya hutvā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvar ity upatiṣṭheta
9.7.3.a.d: यदि सायमग्निहोत्रकालो ऽतिपद्येत दोषा वस्तोर्नमः स्वाहेति कालसमापादनीयं होमं हुत्वा नित्यमग्निहोत्रमुपसाद्या तमितोरप्राणन्नासित्वा समन्य हुत्वा भूर्भुवः सुवर् इत्य् उपतिष्ठेत
9.7.3.a.m: If the time for the evening agnihotra should pass, having offered the oblation that adjusts the proper time with: 'In the evening and in the morning, reverence, svāhā!', having set down the regular agnihotra, having sat without exhaling until exhaustion, having breathed out and offered, he should attend upon [the fire] with 'Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ'.

9.7.4.a.s: yadi prātaḥ prātarvastornamaḥ svāheti kālasamāpādanīyaṃ homaṃ hutvā nityamagnihotramupasādyā tamitoraprāṇannāsitvā samanya hutvā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvar ity upatiṣṭheta
9.7.4.a.d: यदि प्रातः प्रातर्वस्तोर्नमः स्वाहेति कालसमापादनीयं होमं हुत्वा नित्यमग्निहोत्रमुपसाद्या तमितोरप्राणन्नासित्वा समन्य हुत्वा भूर्भुवः सुवर् इत्य् उपतिष्ठेत
9.7.4.a.m: If [it is] in the morning, having offered the time-fitting libation with "In the morning, to the light, homage, svāhā!", having set down the regular agnihotra, having sat without breathing until [he feels] suffocated, having breathed out and offered, he should worship [the sun] with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ!"

9.7.6.a.s: hutvāhavanīyamudvāpyānvagniruṣasāmagramakhyadityanyaṃ praṇīyehaiva kṣemya edhi mā prahāsīnmāmumāmuṣyāyaṇamityādityamupasthāya maitraṃ caruṃ nirvapet
9.7.6.a.d: हुत्वाहवनीयमुद्वाप्यान्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यदित्यन्यं प्रणीयेहैव क्षेम्य एधि मा प्रहासीन्मामुमामुष्यायणमित्यादित्यमुपस्थाय मैत्रं चरुं निर्वपेत्
9.7.6.a.m: Having offered, having extinguished the āhavanīya, having brought forward another [fire] with "Agni has seen the front of the dawns...", and having worshipped the sun with "Be prosperous right here; do not abandon me, such and such a person, son of such and such!", he should offer a caru to Mitra.

9.7.7.a.m: Some teach [a cake] on one potsherd to Sūrya.

9.7.8.a.m: When the sacrifice is completed, the sacrificer and his wife remain fasting and restrained in speech on that day, kindling only the āhavanīya.

9.7.9.a.m: He should offer the evening agnihotra with the milk of two [cows], as before.

9.7.10.a.m: If the sun rises upon one whose fire has not been taken out, he should carry ghee taken in four ladlings to the front;

9.7.10.b.m: following [him], a learned brāhmaṇa of ṛṣi-descent should take out the fire;

9.7.10.c.m: following [him], he should run forward with the agnihotra [milk].

9.7.10.d.s: āyatane 'gniṃ pratiṣṭhāpyoṣāḥ ketunā juṣatāṃ yajñaṃ devebhiranvitam /
9.7.10.d.d: आयतने ऽग्निं प्रतिष्ठाप्योषाः केतुना जुषतां यज्ञं देवेभिरन्वितम् ।
9.7.10.d.m: Having established the fire in its place, [with the verse:] "May Dawn with her banner enjoy the sacrifice attended by the gods,

9.7.10.e.m: most sweet to the gods, svāhā!"—sitting down facing west, he should make an offering with ghee.

9.7.11.a.m: That same is the rite of offering the agnihotra.

9.7.11.b.m: The expiation for that is the one for [the agnihotra whose] time has elapsed in the morning.

9.7.12.b.m: he does not extinguish the āhavanīya here.

9.7.13.b.m: If the sun sets or rises upon one whose fire has not been taken out,

9.8.1.a.s: mano jyotirjuṣatāṃ trayastriṃśattantava iti dve caturgṛhīte juhuyāt
9.8.1.a.d: मनो ज्योतिर्जुषतां त्रयस्त्रिंशत्तन्तव इति द्वे चतुर्गृहीते जुहुयात्
9.8.1.a.m: he should offer two four-fold ladlings [of ghee] with "May the mind enjoy the light..." and "Thirty-three threads...".

9.8.2.a.s: yasya viprakrāntamahutamagnihotraṃ sūryo 'bhyudiyādyathā vijaniṣyamāṇo na vijāyeta tādṛktat /
9.8.2.a.d: यस्य विप्रक्रान्तमहुतमग्निहोत्रं सूर्यो ऽभ्युदियाद्यथा विजनिष्यमाणो न विजायेत तादृक्तत् ।
9.8.2.a.m: If the sun rises upon one whose agnihotra has been carried out but not offered, it is like [a woman] about to give birth who does not give birth;

9.8.2.b.s: ātmānaṃ vā ha yajamāno ruṇaddhi sarvajyāniṃ vā jīyate /
9.8.2.b.d: आत्मानं वा ह यजमानो रुणद्धि सर्वज्यानिं वा जीयते ।
9.8.2.b.m: either the sacrificer obstructs himself, or he suffers total loss.

9.8.2.c.s: nityamagnihotramupasādyā tamitoraprāṇannāsitvā samanya hutvā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarityupatiṣṭheta /
9.8.2.c.d: नित्यमग्निहोत्रमुपसाद्या तमितोरप्राणन्नासित्वा समन्य हुत्वा भूर्भुवः सुवरित्युपतिष्ठेत ।
9.8.2.c.m: Having set down the regular agnihotra, having sat without breathing until [he feels] suffocated, having breathed out and offered, he should worship [the sun] with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ!"

9.8.3.a.m: Having offered, having extinguished it, the re-establishment [of the fires] is its expiation—so says Āśmarathya.

9.8.4.b.m: If it is at the end, having ladled out [the milk], he should run out towards the east.

9.8.4.c.m: Having set it down, he should sit until [he feels] suffocated.

9.8.4.d.s: sa yadā tāmyedatha bhūḥ svāheti juhuyāt /
9.8.4.d.d: स यदा ताम्येदथ भूः स्वाहेति जुहुयात् ।
9.8.4.d.m: When he suffocates, then he should offer with: "Bhūḥ svāhā!"

9.8.4.e.s: prajāpatirvai bhūtastamevopāsaretsa evainaṃ tata unnayati nārtimārchati yajamāna iti vijñāyate
9.8.4.e.d: प्रजापतिर्वै भूतस्तमेवोपासरेत्स एवैनं तत उन्नयति नार्तिमार्छति यजमान इति विज्ञायते
9.8.4.e.m: "Prajāpati, indeed, is Bhūḥ; he approaches him; he raises him from that; the sacrificer suffers no affliction"—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.8.5.a.s: yasyāgnihotraṃ vicchidyeta dvyahe tryahe caturahe vāgnaye tantumate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet
9.8.5.a.d: यस्याग्निहोत्रं विच्छिद्येत द्व्यहे त्र्यहे चतुरहे वाग्नये तन्तुमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत्
9.8.5.a.m: One whose agnihotra has been interrupted for two days, three days, or four days should offer [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni Tantumat.

9.8.6.a.s: svayaṃ kṛṇvānaḥ sugamaprayāvaṃ tigmaśṛṅgo vṛṣabhaḥ śośucānaḥ /
9.8.6.a.d: स्वयं कृण्वानः सुगमप्रयावं तिग्मशृङ्गो वृषभः शोशुचानः ।
9.8.6.a.m: "Making for himself an easy path, unhindered, / the sharp-horned bull gleaming bright,

9.8.6.b.m: beholding his ancient dwelling-place, / Agni has extended the divine thread."

9.8.6.c.s: tvaṃ nastanturuta seturagne tvaṃ panthā bhavasi devayānaḥ /
9.8.6.c.d: त्वं नस्तन्तुरुत सेतुरग्ने त्वं पन्था भवसि देवयानः ।
9.8.6.c.m: "Thou art our thread and our bridge, O Agni; / thou becomest the path leading to the gods.

9.8.6.d.s: tvayāgne pṛṣṭhaṃ vayamāruhemāthā devaiḥ sadhamādaṃ mademeti yajyānuvākye
9.8.6.d.d: त्वयाग्ने पृष्ठं वयमारुहेमाथा देवैः सधमादं मदेमेति यज्यानुवाक्ये
9.8.6.d.m: By thee, O Agni, may we mount to the ridge / and rejoice together with the gods"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

9.8.7.a.s: tantuṃ tanvannudbudhyasvāgna uduttamamudvayaṃ tamasasparyudu tyaṃ citramityupahomāḥ
9.8.7.a.d: तन्तुं तन्वन्नुद्बुध्यस्वाग्न उदुत्तममुद्वयं तमसस्पर्युदु त्यं चित्रमित्युपहोमाः
9.8.7.a.m: "Extending the thread...", "Wake up, O Agni...", "The highest...", "Looking upon the higher light above the darkness...", "The bright face of the gods has arisen..."—these are the minor libations.

9.8.8.a.m: "Bearer of the oblation, vanquisher of foes, / slayer of demons, victorious in battles, / full of light, shining, wise— / we summon Agni Sviṣṭakṛt."

9.8.8.b.m: Luminous, shining, generous, / Agni Sviṣṭakṛt let us invoke.

9.8.8.c.s: sviṣṭamagne abhi tatpṛṇāhi viśvā deva pṛtanā abhiṣya /
9.8.8.c.d: स्विष्टमग्ने अभि तत्पृणाहि विश्वा देव पृतना अभिष्य ।
9.8.8.c.m: "O Agni, fulfill that which is well offered; / overpower all hosts, O god!

9.8.8.d.s: uruṃ naḥ panthāṃ pradiśanvibhāhi jyotiṣmaddhehyajaraṃ na āyuriti saṃyājye
9.8.8.d.d: उरुं नः पन्थां प्रदिशन्विभाहि ज्योतिष्मद्धेह्यजरं न आयुरिति संयाज्ये
9.8.8.d.m: Shine forth, pointing out to us a wide path; / bestow on us an unaging life full of light!"—these are the two saṃyājyā verses.

9.9.1.a.s: yasyāhavanīye 'nudvāte gārhapatya udvāyedāhavanīyamudvāpya gārhapatyaṃ mantheditaḥ prathamaṃ jajñe agnirityetayā /
9.9.1.a.d: यस्याहवनीये ऽनुद्वाते गार्हपत्य उद्वायेदाहवनीयमुद्वाप्य गार्हपत्यं मन्थेदितः प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरित्येतया ।
9.9.1.a.m: If, while his āhavanīya is not extinguished, the gārhapatya should go out, having extinguished the āhavanīya, he should churn out the gārhapatya with this verse: "Agni was born first from here...".

9.9.1.b.s: agne samrāḍiṣe rayyai ramasva sahase dyumnāyorjapatyāyetyabhimantrya samrāḍasi virāḍasi sārasvatu tvotsau samindhātāmannādaṃ tvānnapatyāyetyupasamidhyānvagniruṣasāmagramakhyadityanyaṃ praṇīyāgnaye tapasvate janadvate pāvakavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet
9.9.1.b.d: अग्ने सम्राडिषे रय्यै रमस्व सहसे द्युम्नायोर्जपत्यायेत्यभिमन्त्र्य सम्राडसि विराडसि सारस्वतु त्वोत्सौ समिन्धातामन्नादं त्वान्नपत्यायेत्युपसमिध्यान्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यदित्यन्यं प्रणीयाग्नये तपस्वते जनद्वते पावकवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत्
9.9.1.b.m: Having addressed [the fire] with "O Agni, sovereign, delight in food and wealth, in strength, splendor, and abundance of food!", having kindled it with "Thou art a sovereign, thou art an emperor; may the two Sarasvatī springs kindle thee; thee, the eater of food, for food-lordship!", and having brought forward another [fire] with "Agni has seen the front of the dawns...", he should offer [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni Tapasvat Janadvat Pāvakavat.

9.9.2.a.m: Some teach this sacrifice on extinction under all circumstances.

9.9.3.a.m: "Come with heat among men, O Agni, / purifying with your flame,

9.9.3.c.s: ā no yāhi tapasā janeṣvagne pāvaka dīdyat /
9.9.3.c.d: आ नो याहि तपसा जनेष्वग्ने पावक दीद्यत् ।
9.9.3.c.m: "Come to us with heat among men, / O Agni, shining, purifying,

9.9.3.d.m: placing our oblations among the gods!"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

9.9.4.a.d: आहवनीये ऽनुगते ऽग्नये ज्योतिष्मते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपति
9.9.4.a.m: If the āhavanīya is extinguished, he offers [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni Jyotiṣmat,

9.9.6.a.s: yadi sāyamahute 'gnihotre pūrvo 'gniranugacchedadhiśrityāgnihotramunnīya vāgninā ca sahāgnihotreṇa cānuddravet /
9.9.6.a.d: यदि सायमहुते ऽग्निहोत्रे पूर्वो ऽग्निरनुगच्छेदधिश्रित्याग्निहोत्रमुन्नीय वाग्निना च सहाग्निहोत्रेण चानुद्द्रवेत् ।
9.9.6.a.m: If, in the evening before the agnihotra is offered, the eastern fire should go out, having put the agnihotra [milk] on the fire or having ladled it out, he should run forward together with the fire and the agnihotra [milk];

9.9.6.b.m: a learned brāhmaṇa should take it out;

9.9.6.c.m: whatever wealth he would not previously have given, that he should give.

9.9.6.d.m: "He removes him by means of that which is unshaken"—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.9.7.a.s: yadi prātarahute 'gnihotre 'paro 'gniranugacchedanugamayitvā pūrvaṃ pūrvavanmathitvāparaṃ pūrvavaduddhṛtya jhuyāt
9.9.7.a.d: यदि प्रातरहुते ऽग्निहोत्रे ऽपरो ऽग्निरनुगच्छेदनुगमयित्वा पूर्वं पूर्ववन्मथित्वापरं पूर्ववदुद्धृत्य झुयात्
9.9.7.a.m: If, in the morning before the agnihotra is offered, the western fire should go out, having extinguished the eastern one, having churned out the western one as before, and having taken out [the eastern one] as before, he should offer.

9.9.8.a.s: yadi tvareta pūrvamanvavasāya tataḥ prāṅuddhṛtya juhuyāt
9.9.8.a.d: यदि त्वरेत पूर्वमन्ववसाय ततः प्राङुद्धृत्य जुहुयात्
9.9.8.a.m: If he should be in a hurry, having transferred the eastern [fire to the gārhapatya] and having taken it out towards the east from there, he should offer.

9.9.9.a.d: जमि तु तद्यो ऽस्य पूर्वस्तमपरं करोति ।
9.9.9.a.m: It is, however, an excess when one turns what is his eastern fire into the western fire;

9.9.9.b.m: having transferred it elsewhere, having churned out the western one as before, and having taken out [the eastern one] as before, he should offer.

9.9.9.d.d: श्वोभुते ऽग्नये तपस्वते जनद्वत इति समानम्
9.9.9.d.m: on the next day, [the rite] to Agni Tapasvat Janadvat is the same.

9.9.10.b.m: If someone's fire should go out, he should not pay heed to the time;

9.9.10.c.m: having extinguished the eastern one, having churned out the western one as before, and having taken out [the eastern one] as before, he should offer.

9.9.10.d.m: He should prepare a twelve-pot-sherd cake for Agni Vaiśvānara [and] a barley pap for Varuṇa.

9.9.11.a.s: yadi gārhaptaya āhavanīyo vānugacchettebhya evāvakṣāṇebhyo 'dhi manthitavyaḥ /
9.9.11.a.d: यदि गार्हप्तय आहवनीयो वानुगच्छेत्तेभ्य एवावक्षाणेभ्यो ऽधि मन्थितव्यः ।
9.9.11.a.m: If the gārhapatya or the āhavanīya should go out, it should be churned out from those very embers.

9.9.11.b.s: yadi na tādṛśānīvāvakṣāṇāni syurbhasmanāraṇī saṃsparśya manthitavyaḥ /
9.9.11.b.d: यदि न तादृशानीवावक्षाणानि स्युर्भस्मनारणी संस्पर्श्य मन्थितव्यः ।
9.9.11.b.m: If there should not be such embers, it should be churned after touching the two churning sticks with ashes.

9.9.11.c.m: "He produces it from its own womb," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.9.12.a.m: Likewise when ignited with dung or ignited with grass.

9.9.13.a.m: [The rule] "For Agni possessing heat, accompanied by people" is the same.

9.9.14.a.s: anugateṣṭervā sthāna etā āhutīrjuhuyānmitrāya svāhā varuṇā svāhāgnaye svāhāgnaye vratapataye svāhāgnaye tapasvate janadvate pāvakavate svāhāgnaye śucaye svāhāgnaye jyotiṣmate svāhā sūryāya svāheti vyāhṛtībhirvihṛtābhiḥ samastābhiśca juhuyāt
9.9.14.a.d: अनुगतेष्टेर्वा स्थान एता आहुतीर्जुहुयान्मित्राय स्वाहा वरुणा स्वाहाग्नये स्वाहाग्नये व्रतपतये स्वाहाग्नये तपस्वते जनद्वते पावकवते स्वाहाग्नये शुचये स्वाहाग्नये ज्योतिष्मते स्वाहा सूर्याय स्वाहेति व्याहृतीभिर्विहृताभिः समस्ताभिश्च जुहुयात्
9.9.14.a.m: Or, in place of the sacrifice for the extinguished fire, he should offer these oblations: "To Mitra hail! To Varuṇa hail! To Agni hail! To Agni, lord of vows, hail! To Agni possessing heat, accompanied by people, possessing purifying power, hail! To Agni the pure hail! To Agni the luminous hail! To Sūrya hail!"—[and] he should offer with the sacred utterances separately and together.

9.10.1.a.m: If the āhavanīya should go out before the time of offering, he should bring forth another from the gārhapatya.

9.10.2.a.s: yadi homakale praṇa udānamapayagāditi gārhapatye juhuyāt
9.10.2.a.d: यदि होमकले प्रण उदानमपयगादिति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात्
9.10.2.a.m: If at the time of offering, he should offer into the gārhapatya with: "The out-breath has merged into the up-breath."

9.10.3.a.m: If the gārhapatya [goes out], into the āhavanīya with: "The up-breath has merged into the out-breath."

9.10.4.a.m: If the southern fire [goes out], into the gārhapatya with: "The cross-breath has merged into the up-breath."

9.10.5.a.s: yadi sarve 'nugaccheyuragniṃ mathitvā yāṃ diśaṃ vāto vāyāttāṃ diśamuddhṛtya vāyave svāheti juhuyāt
9.10.5.a.d: यदि सर्वे ऽनुगच्छेयुरग्निं मथित्वा यां दिशं वातो वायात्तां दिशमुद्धृत्य वायवे स्वाहेति जुहुयात्
9.10.5.a.m: If all should go out, having churned fire, taking it out in whichever direction the wind blows, he should offer with: "To Vāyu hail!"

9.10.6.a.s: yadyu vai nivāte mathitvā vihāraṃ sādhayitvāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ yajamāna upaviśya svayamagnihotraṃ pibet /
9.10.6.a.d: यद्यु वै निवाते मथित्वा विहारं साधयित्वापरेणाहवनीयं यजमान उपविश्य स्वयमग्निहोत्रं पिबेत् ।
9.10.6.a.m: If, however, in a windless place, having churned, having arranged the sacrificial layout, the sacrificer, sitting to the west of the āhavanīya, should himself drink the agnihotra;

9.10.6.b.m: "It becomes a substitution for the agnihotra," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.10.7.a.s: yadi prāgastamayājjuhuyātpunarevāstamite hutvā bhavataṃ naḥ samanasāvityupatiṣṭheta
9.10.7.a.d: यदि प्रागस्तमयाज्जुहुयात्पुनरेवास्तमिते हुत्वा भवतं नः समनसावित्युपतिष्ठेत
9.10.7.a.m: If he should offer before sunset, having offered again once it has set, he should attend upon [the fire] with: "Be of one mind with us..."

9.10.8.a.m: If in the dead of night, having offered again at dawn, he should attend upon [the fire] with this very [formula].

9.10.9.a.m: If, while sprinkling the oblation, he should sprinkle upon the fire, he should sacrifice with a sacrifice of clarified butter.

9.10.9.b.m: He should rekindle the fire with: "May the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus rekindle you..."

9.10.10.a.m: Thus in all damages to the fires.

9.10.11.a.m: He on whose fire they bring forth another fire should offer an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni possessed of fire.

9.10.12.a.m: "In whatever manner they bring it forth, there is expiation," says Āśmarathya.

9.10.12.b.s: yadyasaṃnyupte spāśayeyuranugamayeyurenaṃ na prāyaścittam ity ālekhanaḥ
9.10.12.b.d: यद्यसंन्युप्ते स्पाशयेयुरनुगमयेयुरेनं न प्रायश्चित्तम् इत्य् आलेखनः
9.10.12.b.m: "If, before [the oblation] is poured together, they perceive it [and] extinguish it, there is no expiation," says Ālekhana.

9.10.13.a.m: "An eight-pot-sherd [cake] to Agni the luminous" has been stated.

9.10.14.a.m: Then he should offer an oblation with: "The thirty-three threads..."

9.10.15.a.s: yasya sāṃnāyye 'dhiśrite haviṣi vā nirupte puruṣāḥ śvāno ratho vāntarāgnī vīyāddurvarāhaiḍako vā tadatrāpo 'nvatiṣicya gāmanvatyāvartayedvardhatāṃ bhūtirdadhnā ghṛtena muñcatu yajño yajñapatimaṃhasaḥ svāheti
9.10.15.a.d: यस्य सांनाय्ये ऽधिश्रिते हविषि वा निरुप्ते पुरुषाः श्वानो रथो वान्तराग्नी वीयाद्दुर्वराहैडको वा तदत्रापो ऽन्वतिषिच्य गामन्वत्यावर्तयेद्वर्धतां भूतिर्दध्ना घृतेन मुञ्चतु यज्ञो यज्ञपतिमंहसः स्वाहेति
9.10.15.a.m: If, when the milk oblation has been set on the fire or the oblation has been poured out, men, dogs, or a chariot, or a wild boar or a ram should cross between the fires, having poured water along there, he should make a cow walk along it with: "May prosperity increase with curd and ghee; may the sacrifice release the lord of the sacrifice from distress, hail!"

9.10.16.a.s: devāñjanamaganyajñastato mā yajñasyāśīrāgacchatu pitṝnpañcajanāndiśa āpa oṣadhīrvanaspatīñjanamaganyajñastato mā yajñasyāśrīrāgacchatviti ṣaḍāhutīrhutvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti vartma samūhe /
9.10.16.a.d: देवाञ्जनमगन्यज्ञस्ततो मा यज्ञस्याशीरागच्छतु पितॄन्पञ्चजनान्दिश आप ओषधीर्वनस्पतीञ्जनमगन्यज्ञस्ततो मा यज्ञस्याश्रीरागच्छत्विति षडाहुतीर्हुत्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति वर्त्म समूहे ।
9.10.16.a.m: Having offered six oblations with: "The sacrifice has gone to the divine people; thence may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me! To the ancestors, to the five classes of men, to the quarters, to the waters, to the plants and trees, the sacrifice has gone to the people; thence may the prosperity of the sacrifice come to me!", he sweeps together the tracks with: "This Viṣṇu strode..."

9.10.17.a.s: yasyāno vā ratho vāntarāgnī yatyāhavanīyamudvāpya gārhapatyāduddharedyadagne pūrvaṃ prabhṛtaṃ padaṃ hi te sūryasya raśmīnanvātatāna /
9.10.17.a.d: यस्यानो वा रथो वान्तराग्नी यत्याहवनीयमुद्वाप्य गार्हपत्यादुद्धरेद्यदग्ने पूर्वं प्रभृतं पदं हि ते सूर्यस्य रश्मीनन्वाततान ।
9.10.17.a.m: For him between whose fires a cart or a chariot passes, having extinguished the āhavanīya, he should take it out from the gārhapatya with: "Since, O Agni, your former brought-forward step stretched along the rays of the sun,

9.10.17.b.s: tatra rayiṣṭhāmanusaṃbharaitaṃ saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā //
9.10.17.b.d: तत्र रयिष्ठामनुसंभरैतं सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या ॥
9.10.17.b.m: there bring together this resting upon wealth; unite us with good, prize-bearing favor."

9.10.17.c.m: [and] with these two: "You, O Agni, are wide-reaching..."

9.10.17.d.m: Then he should offer a cake to Agni Pathikṛt as before.

9.11.2.a.m: or for him whose fires they cross with fires, or who crosses [them himself];

9.11.3.a.m: or for him between whose fires they distribute fires;

9.11.5.a.m: With the milk of a cow whose calf is fostered by another, he should offer the agnihotra for him until the contact of the body with the fires.

9.11.8.a.s: ye purodañco darbhāstāndakṣiṇāgrānkṛtvā dakṣiṇārdhe gārhapatyasya śīte bhasmanyadhiśritya dakṣiṇodvāsya sakṛdeva sarvaṃ tūṣṇīmunnīyādhastātsamidhaṃ dhārayandakṣiṇena vihāramuddravati
9.11.8.a.d: ये पुरोदञ्चो दर्भास्तान्दक्षिणाग्रान्कृत्वा दक्षिणार्धे गार्हपत्यस्य शीते भस्मन्यधिश्रित्य दक्षिणोद्वास्य सकृदेव सर्वं तूष्णीमुन्नीयाधस्तात्समिधं धारयन्दक्षिणेन विहारमुद्द्रवति
9.11.8.a.m: Having turned the darbha grasses that point east so that their tips point south, having placed [the milk] on cold ashes on the southern half of the gārhapatya, having taken it down towards the south, having drawn it all up silently just once, holding a kindling stick underneath, he runs forth south of the sacrificial layout.

9.11.9.a.m: "For he holds it above for the gods," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.11.10.a.s: sa upaṣadya samidhamādhāya sakṛdeva sarvaṃ tūṣṇīṃ juhuyāt
9.11.10.a.d: स उपषद्य समिधमाधाय सकृदेव सर्वं तूष्णीं जुहुयात्
9.11.10.a.m: Having approached, having laid the kindling stick on [the fire], he should offer everything silently just once.

9.11.11.a.m: Or he should mentally refer to Soma accompanied by the ancestors at the first oblation,

9.11.11.b.m: and to Agni the carrier of kavya at the second.

9.11.12.a.m: The consuming, the pouring out, and the sprinkling around do not take place.

9.11.13.a.m: He gives the sacrificial utensils to Brahmins.

9.11.15.a.m: They throw the earthenware ones into water at home.

9.11.17.a.m: If they should hear that one who has not died is dead, he should prepare an eight-pot-sherd cake for Agni the fragrant.

9.11.18.a.s: yadi pūrvasyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāṃ yajamāno mriyeta dakṣiṇataḥ śīte bhasmanyuttarāmāhutiṃ ninayet
9.11.18.a.d: यदि पूर्वस्यामाहुत्यां हुतायां यजमानो म्रियेत दक्षिणतः शीते भस्मन्युत्तरामाहुतिं निनयेत्
9.11.18.a.m: If, when the first oblation has been offered, the sacrificer should die, he should pour the second oblation to the south into cold ashes.

9.11.19.a.m: Or he should take it to the heap of ashes.

9.11.20.a.m: "He should make here that which is the first oblation in the Pitṛmedha," say some.

9.11.21.a.s: yadi visaṃsthitāyāmiṣṭyāṃ yajamāno mriyeta sarvataḥ samavadāya sarvā devatā anudrutya svāhākāreṇa juhuyāt
9.11.21.a.d: यदि विसंस्थितायामिष्ट्यां यजमानो म्रियेत सर्वतः समवदाय सर्वा देवता अनुद्रुत्य स्वाहाकारेण जुहुयात्
9.11.21.a.m: If the sacrificer should die while a sacrifice is uncompleted, having cut off [portions] from all sides, having recited all the deities in succession, he should offer with the word 'svāhā'.

9.11.22.a.s: yadyāhitāgniḥ proṣitaḥ pramīto na prajñāyeta yāṃ diśamabhiprasthitaḥ syāttāmasyāgnibhiḥ kakṣaṃ daheyuḥ
9.11.22.a.d: यद्याहिताग्निः प्रोषितः प्रमीतो न प्रज्ञायेत यां दिशमभिप्रस्थितः स्यात्तामस्याग्निभिः कक्षं दहेयुः
9.11.22.a.m: If an āhitāgni who has died abroad cannot be found, they should burn dry grass with his fires in whichever direction he had set out.

9.11.23.a.m: Or else three hundred and sixty palāśa stalks.

9.11.23.b.m: With them, they make the form of a man on a black antelope skin.

9.11.23.c.s: palāśavalkaiḥ kuśair vā saṃdhiṣu saṃveṣṭya catvāriṃśatā śiraḥ prakalpayate /
9.11.23.c.d: पलाशवल्कैः कुशैर् वा संधिषु संवेष्ट्य चत्वारिंशता शिरः प्रकल्पयते ।
9.11.23.c.m: Having bound [them] at the joints with palāśa bark or kuśa grass, he forms the head with forty;

9.11.23.d.m: the neck with ten; the chest with twenty; the belly with thirty; each arm with fifty apiece;

9.11.23.e.m: from those two [lots of fifty] he forms the fingers with five apiece;

9.11.23.g.m: From these very [stalks], with five each, he prepares the toes;

9.11.23.h.m: With eight the penis, with twelve the testicles.

9.11.23.i.s: taiḥ kṛṣṇājine puruṣākṛtiṃ kṛtvā snāpayitvālaṃkṛtyānarvedi kṛṣṇājinaṃ dakṣiṇāgrīvamadharalomāstīrya tasminnenamuttānaṃ nipātya pattodaśenāhatena vāsasā pracchādya bāndhavāḥ paryupaviśanti /
9.11.23.i.d: तैः कृष्णाजिने पुरुषाकृतिं कृत्वा स्नापयित्वालंकृत्यानर्वेदि कृष्णाजिनं दक्षिणाग्रीवमधरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नेनमुत्तानं निपात्य पत्तोदशेनाहतेन वाससा प्रच्छाद्य बान्धवाः पर्युपविशन्ति ।
9.11.23.i.m: Having fashioned an effigy of a man with them upon a black-antelope skin, having bathed and adorned it, having spread out a black-antelope skin inside the altar ground with the neck pointing to the south and the hair turned downward, having laid it down supine upon that [skin], and having covered it with an unwashed garment that has fringes on its feet-side, the kinsmen sit round it.

9.11.23.j.s: abhimṛśantyayamasyāsau yasya ta ime agnaya iti prete 'mātyāḥ /
9.11.23.j.d: अभिमृशन्त्ययमस्यासौ यस्य त इमे अग्नय इति प्रेते ऽमात्याः ।
9.11.23.j.m: The relatives touch the deceased, [saying]: 'This one is his... so-and-so, whose these fires are.'

9.11.23.k.m: Beginning with this rite, one proceeds.

9.11.23.l.m: 'Having made [the effigy], they should burn it with his fires,' so says the Vājasaneyaka.

9.11.24.a.s: yadi havīṃṣyāsannāni kṛṣṇaśakuniruparyuparyatipatetpakṣābhyāmādhūnvāna ivābhiniṣīdedvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ity āhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.11.24.a.d: यदि हवींष्यासन्नानि कृष्णशकुनिरुपर्युपर्यतिपतेत्पक्षाभ्यामाधून्वान इवाभिनिषीदेद्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्य् आहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.11.24.a.m: If, when the oblations have been placed [near], a black bird should fly over them or alight flapping its wings as it were, he should offer an oblation with: 'Vishnu strode out through this...'

9.11.25.a.m: If it flies high, he should not pay heed to that.

9.11.26.a.s: yadyucchriyamāṇo yūpaścaṣālaṃ vā padyeta brahma pratiṣṭhā manasa ityāhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.11.26.a.d: यद्युच्छ्रियमाणो यूपश्चषालं वा पद्येत ब्रह्म प्रतिष्ठा मनस इत्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.11.26.a.m: If the sacrificial post while being erected, or the wooden ring, should fall, he should offer an oblation with: 'The brahman is the firm support of the mind...'

9.12.1.a.s: yadi haviḥśeṣānanudvāsitānanūyājair abhyāśrāvayedyadvā devā atipādayānītyāhutiṃ juhuyāt (āśrāvayadyadvo?)
9.12.1.a.d: यदि हविःशेषाननुद्वासिताननूयाजैर् अभ्याश्रावयेद्यद्वा देवा अतिपादयानीत्याहुतिं जुहुयात् (आश्रावयद्यद्वो?)
9.12.1.a.m: If one should cause the call to be given for the after-offerings while the remnants of the oblation have not been removed, he should offer an oblation with: 'Or whatever, O gods, I might omit...'

9.12.2.a.s: yadi praṇītā skandeyurupadasyeyurvāpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva iti tisṛbhiḥ punargṛhītvā tataṃ ma āpa ityāhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.12.2.a.d: यदि प्रणीता स्कन्देयुरुपदस्येयुर्वापो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इति तिसृभिः पुनर्गृहीत्वा ततं म आप इत्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.12.2.a.m: If the praṇītā-waters should spill or dry up, having drawn them again with the three [verses]: 'Waters indeed are you, bestowal of bliss...', he should offer an oblation with: 'The waters have stretched out for me...'

9.12.3.a.s: yadyagnyādheye sūryo 'nāviḥ syādudvayaṃ tamasasparyudu tyaṃ citramityāhutīrjuhuyāt
9.12.3.a.d: यद्यग्न्याधेये सूर्यो ऽनाविः स्यादुद्वयं तमसस्पर्युदु त्यं चित्रमित्याहुतीर्जुहुयात्
9.12.3.a.m: If at the setting up of the fires the sun should not be visible, he should offer oblations with: 'Up from darkness...', 'Up that [banner]...', and 'The bright [face of the gods]...'

9.12.4.a.s: yadyenamupadhāveyurgomāyavo 'vādiṣurekasṛko 'vādī dabhimṛtāḥ smaḥ paridhiṃ naḥ kurviti pālāśamidhmamupasamādhāyemaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpata iti ṣaḍāhutīrhutvemaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi maiṣāṃ nu gādayaro ardhametam /
9.12.4.a.d: यद्येनमुपधावेयुर्गोमायवो ऽवादिषुरेकसृको ऽवादी दभिमृताः स्मः परिधिं नः कुर्विति पालाशमिध्ममुपसमाधायेमं मे वरुण तत्त्वा यामि त्वं नो अग्ने स त्वं नो अग्ने त्वमग्ने अयासि प्रजापत इति षडाहुतीर्हुत्वेमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि मैषां नु गादयरो अर्धमेतम् ।
9.12.4.a.m: If [the people] should run up to him, [saying:] 'Jackals have howled, a solitary wolf has howled, we are afflicted by death; make an enclosing stick for us,' having put fuel of palāśa wood onto the fire and having offered six oblations with: 'This my prayer, O Varuṇa...', 'To you I go with prayer...', 'Do you, O Agni, to us...', 'So do you, O Agni, to us...', 'You, O Agni, are the goer...', [and] 'O Prajāpati...', [he lays an enclosing stick, saying:] 'This enclosing stick I place for the living, that no other of them may now go to this destination;'

9.12.4.b.s: śataṃ jivantu śaradaḥ purūcīstiro mṛtyuṃ dadhatāṃ parvateneti dakṣiṇato 'śmānaṃ paridhiṃ dadhāti
9.12.4.b.d: शतं जिवन्तु शरदः पुरूचीस्तिरो मृत्युं दधतां पर्वतेनेति दक्षिणतो ऽश्मानं परिधिं दधाति
9.12.4.b.m: 'May they live a hundred full autumns; may they keep death away through the mountain,' with this verse he places a stone as an enclosing stick to the south.

9.12.5.a.m: The firewood is of nyagrodha wood for a kṣatriya, at the boundary of his realm;

9.12.6.a.m: Of aśvattha wood for a vaiśya, at the boundary of his field.

9.12.7.a.m: The eight oblations [beginning with]: 'To the sacrifices, svāhā' may alternate with all the expiations belonging to the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

9.12.8.a.s: yadi dauḥṣvapnyamanyadvā bhayaṃ paśyedyata indra bhayāmaha ityāhutī juhuyāt /
9.12.8.a.d: यदि दौःष्वप्न्यमन्यद्वा भयं पश्येद्यत इन्द्र भयामह इत्याहुती जुहुयात् ।
9.12.8.a.m: If he should see bad dreams or other danger, he should offer oblations with: 'From where, O Indra, we are afraid...'

9.12.9.a.m: 'The hot oblation indeed shines with the brilliance of all,' [so says the brāhmaṇa].

9.12.9.b.m: Therefore, having performed the rite with the Pravargya, or having heard [the sound] of it being set up, he should offer an oblation with: 'With these songs...'

9.12.10.a.s: yadi homāyopasamiddheṣvahuteṣvagniṣu yajamāno 'śnīyādyatte vayaṃ yathā ha tadity āhutī juhuyāt /
9.12.10.a.d: यदि होमायोपसमिद्धेष्वहुतेष्वग्निषु यजमानो ऽश्नीयाद्यत्ते वयं यथा ह तदित्य् आहुती जुहुयात् ।
9.12.10.a.m: If, when the fires have been kindled for the offering but the oblations have not yet been made, the sacrificer should eat, he should offer oblations with: 'What of you we...', [and] 'Even as that...'

9.12.11.a.m: One over whom the sun has set, over whom the sun has risen, a paryāhita, a parīṣṭa, a parivitta, a parivinna, or a parivividāna should offer with these two [verses]: 'Whatever defect has arisen in my self...', and 'Agni has given back sight...'

9.12.12.a.m: In the case of what is unknown, he should offer with the three [verses beginning with]: 'What is unknown...'

9.13.1.a.m: If someone's unpurified clarified butter should spill, he should give a living creature that bites.

9.13.2.a.m: If it is purified, a speckled [animal] is to be given;

9.13.4.a.s: yadi sruggataṃ yadasya gṛhe puṣkalaṃ syāttaddadyāt /
9.13.4.a.d: यदि स्रुग्गतं यदस्य गृहे पुष्कलं स्यात्तद्दद्यात् ।
9.13.4.a.m: If it was in the ladle, he should give whatever abundant [thing] may be in his house.

9.13.4.b.s: saṃ tvā siñcāmīti tatsaṃsiñcedabhi vā mantrayeta
9.13.4.b.d: सं त्वा सिञ्चामीति तत्संसिञ्चेदभि वा मन्त्रयेत
9.13.4.b.m: He should pour [more butter] into it, with: 'I pour you together...', or he should consecrate it [with the mantra].

9.13.5.a.m: 'The sacrifice has gone to the divine folk,' according to some, he pronounces immediately after the clarified butter.

9.13.6.a.s: yajñasya tvā pramayābhimayā pratimayonmayā parigṛhṇāmīti tatparigṛhya bhūpataye svāheti prāñcaṃ prādeśaṃ mimīte /
9.13.6.a.d: यज्ञस्य त्वा प्रमयाभिमया प्रतिमयोन्मया परिगृह्णामीति तत्परिगृह्य भूपतये स्वाहेति प्राञ्चं प्रादेशं मिमीते ।
9.13.6.a.m: Having encircled that [spilled butter] with: 'With the measure, the counter-measure, the matching measure, the upward measure of the sacrifice I encircle you,' he measures a span to the east, with: 'To the lord of the earth, svāhā;'

9.13.6.b.m: To the south, with: 'To the lord of the world, svāhā;'

9.13.6.c.m: To the west, with: 'To the lord of beings, svāhā;'

9.13.6.d.m: To the north, with: 'To prosperity, svāhā;'

9.13.7.a.s: bhūpataye svāhā bhuvanapataye svāhā bhūtānāṃ pataye svāheti skannamanumantrayeteti sarvahaviṣāmanavayavena śrūyate
9.13.7.a.d: भूपतये स्वाहा भुवनपतये स्वाहा भूतानां पतये स्वाहेति स्कन्नमनुमन्त्रयेतेति सर्वहविषामनवयवेन श्रूयते
9.13.7.a.m: 'One should follow what has spilled with the mantra: 'To the lord of the earth, svāhā; to the lord of the world, svāhā; to the lord of beings, svāhā,'—thus it is taught in the sacred scripture without exception for all oblations.

9.13.8.a.s: yadi kapālaṃ bhidyeta gāyatryā tvā śatākṣarayā saṃdadhāmīti tatsaṃdhāyopari gārhapatye dhāryamāṇamabhijuhuyānmano jyotirjuṣatāmiti
9.13.8.a.d: यदि कपालं भिद्येत गायत्र्या त्वा शताक्षरया संदधामीति तत्संधायोपरि गार्हपत्ये धार्यमाणमभिजुहुयान्मनो ज्योतिर्जुषतामिति
9.13.8.a.m: If a potsherd should break, having joined it together with: 'With the hundred-syllabled Gāyatrī I join you together,' he should make an oblation over it while it is held above the gārhapatya fire, with: 'May the mind enjoy the light...'

9.13.9.a.m: Then he should carry it down to the waters with: 'Unbroken is the hot vessel, granting swiftness...'

9.13.10.a.m: Then, having consecrated another, he should insert it among the potsherds with: 'Thirty-three threads...', if it should break before being set down.

9.13.11.a.m: Now, if it breaks among those already set down, he should set down another with this very mantra;

9.13.12.a.m: Or [with the mantra] in place of which it broke.

9.13.13.a.s: yadi prayuktānāṃ prāgarthakarmaṇaḥ kapālaṃ naśyedāśvinaṃ dvikapālaṃ nirvapeddyāvāpṛthivyamekakapālam
9.13.13.a.d: यदि प्रयुक्तानां प्रागर्थकर्मणः कपालं नश्येदाश्विनं द्विकपालं निर्वपेद्द्यावापृथिव्यमेककपालम्
9.13.13.a.m: If, of those arranged, a potsherd should be lost before the meaningful action, he should offer a cake on two potsherds to the Aśvins, and a cake on one potsherd to Dyāvāpṛthivī.

9.13.15.a.s: mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivyayarcā sruvāhutimatra vājasaneyinaḥ samāmananti
9.13.15.a.d: मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिव्ययर्चा स्रुवाहुतिमत्र वाजसनेयिनः समामनन्ति
9.13.15.a.m: Here the followers of the Vājasaneyi recension prescribe an offering with the dipping-ladle accompanied by the verse to Dyāvāpṛthivī: 'Great heaven and earth to us...'

9.14.1.a.s: yadyekakapālaḥ skandetpari vāvarteta prajāpatervartanimanuvartasvānu vīrairanurādhyāma gobhiḥ /
9.14.1.a.d: यद्येककपालः स्कन्देत्परि वावर्तेत प्रजापतेर्वर्तनिमनुवर्तस्वानु वीरैरनुराध्याम गोभिः ।
9.14.1.a.m: If a single potsherd should spill or overturn, with: 'Follow the track of Prajāpati; may we prosper along with heroes, along with cattle;

9.14.1.b.s: anvaśvairanu sarvairupuṣṭairanu prajayānvindriyeṇa devā no yajñamṛjudhā nayantviti yathāsthānaṃ kalpayati
9.14.1.b.d: अन्वश्वैरनु सर्वैरुपुष्टैरनु प्रजयान्विन्द्रियेण देवा नो यज्ञमृजुधा नयन्त्विति यथास्थानं कल्पयति
9.14.1.b.m: Along with horses, along with all nourished ones, along with offspring, along with sensory power; may the gods lead our sacrifice straight,' he sets it into its proper place.

9.14.2.a.s: taṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrayate prati kṣatre pratitiṣṭhāmi rāṣṭre pratyaśveṣu pratitiṣṭhāmi goṣu /
9.14.2.a.d: तं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयते प्रति क्षत्रे प्रतितिष्ठामि राष्ट्रे प्रत्यश्वेषु प्रतितिष्ठामि गोषु ।
9.14.2.a.m: The sacrificer addresses it with: 'I establish myself in dominion, in the realm; I establish myself in horses, in cattle;

9.14.2.b.m: I establish myself in offspring, in prosperity.

9.14.2.c.m: One of the two has magnified the all; upon the other that is supported.

9.14.2.d.s: dive ca viśvakarmaṇe pṛthivyai cākaraṃ nama iti /
9.14.2.d.d: दिवे च विश्वकर्मणे पृथिव्यै चाकरं नम इति ।
9.14.2.d.m: To heaven and to Viśvakarman, and to earth I have paid homage.'

9.14.2.e.m: Then he should offer oblations with: 'The heaven has spilled, the earth...'

9.14.3.a.m: He should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara if he should pour an oblation upon a potsherd while performing the offerings to the wives.

9.14.4.a.m: 'He should offer this very [cake], who performs the New and Full Moon sacrifices,' thus it has been stated.

9.14.5.a.m: He should offer this very [sacrifice] if, without having performed the Āgrayaṇa, he should eat of the new [harvest].

9.14.6.a.s: ānīto vā eṣa devānāṃ ya āhitāgniradantyasya devā annam /
9.14.6.a.d: आनीतो वा एष देवानां य आहिताग्निरदन्त्यस्य देवा अन्नम् ।
9.14.6.a.m: Brought near indeed to the gods is he who has established the fires; the gods eat his food.

9.14.6.b.m: If, without having performed the Āgrayaṇa, he should eat of the new [harvest], he would eat the portion apportioned to the gods; he would incur misfortune.

9.14.7.a.s: mārutaṃ trayodaśakapālaṃ nirvapedyasya yamau jāyeyātāṃ gāvau vā puruṣau vā
9.14.7.a.d: मारुतं त्रयोदशकपालं निर्वपेद्यस्य यमौ जायेयातां गावौ वा पुरुषौ वा
9.14.7.a.m: He should offer a [cake] on thirteen potsherds to the Maruts, to whom twins are born, whether cattle or human beings.

9.14.8.a.m: For a man brings about loss of virility,

9.14.9.a.m: The invitatory verse is in the Gāyatrī metre;

9.14.10.a.m: He should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to Agni and Viṣṇu, whom they sacrifice for upon the fires of another, or upon whose fires another sacrifices.

9.14.11.a.s: raudraṃ vāstumayaṃ caruṃ nirvapedyasya rudraḥ paśūñchamāyeta
9.14.11.a.d: रौद्रं वास्तुमयं चरुं निर्वपेद्यस्य रुद्रः पशूञ्छमायेत
9.14.11.a.m: He should offer an oblation of wild rice to Rudra, whose cattle Rudra afflicts.

9.14.12.a.m: According to this very rite he should sacrifice for a chieftain of the Niṣādas.

9.14.14.a.s: kṛṣṇājinaṃ dakṣiṇā kūṭaṃ vā karṇo vā gardabho hariṇo vā hariṇapṛṇākā vā śyāmākapātro vā śaphako veti vijñāyate
9.14.14.a.d: कृष्णाजिनं दक्षिणा कूटं वा कर्णो वा गर्दभो हरिणो वा हरिणपृणाका वा श्यामाकपात्रो वा शफको वेति विज्ञायते
9.14.14.a.m: A black-antelope skin is the sacrificial gift, or a hornless beast, or an animal with large ears, or a donkey, or a deer, or a deer-skin, or a bowl of wild rice, or a hoofed animal—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.15.1.a.m: A student of the Veda who has approached a woman should sacrifice a donkey as a victim.

9.15.2.a.m: He should bake a sacrificial cake without potsherds on the bare ground.

9.15.3.a.m: They should perform the rite with portions [cast] into water.

9.15.4.a.m: It should have the Rakṣases as its deity, or have Nirṛti as its deity.

9.15.5.a.m: He should sacrifice to Nirṛti with a cooked offering.

9.15.6.a.s: yasya haviḥ kṣāyati taṃ yajñaṃ nirṛtirgṛhṇāti /
9.15.6.a.d: यस्य हविः क्षायति तं यज्ञं निरृतिर्गृह्णाति ।
9.15.6.a.m: Whose oblation burns, his sacrifice Nirṛti seizes.

9.15.6.b.m: Having concluded that, he should offer another oblation to that deity.

9.15.7.b.s: yasya puroḍāśaḥ kṣāyati taṃ yajñaṃ nirṛtirgṛhṇāti /
9.15.7.b.d: यस्य पुरोडाशः क्षायति तं यज्ञं निरृतिर्गृह्णाति ।
9.15.7.b.m: Whose sacrificial cake burns, his sacrifice Nirṛti seizes.

9.15.7.c.s: yaducchiṣṭaṃ syāttena pracareddveṣyāya tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ havirucchiṣṭaṃ ca dadyāt /
9.15.7.c.d: यदुच्छिष्टं स्यात्तेन प्रचरेद्द्वेष्याय तां दक्षिणां हविरुच्छिष्टं च दद्यात् ।
9.15.7.c.m: With what remains of it he should proceed; he should give that sacrificial gift and the remainder of the oblation to a hated enemy;

9.15.7.d.m: thereby he causes Nirṛti to seize him alone—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.15.8.a.m: [This is] the expiation when it burns completely,

9.15.9.a.m: or if it does not suffice for the portions.

9.15.10.a.m: If an oblation fails before its deity has been assigned, he should offer another oblation to that deity.

9.15.11.a.m: There the mantras beginning with the taking of the ladle should be repeated,

9.15.12.a.m: or as far as the end [of the rite where] it failed.

9.15.13.a.m: If its deity had been assigned, he should conclude the remainder with clarified butter.
