9.15.14.a.s: yasya sarvāṇi havīṃṣi naśyeyur duṣyeyur apahareyur vājyenaitā devatāḥ pratisaṃkhyāya yajeta
9.15.14.a.d: यस्य सर्वाणि हवींषि नश्येयुर् दुष्येयुर् अपहरेयुर् वाज्येनैता देवताः प्रतिसंख्याय यजेत
9.15.14.a.m: Whose oblations are all lost, spoiled, or carried away, should sacrifice with clarified butter, reciting mentally these deities.

9.15.15.a.m: Then he should perform another sacrifice without fault;

9.15.15.b.m: for sacrifice is the expiation of sacrifice.

9.15.16.a.m: He takes down the ruined oblation to the waters—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.15.17.a.m: What is unfit to be eaten by Āryas, he should not sacrifice with that.

9.15.18.a.s: yasya puroḍāśo duḥśṛtastaddhaviryamadaivatyaṃ yamameva tadgacchatīti vijñāyate /
9.15.18.a.d: यस्य पुरोडाशो दुःशृतस्तद्धविर्यमदैवत्यं यममेव तद्गच्छतीति विज्ञायते ।
9.15.18.a.m: Whose sacrificial cake is badly cooked, that oblation has Yama as its deity; it goes to Yama alone—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

9.15.18.b.s: saṃsthāpya tadanvāhāryapacane catuḥśarāvamodanaṃ paktvā caturo brāhmaṇānbhojayet
9.15.18.b.d: संस्थाप्य तदन्वाहार्यपचने चतुःशरावमोदनं पक्त्वा चतुरो ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्
9.15.18.b.m: Having concluded it, he should cook a mess of boiled rice measuring four platters on the anvāhāryapacana and feed four brāhmaṇas.

9.15.19.a.m: Of them, one among the partakers should be a Bhārgava.

9.15.20.a.s: yo 'dakṣiṇena yajñena yajeta sa yajñaḥ prakṣāmo 'nāyuḥ /
9.15.20.a.d: यो ऽदक्षिणेन यज्ञेन यजेत स यज्ञः प्रक्षामो ऽनायुः ।
9.15.20.a.m: He who sacrifices with a sacrifice without a sacrificial gift—that sacrifice is burnt out, without longevity.

9.15.21.a.m: If he should omit the prescribed sacrificial gift, a firmly established fertile field is to be given;

9.15.22.a.m: If he should invoke a portionless deity, he should sacrifice to it with clarified butter according as it was invoked,

9.15.22.b.m: or before the [offering to Agni] Sviṣṭakṛt.

9.15.23.a.s: yadi bhaginīṃ nāvāhayedyatra smarettadupotthāya manasāvāhya yadvo devā atipādayānītyāhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.15.23.a.d: यदि भगिनीं नावाहयेद्यत्र स्मरेत्तदुपोत्थाय मनसावाह्य यद्वो देवा अतिपादयानीत्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.15.23.a.m: If he should not invoke an entitled deity, wherever he remembers it, having risen near there, having invoked it mentally, he should offer an oblation with: 'Whatever of you, O gods, I may omit…'

9.16.1.a.s: yadi purā prayājebhyo bahiḥparidhyāhutiḥ skandedāgnīdhraṃ brūyādetāṃ saṃkṛsya juhudhīti /
9.16.1.a.d: यदि पुरा प्रयाजेभ्यो बहिःपरिध्याहुतिः स्कन्देदाग्नीध्रं ब्रूयादेतां संकृस्य जुहुधीति ।
9.16.1.a.m: If before the fore-offerings an oblation should spill outside the enclosing sticks, he should say to the agnīdh: 'Scraping this together, offer [it]!'

9.16.1.c.m: To him a full vessel should be given.

9.16.2.a.d: यत्किंच यज्ञे मृन्मयं भिद्येत तदपो ऽभ्यवहरेद्भुमिर्भूमिमगादिति
9.16.2.a.m: Whatever earthenware should break in the sacrifice, he should consign that to the waters with: 'Earth has gone to earth.'

9.16.4.a.s: yadyṛkto yajñaṃ bhreṣa āgacchedbhuriti gārhapatye juhuyāt /
9.16.4.a.d: यद्यृक्तो यज्ञं भ्रेष आगच्छेद्भुरिति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् ।
9.16.4.a.m: If an error should come to the sacrifice through an ṛc, he should offer in the gārhapatya with: 'Bhūḥ!'

9.16.4.b.m: If through a yajus, in the dakṣiṇāgni with: 'Bhuvaḥ!'

9.16.4.c.m: If through a sāman, in the āhavanīya with: 'Suvaḥ!'

9.16.5.a.m: If from every [quarter], he should offer them all.

9.16.6.a.m: 'This universal expiation should be performed everywhere,' says Āśmarathya.

9.16.6.b.m: 'It should be performed where none is handed down,' says Ālekhana.

9.16.6.c.m: Another [view is]: there should be a combination everywhere.

9.16.7.a.s: yadyenaṃ vihāre barhirvā bhayaṃ vindetprajāpatirviśvakarmā tasya mano devaṃ yajñena rādhyāsam /
9.16.7.a.d: यद्येनं विहारे बर्हिर्वा भयं विन्देत्प्रजापतिर्विश्वकर्मा तस्य मनो देवं यज्ञेन राध्यासम् ।
9.16.7.a.m: If in the ritual area grass [in the eye] or fear should afflict him, [with the verse:] "Prajāpati Viśvakarman, through the sacrifice may I succeed in the divine mind of him; /"

9.16.7.b.s: arthegā asya jahito 'vasānapate 'vasānaṃ me vindetyāhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.16.7.b.d: अर्थेगा अस्य जहितो ऽवसानपते ऽवसानं मे विन्देत्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.16.7.b.m: "You are one who goes to the goal of it; O lord of the resting place, do not abandon [us], find a resting place for me," he should offer an oblation.

9.16.8.a.m: If the oblation scooped out for someone should spill, he should give a living being that can bite.

9.16.8.b.m: If it was purified [by winnowing], a variegated [animal/object] is to be given.

9.16.9.a.s: yasya devate avadāne havīṃṣi yājyānuvākye vā viparihareyuryasya vā devatāyai bṛhītamahutaṃ skandeddevatāntaraye vā yadasya gṛhe puṣkalaṃ syāttaddadyāt
9.16.9.a.d: यस्य देवते अवदाने हवींषि याज्यानुवाक्ये वा विपरिहरेयुर्यस्य वा देवतायै बृहीतमहुतं स्कन्देद्देवतान्तरये वा यदस्य गृहे पुष्कलं स्यात्तद्दद्यात्
9.16.9.a.m: For whom the deities, portions, oblations, or the invitatory and consecratory verses are interchanged, or for whose deity [the oblation] taken should spill unoffered, or upon omission of a deity, he should give whatever is abundant in his house.

9.16.10.a.s: tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agna iti sarvatrāntaraye viparyāse caite āhutī juhotīty eke
9.16.10.a.d: त्वं नो अग्ने स त्वं नो अग्न इति सर्वत्रान्तरये विपर्यासे चैते आहुती जुहोतीत्य् एके
9.16.10.a.m: Some [say that] with 'You, O Agni, to us' [and] 'So, you, O Agni, to us,' he offers these two oblations everywhere upon omission and upon interchange.

9.16.11.a.s: yasya puroḍāśa udvā patetsaṃ vā vijeta tamudvāsya barhiṣadaṃ kṛtvā kimutpatasi kimutproṣṭhāḥ śāntaḥ śānterihāgahi /
9.16.11.a.d: यस्य पुरोडाश उद्वा पतेत्सं वा विजेत तमुद्वास्य बर्हिषदं कृत्वा किमुत्पतसि किमुत्प्रोष्ठाः शान्तः शान्तेरिहागहि ।
9.16.11.a.m: If someone's sacrificial cake should fly up or shake violently, having removed it [from the fire] and placed it on the barhis, [with the verses:] "Why do you fly up, why did you leap up? Calmed, come here through calm; /"

9.16.11.b.s: aghoro yajñiyo bhūtvāsīda sadanaṃ svamāsīda sadanaṃ svam //
9.16.11.b.d: अघोरो यज्ञियो भूत्वासीद सदनं स्वमासीद सदनं स्वम् ॥
9.16.11.b.m: "Becoming non-terrible and worthy of sacrifice, sit on your own seat, sit on your own seat! //"

9.16.11.c.s: mā hiṃsīrdeva preṣita ājyena tejasājyasva mā naḥ kiṃcana rīriṣaḥ /
9.16.11.c.d: मा हिंसीर्देव प्रेषित आज्येन तेजसाज्यस्व मा नः किंचन रीरिषः ।
9.16.11.c.m: "Do not injure, sent forth by the god! Anoint yourself with brilliance, with clarified butter; do not harm anything of ours! /"

9.16.11.d.s: yogakṣemasya śantyā asminnāsīda barhiṣītyetābhyāmabhimantrayetābhi ca ghārayet
9.16.11.d.d: योगक्षेमस्य शन्त्या अस्मिन्नासीद बर्हिषीत्येताभ्यामभिमन्त्रयेताभि च घारयेत्
9.16.11.d.m: "For the peace of security, sit on this barhis," he should address it with these two [verses] and sprinkle clarified butter over [it].

9.16.12.a.s: bhūtvā prabhavati yajamāno yasyaitāṃ yajñe prāyaścittiṃ kurvanti
9.16.12.a.d: भूत्वा प्रभवति यजमानो यस्यैतां यज्ञे प्रायश्चित्तिं कुर्वन्ति
9.16.12.a.m: Having become [strong], the sacrificer prospers for whom they perform this expiation in the sacrifice.

9.17.1.a.s: skannā dyauḥ skannā pṛthivī skannaṃ viśvamidaṃ jagat skannādo viśvā bhūtāni pra skannājjāyatāṃ haviḥ //
9.17.1.a.d: स्कन्ना द्यौः स्कन्ना पृथिवी स्कन्नं विश्वमिदं जगत् स्कन्नादो विश्वा भूतानि प्र स्कन्नाज्जायतां हविः ॥
9.17.1.a.m: "Spilled is heaven, spilled is the earth, spilled is all this moving world; / of the spilled one all beings [partake]; may the oblation be born from the spilled! //"

9.17.1.b.m: "Here be born, O cows! Here, horses! Here, men! /"

9.17.1.c.m: "And here may prosperity of wealth with a thousand sacrificial gifts settle down! //"

9.17.1.d.s: ayaṃ yajño vardhatāṃ gobhiraśvairiyaṃ vediḥ svapatyā suvīrā /
9.17.1.d.d: अयं यज्ञो वर्धतां गोभिरश्वैरियं वेदिः स्वपत्या सुवीरा ।
9.17.1.d.m: "May this sacrifice increase with cattle, with horses; [may] this altar ground [abound] in good offspring, in good heroes; /"

9.17.1.e.s: idaṃ barhirati barhīṃṣyanyemaṃ yajñaṃ viśve avantu devāḥ //
9.17.1.e.d: इदं बर्हिरति बर्हींष्यन्येमं यज्ञं विश्वे अवन्तु देवाः ॥
9.17.1.e.m: "May this barhis surpass other barhis grasses; may all the gods favor this sacrifice! //"

9.17.1.f.s: payasvatīroṣadhaya ityetābhiścatasṛbhiḥ pṛṣadājyaṃ skannamabhimantryāpo 'bhyavahṛtya nirṇijya srucaṃ śatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ srucyavadhāyedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ityanyatpṛṣadājyaṃ gṛhītvāśvenāvaghrāpyāyatane sādayet
9.17.1.f.d: पयस्वतीरोषधय इत्येताभिश्चतसृभिः पृषदाज्यं स्कन्नमभिमन्त्र्यापो ऽभ्यवहृत्य निर्णिज्य स्रुचं शतमानं हिरण्यं स्रुच्यवधायेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्यन्यत्पृषदाज्यं गृहीत्वाश्वेनावघ्राप्यायतने सादयेत्
9.17.1.f.m: [With the four verses beginning with] 'The plants full of milk...', having addressed the spilled clotted butter with these four [verses], having thrown [it] into water, having cleansed the ladle, having placed gold weighing a hundred mānas into the ladle, having taken another [portion of] clotted butter with 'Through this Viṣṇu strode...', and having caused a horse to smell it, he should set it down in its place.

9.17.2.b.s: pṛṣadājye skanne pṛṣadājye pṛṣadājyamabhigṛhya mano jyotirjuṣatāmityāhutiṃ juhuyāt
9.17.2.b.d: पृषदाज्ये स्कन्ने पृषदाज्ये पृषदाज्यमभिगृह्य मनो ज्योतिर्जुषतामित्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
9.17.2.b.m: When the clotted butter has spilled, having scooped clotted butter over clotted butter, he should offer an oblation with 'May the mind enjoy the light...'

9.17.3.a.s: evaṃ some skanne some somamabhigṛhya juhuyāt
9.17.3.a.d: एवं सोमे स्कन्ने सोमे सोममभिगृह्य जुहुयात्
9.17.3.a.m: Similarly, when soma has spilled, having scooped soma over soma, he should offer.

9.17.4.a.m: "What the bird has touched with its beak, [as an omen] of your destruction, /"

9.17.4.b.s: agniṣṭatsarvaṃ śundhatu havyavāḍ ghṛtasūdana iti kṛṣṇaśakunyavamṛṣṭamabhimantrayate /
9.17.4.b.d: अग्निष्टत्सर्वं शुन्धतु हव्यवाड् घृतसूदन इति कृष्णशकुन्यवमृष्टमभिमन्त्रयते ।
9.17.4.b.m: "May Agni, conveying the oblation, purifying the ghee, cleanse all that!" With this verse he addresses [an oblation] touched by a black bird.

9.17.4.c.m: Throwing into water and the rest are as before.

9.17.4.d.m: Here the vessel is scraped clean.

9.17.5.a.m: "What the beast of prey has licked with its mouth, [as an omen] of your destruction, /"

9.17.5.b.s: agniṣṭatsarvaṃ śundhatu havyavāḍ ghṛtasūdana iti śvāpadāvamṛṣṭamabhimantrayate /
9.17.5.b.d: अग्निष्टत्सर्वं शुन्धतु हव्यवाड् घृतसूदन इति श्वापदावमृष्टमभिमन्त्रयते ।
9.17.5.b.m: "May Agni, conveying the oblation, purifying the ghee, cleanse all that!" With this verse he addresses [an oblation] touched by a beast of prey.

9.17.5.c.m: Throwing into water and the rest are as before.

9.17.5.d.m: Here the vessel is not used again.

9.17.6.a.s: yadi paśurupākṛto vāśyeta yadasya pāre rajasa ity āhutiṃ juhuyāt /
9.17.6.a.d: यदि पशुरुपाकृतो वाश्येत यदस्य पारे रजस इत्य् आहुतिं जुहुयात् ।
9.17.6.a.m: If the animal, having been brought near, should bellow, he should offer an oblation with 'What at the end of the realm of space...';

9.17.6.b.m: Or, [with the verse:] "Through fear of what you bellowed, make us fearless from that; /"

9.17.6.c.s: prajābhyaḥ sarvābhyo mṛḍa namo rudrāya mīḍhuṣa iti juhuyād abhi vā mantrayeta
9.17.6.c.d: प्रजाभ्यः सर्वाभ्यो मृड नमो रुद्राय मीढुष इति जुहुयाद् अभि वा मन्त्रयेत
9.17.6.c.m: "Be gracious to all creatures; homage to bounteous Rudra!" he should offer or address [it].

9.17.7.a.s: yadyu vai niṣīdedetayaiva yasmādbhīṣā nyaṣada iti dvitīyām
9.17.7.a.d: यद्यु वै निषीदेदेतयैव यस्माद्भीषा न्यषद इति द्वितीयाम्
9.17.7.a.m: If it should sit down, [he recites] the second [verse] with this very [formula, adapted as:] 'through fear of what you sat down...';

9.17.8.a.m: When it has sat down, he should raise it with the staff of the maitrāvaruṇa.

9.18.1.a.s: udusra tiṣṭha pratitiṣṭha mā riṣo memaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca rīriṣaḥ /
9.18.1.a.d: उदुस्र तिष्ठ प्रतितिष्ठ मा रिषो मेमं यज्ञं यजमानं च रीरिषः ।
9.18.1.a.m: "Rise up, O bull, stand firm! Do not be harmed; do not harm this sacrifice and the sacrificer! /"

9.18.1.b.s: suvarge loke yajamānaṃ hi dhehi śaṃ na edhi dvipade śaṃ catuṣpada iti
9.18.1.b.d: सुवर्गे लोके यजमानं हि धेहि शं न एधि द्विपदे शं चतुष्पद इति
9.18.1.b.m: "For place the sacrificer in the heavenly world; be auspicious to our two-footed, auspicious to our four-footed!"—

9.18.3.a.m: With 'Through fear of what you trembled...' as the second [verse] when it is trembling;

9.18.4.a.m: With 'Through fear of what you ran away...' as the second [verse] when it has run away;

9.18.5.a.m: If it does not return, having brought near another [animal] of that appearance, color, and age, dedicated to that deity, he should sacrifice.

9.18.6.a.m: With 'Through fear of what you consented...' as the second [verse] if it is suffocated against its will;

9.18.7.a.s: ya idamakastasmai namastasmai svāheti sarvatra tṛtīyām
9.18.7.a.d: य इदमकस्तस्मै नमस्तस्मै स्वाहेति सर्वत्र तृतीयाम्
9.18.7.a.m: Everywhere [he recites] as the third [verse:] 'Homage to him who did this; svāhā to him!'

9.18.8.c.s: āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva ityetābhiścatasṛbhirapo 'bhyavahṛtyānyaṃ tadrūpavarṇavayasaṃ taddaivatamupākṛtya yajeta
9.18.8.c.d: आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इत्येताभिश्चतसृभिरपो ऽभ्यवहृत्यान्यं तद्रूपवर्णवयसं तद्दैवतमुपाकृत्य यजेत
9.18.8.c.m: Having thrown [the dead body] into water with these four [verses beginning with] 'For waters are refreshing...', having brought near another [animal] of that appearance, color, and age, dedicated to that deity, he should sacrifice.

9.18.9.a.m: With 'Through fear of what you urinate...' as the second [verse] when it urinates;

9.18.9.b.m: With 'Through fear of what you dung...' as the second [verse] when it dungs.

9.18.10.a.s: ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya ityucchrayantamabhimantrayate
9.18.10.a.d: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय इत्युच्छ्रयन्तमभिमन्त्रयते
9.18.10.a.m: With 'Upright indeed for our protection...' he addresses it when it stands up.

9.18.11.a.s: yadyupapāyyamāno na pibenna vā uvetanmriyasa ityupapāyayet
9.18.11.a.d: यद्युपपाय्यमानो न पिबेन्न वा उवेतन्म्रियस इत्युपपाययेत्
9.18.11.a.m: If, while being made to drink, it should not drink, he should make it drink with 'Indeed, you do not die in this way...'

9.18.12.a.s: garbhaṃ sravantīmagadāmakarmāgnirhotā pṛthivyantarikṣaṃ dyauryaścyutadagnāveva tanna tatprāpnoti nirṛtiṃ parācairiti paśūkhāṃ sravantīmabhimantrayate
9.18.12.a.d: गर्भं स्रवन्तीमगदामकर्माग्निर्होता पृथिव्यन्तरिक्षं द्यौर्यश्च्युतदग्नावेव तन्न तत्प्राप्नोति निरृतिं पराचैरिति पशूखां स्रवन्तीमभिमन्त्रयते
9.18.12.a.m: With 'We have made healthy the one dripping a fetus; Agni is the hotṛ, the earth, the atmosphere, the sky; whatever trickled, it is in Agni alone; it does not reach destruction turning away,' he addresses the animal-cooking pot when it is leaking.

9.18.13.a.m: When they lead the animal northward after it is appeased by the Āprī verses, it has been explained.

9.18.14.a.s: ye paśuṃ vimathnīranyastānkāmayetārtimārcheyuriti kuvidaṅgeti namovṛktivatyarcāgnīdhre juhuyāt /
9.18.14.a.d: ये पशुं विमथ्नीरन्यस्तान्कामयेतार्तिमार्छेयुरिति कुविदङ्गेति नमोवृक्तिवत्यर्चाग्नीध्रे जुहुयात् ।
9.18.14.a.m: If he should wish that those who tear apart the animal should suffer misfortune, he should offer in the āgnīdhra [fire] with the verse containing 'surely' and containing 'reverence' [namovṛkti];

9.18.14.b.m: In the āhavanīya or the śāmitra fire in the case of the independent animal sacrifice.

9.18.15.a.s: yadi vapā haviravadānaṃ vā skandedā tvā dade yaśase vīryāya cāsmāsvaghniyā yūyaṃ dadhāthendriyaṃ paya ityādāya yaste drapso yasta udarṣo daivyaḥ keturviśvaṃ bhuvanamāviveśa /
9.18.15.a.d: यदि वपा हविरवदानं वा स्कन्देदा त्वा ददे यशसे वीर्याय चास्मास्वघ्निया यूयं दधाथेन्द्रियं पय इत्यादाय यस्ते द्रप्सो यस्त उदर्षो दैव्यः केतुर्विश्वं भुवनमाविवेश ।
9.18.15.a.m: If the omentum or a cut portion of the oblation should spill, having picked it up with 'I take you for glory and for strength; do you, inviolable ones, place in us vigorous milk,' [and reciting:] 'Whatever drop of yours, whatever divine banner of yours has flown up, [and] has entered the whole world, /'

9.18.15.b.m: 'May that protect us from injury, svāhā!' he should offer the oblation.

9.18.16.a.s: yadyaṣṭāpadītyanubudhyeta dhātā rātiḥ sūryo devo diviṣadbhya ity āhutī hutvāṣṭāprūḍḍhiraṇyamuṣṇīṣeṇāveṣṭya
9.18.16.a.d: यद्यष्टापदीत्यनुबुध्येत धाता रातिः सूर्यो देवो दिविषद्भ्य इत्य् आहुती हुत्वाष्टाप्रूड्ढिरण्यमुष्णीषेणावेष्ट्य
9.18.16.a.m: If he should realize [that the animal was] eight-footed [pregnant], having offered the oblations with 'Dhātṛ, the gift, the divine Sun, for those dwelling in heaven...', having wrapped a piece of gold of eight prūṭas with a turban...

9.19.1.a.d: कोशे ऽवधाय द्वितीये ऽवधाय तृतीये ऽवदधाति
9.19.1.a.m: Having placed [the fetus] in a basket, having placed it in a second, he places it in a third.

9.19.2.a.m: Having made the baskets as if rimless, the adhvaryu addresses it with a mantra.

9.19.3.a.s: ā vartana vartayeti pradakṣiṇaṃ garbhamāvṛtya vi te bhinadmi takarīmityulbamādhyati
9.19.3.a.d: आ वर्तन वर्तयेति प्रदक्षिणं गर्भमावृत्य वि ते भिनद्मि तकरीमित्युल्बमाध्यति
9.19.3.a.m: With: 'Turn toward, roll!', turning the fetus around to the right, he pierces the fetal membrane with: 'I tear open your covering.'

9.19.4.a.s: bahiste astu bālityantarā sakthinī garbhaṃ nirasya śūle praṇīkṣya śāmitre nihatya śrapayati
9.19.4.a.d: बहिस्ते अस्तु बालित्यन्तरा सक्थिनी गर्भं निरस्य शूले प्रणीक्ष्य शामित्रे निहत्य श्रपयति
9.19.4.a.m: With: 'Out with you, babe!', having expelled the fetus between the thighs, having pierced it on a spit, and having driven it down in the śāmitra fire, he cooks it.

9.19.5.a.m: With [the verse], 'A broad drop, of every form, the sparkling drop,' he pushes a vessel underneath for the juice of the foetus.

9.19.6.a.m: Having apportioned the sacrificial cake for the animal, he apportions the sacrificial cake for the foetus, baked on one potsherd, dedicated to Heaven and Earth according to apportioning.

9.19.7.a.s: paśupuroḍāśena pracarya garbhapuroḍāśena pracarati bhaktīdyāvā pṛthivyeneti
9.19.7.a.d: पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्य गर्भपुरोडाशेन प्रचरति भक्तीद्यावा पृथिव्येनेति
9.19.7.a.m: Having proceeded with the sacrificial cake for the animal, he proceeds with the sacrificial cake for the foetus, dedicated to Heaven and Earth according to apportioning.

9.19.8.a.m: Cutting off the portions for the deity from the animal, having cut off another portion from in front of the navel of the foetus, he deposits it among the portions for the deity;

9.19.8.b.m: and another from above [the navel] among the portions for Sviṣṭakṛt.

9.19.9.a.m: He divides the juice of the foetus into three parts and pours it out among the portions for the deity, for Sviṣṭakṛt, and for the iḍā.

9.19.10.a.m: With [the formula], 'One-footed, two-footed,' he makes an offering before the Sviṣṭakṛt [offering].

9.19.11.a.m: Gold weighing eight prūṭis is the dakṣiṇā.

9.19.12.a.s: garbhasya dakṣiṇaṃ pūrvapādaṃ pracchidya viṣṇuṃ śipiviṣṭaṃ yajati pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmeti /
9.19.12.a.d: गर्भस्य दक्षिणं पूर्वपादं प्रच्छिद्य विष्णुं शिपिविष्टं यजति प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामेति ।
9.19.12.a.m: Having cut off the right forefoot of the foetus, he sacrifices to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa with [the verse], 'May I proclaim today, O Śipiviṣṭa, your name,'

9.19.13.a.s: maruto yasya hi kṣaya iti garbhaṃ garbhapuroḍāśaṃ cottareṇa gārhapatyasya śāmitrasya vā śīte bhasmanyupopya mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti śītena bhasmanābhisamūhyaitaṃ yuvānamiti pañcabhirupatiṣṭhate
9.19.13.a.d: मरुतो यस्य हि क्षय इति गर्भं गर्भपुरोडाशं चोत्तरेण गार्हपत्यस्य शामित्रस्य वा शीते भस्मन्युपोप्य मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति शीतेन भस्मनाभिसमूह्यैतं युवानमिति पञ्चभिरुपतिष्ठते
9.19.13.a.m: With [the verse], 'The Maruts, to whose house,' having buried the foetus and the sacrificial cake of the foetus in cold ashes north of the gārhapatya or of the śāmitra fire, having heaped cold ashes over them with [the verse], 'Great Heaven and Earth for us,' he attends [the spot] with the five [verses beginning], 'This young man.'

9.19.14.a.m: Āśmarathya holds: 'This expiation for a pregnant [victim] should be performed everywhere.'

9.19.14.b.m: Ālekhana holds: 'It should be performed where it is not specifically enjoined [otherwise].'

9.19.15.a.s: yadyanapavṛktārtho yūpo virohettasmiṃstvāṣṭraṃ sāṇḍaṃ lomaśaṃ piṅgalaṃ bahurūpaṃ savanīyasyopālambhyaṃ kuryāt
9.19.15.a.d: यद्यनपवृक्तार्थो यूपो विरोहेत्तस्मिंस्त्वाष्ट्रं साण्डं लोमशं पिङ्गलं बहुरूपं सवनीयस्योपालम्भ्यं कुर्यात्
9.19.15.a.m: If the sacrificial post, before its purpose is fulfilled, should sprout, he should tie to it, as an additional offering alongside the savanīya victim, an uncastrated, hairy, reddish-brown, variegated animal dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ.

9.19.16.a.m: Here the Vājasaneyins prescribe a caru dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ.

9.19.17.a.m: Some say: 'Here he merely offers spoon-oblations dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ.'

9.20.1.a.s: yadi yupaḥ suṣiraḥ syādatīsāreṇa yajamāno mriyeta /
9.20.1.a.d: यदि युपः सुषिरः स्यादतीसारेण यजमानो म्रियेत ।
9.20.1.a.m: If the sacrificial post should be hollow, the sacrificer would die of dysentery;

9.20.1.b.s: vaiṣṇavyā vyāhṛtibhiḥ prājāpatyayā ca hutvā taṃ saṃvṛścyāgnau pravṛjyāthānyaṃ sādhayet
9.20.1.b.d: वैष्णव्या व्याहृतिभिः प्राजापत्यया च हुत्वा तं संवृश्च्याग्नौ प्रवृज्याथान्यं साधयेत्
9.20.1.b.m: having offered [an oblation] to Viṣṇu, with the vyāhṛtis, and [one] to Prajāpati, having chopped it down and cast it into the fire, he should then prepare another.

9.20.2.a.m: If worms should eat it because it is worm-eaten,

9.20.3.a.m: If it should fall into the felling-trench, one should know: 'The wife will transgress against him';

9.20.3.b.m: the subsequent [procedure] beginning with the vyāhṛtis is the same.

9.20.4.a.s: yadi dakṣiṇā patetpratyaṅvā saṃ vā śīryeta śākhāsu vā sajyeta yajamāno mriyeta /
9.20.4.a.d: यदि दक्षिणा पतेत्प्रत्यङ्वा सं वा शीर्येत शाखासु वा सज्येत यजमानो म्रियेत ।
9.20.4.a.m: If it should fall southward or westward, or shatter, or become entangled in branches, the sacrificer would die;

9.20.4.b.m: in place of the [oblation] to Viṣṇu, there is one to Yama;

9.20.5.a.m: If it should fall into water, he would die in water;

9.20.5.b.m: in place of the [oblation] to Viṣṇu, there is one to Varuṇa;

9.20.6.a.m: If robbers should carry it off by force, he would be deprived of all his property;

9.20.6.b.m: in place of the [oblation] to Viṣṇu, there is one to Indra;

9.20.7.a.s: yadi mūla upaśuṣkaḥ syānna pitṛbhyo yathāpuraṃ kariṣyatīti vidyāt /
9.20.7.a.d: यदि मूल उपशुष्कः स्यान्न पितृभ्यो यथापुरं करिष्यतीति विद्यात् ।
9.20.7.a.m: If it should dry up at the base, one should know: 'He will not perform [offerings] for the ancestors as formerly';

9.20.7.b.m: if in the middle: 'He will die of hunger';

9.20.7.c.m: if at the top: 'He will not go to the heavenly world.'

9.20.7.d.m: If the [corner] facing the fire should split, the sacrificer would die;

9.20.7.g.m: if the southern one, the son of the chief queen;

9.20.7.h.m: if the northern one, the son born after the eldest;

9.20.7.i.m: if the south-eastern one, the brahman;

9.20.7.k.m: if the north-western one, the adhvaryu;

9.20.7.l.m: if the north-eastern one, the agnīdh.

9.20.8.a.m: In all [cases of] drying up and the like, the subsequent [procedure] beginning with [the oblation to] Yama is the same.

9.20.9.a.s: yadi lohinyo lekhāḥ prasavyaṃ yūpaṃ parihareyurna sāhasraṃ kratumāhariṣyatīti vidyāt /
9.20.9.a.d: यदि लोहिन्यो लेखाः प्रसव्यं यूपं परिहरेयुर्न साहस्रं क्रतुमाहरिष्यतीति विद्यात् ।
9.20.9.a.m: If red lines should encircle the sacrificial post counter-clockwise, one should know: 'He will not perform a sacrifice with a thousand [cows as dakṣiṇā]';

9.20.9.b.m: if white ones [encircle it] clockwise, [one should know]: 'He will soon perform a sacrifice with a thousand [cows as dakṣiṇā].'

9.20.10.a.s: yadyāhutau hutāyāṃ kṛṣṇo dhūmo dakṣiṇāṃ diśamabhinihanyādvāto vā prasavyaṃ dhumamāveṣṭayedyajamāno mriyeta /
9.20.10.a.d: यद्याहुतौ हुतायां कृष्णो धूमो दक्षिणां दिशमभिनिहन्याद्वातो वा प्रसव्यं धुममावेष्टयेद्यजमानो म्रियेत ।
9.20.10.a.m: If, when the oblation is offered, black smoke should strike toward the south, or the wind should wrap the smoke counter-clockwise, the sacrificer would die;

9.20.10.b.m: he should offer the all-expiation oblation—he should offer it.

10.1.1.a.s: somena yakṣyamāṇo brāhmaṇānārṣeyānṛtvijo vṛṇīte yūnaḥ sthavirānvānūcānānūrdhvavāco 'naṅgahīnān
10.1.1.a.d: सोमेन यक्ष्यमाणो ब्राह्मणानार्षेयानृत्विजो वृणीते यूनः स्थविरान्वानूचानानूर्ध्ववाचो ऽनङ्गहीनान्
10.1.1.a.m: Intending to sacrifice with soma, he chooses the officiating priests: Brāhmaṇas descended from ṛṣis, young or elderly, learned in the Veda, loud-voiced, and free from bodily defects.

10.1.3.a.s: taṃ pṛcchati ka ṛtvijaḥ ke yājayanti kaccinnāhīnaḥ kaccinna nyastamārtvijyaṃ kaccitkalyāṇyo dakṣiṇā iti chandogabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
10.1.3.a.d: तं पृच्छति क ऋत्विजः के याजयन्ति कच्चिन्नाहीनः कच्चिन्न न्यस्तमार्त्विज्यं कच्चित्कल्याण्यो दक्षिणा इति छन्दोगब्राह्मणं भवति
10.1.3.a.m: 'He asks him: "Who are the officiating priests? Who conduct the sacrifice? Is it not an ahīna? Is the office of officiating priest not cast away? Are the dakṣiṇās auspicious?"'—thus says a Chāndoga-Brāhmaṇa.

10.1.4.a.s: atha japati mahanme 'voco bhargo me 'voco yaśo me vocaḥ stomaṃ me 'vocaḥ kḷptiṃ me 'voco bhuktiṃ me 'vocaḥ sarvaṃ me 'vocastanmāvatu tanmāviśatu tena bhukṣiṣīyeti
10.1.4.a.d: अथ जपति महन्मे ऽवोचो भर्गो मे ऽवोचो यशो मे वोचः स्तोमं मे ऽवोचः कॢप्तिं मे ऽवोचो भुक्तिं मे ऽवोचः सर्वं मे ऽवोचस्तन्मावतु तन्माविशतु तेन भुक्षिषीयेति
10.1.4.a.m: Then he mutters: 'Greatness you have spoken to me, splendor you have spoken to me, glory you have spoken to me, praise you have spoken to me, fitness you have spoken to me, enjoyment you have spoken to me, everything you have spoken to me; may that protect me, may that enter me, may I enjoy through that.'

10.1.5.a.s: padvā nāmāsi srutiḥ somasaraṇī somaṃ gameyamiti panthānamātiṣṭhate
10.1.5.a.d: पद्वा नामासि स्रुतिः सोमसरणी सोमं गमेयमिति पन्थानमातिष्ठते
10.1.5.a.m: With [the formula], 'Footpath by name are you, the trail leading to Soma; may I go to Soma,' he sets out upon the road.

10.1.6.a.s: devo devametu somaḥ somametvṛtasya pathā vihāya dauṣkṛtyamityabhipravrajati
10.1.6.a.d: देवो देवमेतु सोमः सोममेत्वृतस्य पथा विहाय दौष्कृत्यमित्यभिप्रव्रजति
10.1.6.a.m: With [the formula], 'May god go to god, may soma go to soma along the path of truth, leaving behind evil deeds,' he proceeds towards [the sacrificial enclosure].

10.1.7.a.m: Having turned toward the south, he attends the ancestors with [the formula], 'Ancestors! Bhūḥ!'

10.1.8.a.m: He chooses them, either four [at a time] or all one by one:

10.1.9.a.s: adhvaryuṃ pratiprasthātāraṃ neṣṭāram unnetāram ity adhvaryūn /
10.1.9.a.d: अध्वर्युं प्रतिप्रस्थातारं नेष्टारम् उन्नेतारम् इत्य् अध्वर्यून् ।
10.1.9.a.m: the adhvaryu, the pratiprasthātṛ, the neṣṭṛ, and the unnetṛ, as the adhvaryu priests;

10.1.9.b.m: the brahman, the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the āgnīdhra, and the potṛ, as the brahman priests;

10.1.9.c.s: hotāraṃ maitrāvaruṇam acchāvākaṃ grāvastutam iti hotṝn /
10.1.9.c.d: होतारं मैत्रावरुणम् अच्छावाकं ग्रावस्तुतम् इति होतॄन् ।
10.1.9.c.m: the hotṛ, the maitrāvaruṇa, the acchāvāka, and the grāvastut, as the hotṛ priests;

10.1.9.d.s: udgātāraṃ prastotāraṃ pratihartāraṃ subrahmaṇyam ity udgātṝn
10.1.9.d.d: उद्गातारं प्रस्तोतारं प्रतिहर्तारं सुब्रह्मण्यम् इत्य् उद्गातॄन्
10.1.9.d.m: the udgātṛ, the prastotṛ, the pratihartṛ, and the subrahmaṇya, as the udgātṛ priests.

10.1.10.a.m: The Kauṣītakins teach a seventeenth [priest], the sadasya.

10.1.11.a.m: He is the overseer of the ritual acts.

10.1.14.a.s: agnirme hotādityo me 'dhvaryuścandramā me brahmā parjanyo ma udgātākāśo me sadasya āpo me hotrāśaṃsino raśmayo me camasādhvaryava ityupāṃśu devatādeśanam /
10.1.14.a.d: अग्निर्मे होतादित्यो मे ऽध्वर्युश्चन्द्रमा मे ब्रह्मा पर्जन्यो म उद्गाताकाशो मे सदस्य आपो मे होत्राशंसिनो रश्मयो मे चमसाध्वर्यव इत्युपांशु देवतादेशनम् ।
10.1.14.a.m: “Agni is my hotṛ; Āditya is my adhvaryu; Candramas is my brahman; Parjanya is my udgātṛ; the space is my sadasya; the waters are my hotrā-reciters; the rays are my camasādhvaryus”—this designation of deities is [uttered] in a low voice.

10.2.1.a.m: One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma.

10.2.1.c.m: He may desire [them] simultaneously or at separate performances.

10.2.2.a.m: In spring one should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma.

10.2.3.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is the first sacrifice.

10.2.5.a.m: Every spring one should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma.

10.2.5.b.s: tasya tisro dakṣiṇā iti chandogabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
10.2.5.b.d: तस्य तिस्रो दक्षिणा इति छन्दोगब्राह्मणं भवति
10.2.5.b.m: “Its sacrificial gifts are three [cows],” says a Chāndoga Brāhmaṇa.

10.2.6.a.m: One should sacrifice for the first time with the Rathaṃtara-sāman, with the Bṛhat-sāman, or with both sāmans.

10.2.7.a.m: Some say that without having performed [the sacrifice] with the Rathaṃtara-sāman, one should not undertake the one with the Bṛhat-sāman.

10.2.8.a.s: yadīṣṭyā yadi paśunā yad somena yajetāmāvāsyāyāṃ vaiva paurṇamāsyāṃ vā yajeta
10.2.8.a.d: यदीष्ट्या यदि पशुना यद् सोमेन यजेतामावास्यायां वैव पौर्णमास्यां वा यजेत
10.2.8.a.m: Whether he sacrifices with an iṣṭi, with an animal [sacrifice], or with soma, he should sacrifice only on the new moon or on the full moon.

10.2.9.a.s: deva varuṇa devayajanaṃ me dehīti yajamāno rājānaṃ devayajanaṃ yācet
10.2.9.a.d: देव वरुण देवयजनं मे देहीति यजमानो राजानं देवयजनं याचेत्
10.2.9.a.m: The sacrificer should request the place of sacrifice from the king [of the land], saying: “O divine Varuṇa, give me the place of sacrifice!”

10.2.10.a.s: sa yadi dadāti devayajanavān bhūyā ityenamāha /
10.2.10.a.d: स यदि ददाति देवयजनवान् भूया इत्येनमाह ।
10.2.10.a.m: If he grants it, he says to him: “May you possess a place of sacrifice.”

10.2.10.b.s: yadi na dadāti yadahaṃ devayajanaṃ veda tasmiṃstvā devayajana ā kṣiṇomīti
10.2.10.b.d: यदि न ददाति यदहं देवयजनं वेद तस्मिंस्त्वा देवयजन आ क्षिणोमीति
10.2.10.b.m: If he does not grant it, [he says]: “In that place of sacrifice which I know, I destroy you upon that place of sacrifice!”

10.2.11.b.m: “You have struck at the mind; the mind shall abandon you!”—says the brahman.

10.2.11.c.m: “You have struck at speech; speech shall abandon you!”—says the hotṛ.

10.2.11.d.m: “You have struck at the breath; the breath shall abandon you!”—says the adhvaryu.

10.2.11.e.m: “You have struck at sight; sight shall abandon you!”—says the udgātṛ.

10.2.11.f.m: “You have struck at the self; the self shall abandon you!”—says the sadasya.

10.2.11.g.m: “You have struck at procreation; offspring shall abandon you!”—says the sacrificer.

10.2.11.h.m: “You have struck at the limbs; the limbs shall abandon you!”—say the hotrakas.

10.2.11.i.m: “You have struck at all beings; all beings shall abandon you!”—say all the officiating priests.

10.3.1.a.m: The king [sacrificer] requests the place of sacrifice:

10.3.1.b.s: agnirhotā sa me hotā hotardevayajanaṃ me dehīti hotāram /
10.3.1.b.d: अग्निर्होता स मे होता होतर्देवयजनं मे देहीति होतारम् ।
10.3.1.b.m: “Agni is the hotṛ, he is my hotṛ; O hotṛ, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the hotṛ.

10.3.1.c.s: ādityo 'dhvaryuḥ sa me 'dhvaryuradhvaryo devayajanaṃ me dehītyadhvaryum /
10.3.1.c.d: आदित्यो ऽध्वर्युः स मे ऽध्वर्युरध्वर्यो देवयजनं मे देहीत्यध्वर्युम् ।
10.3.1.c.m: “Āditya is the adhvaryu, he is my adhvaryu; O adhvaryu, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the adhvaryu.

10.3.1.d.s: candramā brahmā sa me brahmā brahmandevayajanaṃ me dehīti brahmāṇam /
10.3.1.d.d: चन्द्रमा ब्रह्मा स मे ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मन्देवयजनं मे देहीति ब्रह्माणम् ।
10.3.1.d.m: “Candramas is the brahman, he is my brahman; O brahman, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the brahman.

10.3.1.e.s: prajanya udgātā sa ma udgātodgātardevayajanaṃ me dehītyudgātāram /
10.3.1.e.d: प्रजन्य उद्गाता स म उद्गातोद्गातर्देवयजनं मे देहीत्युद्गातारम् ।
10.3.1.e.m: “Parjanya is the udgātṛ, he is my udgātṛ; O udgātṛ, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the udgātṛ.

10.3.1.f.s: ākāśaḥ sadasyaḥ sa me sadasyaḥ sadasya devayajanaṃ me dehīti sadasyam /
10.3.1.f.d: आकाशः सदस्यः स मे सदस्यः सदस्य देवयजनं मे देहीति सदस्यम् ।
10.3.1.f.m: “The space is the sadasya, it is my sadasya; O sadasya, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the sadasya.

10.3.1.g.s: āpo hotrāśaṃsinaste me hotrāśaṃsino hotrāśaṃsino devayajanaṃ me datteti hotrakān /
10.3.1.g.d: आपो होत्राशंसिनस्ते मे होत्राशंसिनो होत्राशंसिनो देवयजनं मे दत्तेति होत्रकान् ।
10.3.1.g.m: “The waters are the hotrā-reciters, they are my hotrā-reciters; O hotrā-reciters, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the hotrakas.

10.3.1.h.s: raśmayaścamasādhvaryuvaste me camasādhvaryavaścamasā dhvaryavo devayajanaṃ me datteti camasādhvaryūn
10.3.1.h.d: रश्मयश्चमसाध्वर्युवस्ते मे चमसाध्वर्यवश्चमसा ध्वर्यवो देवयजनं मे दत्तेति चमसाध्वर्यून्
10.3.1.h.m: “The rays are the camasādhvaryus, they are my camasādhvaryus; O camasādhvaryus, give me the place of sacrifice!”—[he says] to the camasādhvaryus.

10.3.2.a.m: Or rather, he should not request the place of sacrifice.

10.3.2.b.s: devatā evopatiṣṭheta sakṣedaṃ paśya vidhartaridaṃ paśya nākedaṃ paśya /
10.3.2.b.d: देवता एवोपतिष्ठेत सक्षेदं पश्य विधर्तरिदं पश्य नाकेदं पश्य ।
10.3.2.b.m: He should just revere the deities: “O conqueror, see this! O sustainer, see this! O vault of heaven, see this!

10.3.2.c.s: ramatiḥ paniṣṭhartaṃ varṣiṣṭhamamṛtā yānyāhuḥ sūryo variṣṭho akṣabhirvibhātyanu dyāvāpṛthivī devaputre iti
10.3.2.c.d: रमतिः पनिष्ठर्तं वर्षिष्ठममृता यान्याहुः सूर्यो वरिष्ठो अक्षभिर्विभात्यनु द्यावापृथिवी देवपुत्रे इति
10.3.2.c.m: Rest is the most praiseworthy, truth is the highest, which they call immortal; the sun, greatest, shines with his eyes along heaven and earth, the mothers of the gods.”

10.3.3.a.s: edamaganma devayajanaṃ pṛthivyā iti devayajanam adhyavasyati
10.3.3.a.d: एदमगन्म देवयजनं पृथिव्या इति देवयजनम् अध्यवस्यति
10.3.3.a.m: With the formula, “Here we have come to the place of sacrifice on earth,” he occupies the place of sacrifice.

10.3.4.a.m: Having grasped the middle main post of the east-facing hall, he mutters—according to the Vājasaneyaka.

10.3.6.a.m: This anuvāka, beginning “Agni with the yajuses, Savitṛ with the stomas,” is recited.

10.3.7.a.m: At this point, having brought king [Soma], they serve him with milk-rice until the purchase.

10.3.8.a.s: sve dakṣe dakṣapiteha sīda devānāṃ sumno mahate raṇāya /
10.3.8.a.d: स्वे दक्षे दक्षपितेह सीद देवानां सुम्नो महते रणाय ।
10.3.8.a.m: “In your own skill, O father of skill, sit here, a favour of the gods for the great battle!

10.3.8.b.s: svāsasthastanuvā saṃviśasva pitevaidhi sūnava ā suśevaḥ /
10.3.8.b.d: स्वासस्थस्तनुवा संविशस्व पितेवैधि सूनव आ सुशेवः ।
10.3.8.b.m: Well-seated, enter together with your body; be like a father to a son, most gracious!

10.3.8.c.s: śivo mā śivamāviśa satyaṃ ma ātmā śraddhā me 'kṣitistapo me pratiṣṭhā /
10.3.8.c.d: शिवो मा शिवमाविश सत्यं म आत्मा श्रद्धा मे ऽक्षितिस्तपो मे प्रतिष्ठा ।
10.3.8.c.m: Auspicious, enter me who am auspicious; truth is my self, faith my imperishability, ascetic heat my support!

10.3.8.d.s: savitṛprasūtā mā diśo dīkṣayantu satyamasmīti purastāddīkṣaṇīyāyā āhavanīyaṃ yajamāna upatiṣṭhate /
10.3.8.d.d: सवितृप्रसूता मा दिशो दीक्षयन्तु सत्यमस्मीति पुरस्ताद्दीक्षणीयाया आहवनीयं यजमान उपतिष्ठते ।
10.3.8.d.m: Impelled by Savitṛ, let the directions consecrate me; I am truth”—with these formulas the sacrificer reveres the āhavanīya prior to the consecration sacrifice.

10.3.8.e.m: Having run through the saptahotṛ formula mentally and having offered it into the āhavanīya with the draught portion,

10.4.1.a.m: he sets in motion the procedure of the consecration sacrifice.

10.4.2.a.m: He measures out [the grains] for a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu.

10.4.2.b.m: Or a mess of cooked grain in ghee to Agni and Viṣṇu.

10.4.3.a.m: The cake is for one who desires spiritual lustre;

10.4.3.b.m: the mess of cooked grain in ghee is for one who desires offspring or for one who desires cattle.

10.4.4.a.s: ādityaṃ ghṛte caruṃ dvitīyaṃ prajākāmapaśukāmasyaike samāmananti
10.4.4.a.d: आदित्यं घृते चरुं द्वितीयं प्रजाकामपशुकामस्यैके समामनन्ति
10.4.4.a.m: Some teach a second mess of cooked grain in ghee to Āditi for one who desires offspring or cattle.

10.4.5.a.m: There are fifteen or seventeen kindling verses.

10.4.6.a.m: Some teach [erecting] the east-facing hall first;

10.4.7.a.m: The consecration sacrifice concludes with the patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

10.4.8.a.m: He keeps the clarified butter of the dhruvā ladel.

10.4.9.a.m: With that he proceeds in a low voice up to the Agnīṣomīya [animal sacrifice].

10.4.10.b.m: With as much voice as he has, so much he recites at the consecration offering (Dīkṣaṇīyā);

10.4.10.c.m: lower than that at the introductory offering (Prāyaṇīyā);

10.4.10.d.m: still lower at the hospitality offering (Ātithyā);

10.4.11.a.m: In a low tone at the Dīkṣaṇīyā;

10.4.11.b.m: in a lower tone at the Prāyaṇīyā;

10.4.11.c.m: in a still lower tone at the Ātithyā;

10.4.11.f.m: Or, in a whisper at the Dīkṣaṇīyā;

10.4.11.g.m: in a lower whisper at the Prāyaṇīyā;

10.4.11.h.m: in a still lower whisper at the Ātithyā;

10.4.12.a.s: darśapūrṇamāsaprakṛtīnāṃ some 'gnyanvādhānaṃ vratopāyanamāraṇyāśanaṃ jāgaraṇamanvāhāryasya ca dānaṃ patnyāḥ saṃnahanaṃ vimocanamiti na vidyante
10.4.12.a.d: दर्शपूर्णमासप्रकृतीनां सोमे ऽग्न्यन्वाधानं व्रतोपायनमारण्याशनं जागरणमन्वाहार्यस्य च दानं पत्न्याः संनहनं विमोचनमिति न विद्यन्ते
10.4.12.a.m: In the Soma sacrifice, for the rituals having the New and Full Moon sacrifices as their archetype, the following are not present: adding fuel to the fires, undertaking the vow, eating wild food, keeping awake, giving the anvāhārya cooked rice, and the tying and untying of the wife's girdle.

10.4.13.a.s: agnyanvādhānaṃ tu dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ kriyeta patnyāśca saṃnahanam
10.4.13.a.d: अग्न्यन्वाधानं तु दीक्षणीयायां क्रियेत पत्न्याश्च संनहनम्
10.4.13.a.m: However, adding fuel to the fires and the tying of the wife's girdle should be performed at the Dīkṣaṇīyā.

10.4.14.a.m: During the consecration days (dīkṣās), he has the sacrificial post made;

10.4.15.a.m: or when the King [Soma] has been purchased, or during the Upasads.

10.5.1.a.s: prācīnavaṃśaṃ karoti purastādunnataṃ paścānninataṃ sarvataḥ pariśritam
10.5.1.a.d: प्राचीनवंशं करोति पुरस्तादुन्नतं पश्चान्निनतं सर्वतः परिश्रितम्
10.5.1.a.m: He constructs the hall with the roof-beam pointing eastward, elevated in front, lower at the back, [and] enclosed on all sides.

10.5.2.a.m: The corners are in the intermediate directions.

10.5.3.a.m: He makes openings in the corners.

10.5.5.a.m: One desiring heaven [should make] a door to the east;

10.5.5.b.m: he who desires, 'May I thrive in the world of the fathers,' to the south;

10.5.5.c.m: one desiring the world of men, to the west;

10.5.5.d.m: he who desires, 'May I thrive in the world of the gods,' to the north;

10.5.5.e.m: he who desires, 'May I thrive in both worlds,' to the north-east;

10.5.5.f.m: he who desires, 'May I thrive in all quarters,' on all sides.

10.5.6.a.s: uttareṇa bahiḥ prāgvaṃśaṃ pariśrite yajamānaḥ keśaśmaśru vāpayate
10.5.6.a.d: उत्तरेण बहिः प्राग्वंशं परिश्रिते यजमानः केशश्मश्रु वापयते
10.5.6.a.m: In an enclosed space to the north outside the east-beamed hall, the sacrificer has his hair and beard shaved.

10.5.7.a.m: First the armpits, then the beard, then the hair;

10.5.7.b.m: or rather: the beard, the armpits, then the hair.

10.5.8.a.m: With 'May the waters moisten [thee],' he moistens the right side of the head.

10.5.8.b.s: oṣadhe trāyasvainamiti prāgagraṃ darbhamantardhāya svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīriti svadhitinābhinidhāya devaśrūriti pravapati
10.5.8.b.d: ओषधे त्रायस्वैनमिति प्रागग्रं दर्भमन्तर्धाय स्वधिते मैनं हिंसीरिति स्वधितिनाभिनिधाय देवश्रूरिति प्रवपति
10.5.8.b.m: Interposing a blade of darbha grass with its tip pointing eastward with 'O plant, protect him,' placing the razor upon it with 'O razor, harm him not,' he shaves with 'Listening to the gods.'

10.5.10.a.s: oṣadhe trāyasva mā svadhite mā mā hiṃsīḥ svastryuttarāṇyaśīyeti yajamāno japati
10.5.10.a.d: ओषधे त्रायस्व मा स्वधिते मा मा हिंसीः स्वस्त्र्युत्तराण्यशीयेति यजमानो जपति
10.5.10.a.m: The sacrificer whispers: 'O plant, protect me; O razor, harm me not; may I attain auspicious subsequent [rites].'

10.5.11.a.m: He has his nails pared toward the interior.

10.5.12.a.m: First of the left hand, beginning from the little finger.

10.5.13.a.m: First those of the hands, then those of the feet.

10.5.14.a.m: He cleans his teeth with an udumbara twig, not causing bleeding.

10.5.15.a.m: He bathes in standing water containing shells, overgrown with avakā plants, at a grassy ford.

10.5.16.a.m: 'Having placed gold in a jar, he bathes in it,' thus says the Vājasaneyaka.

10.6.1.a.m: With 'May the waters, our mothers, purify us,'

10.6.1.b.m: 'Golden in color, pure, purifying, the waters have flowed forth leaving behind imperfection,'

10.6.1.c.s: śataṃ pavitrā vitatā hyāsu tābhirno devaḥ savitā punātviti /
10.6.1.c.d: शतं पवित्रा वितता ह्यासु ताभिर्नो देवः सविता पुनात्विति ।
10.6.1.c.m: 'A hundred strainers are spread out in them; with these may the divine Savitṛ purify us,'

10.6.1.d.m: and with these two verses: 'Golden in color, pure, purifying...' [he bathes].

10.6.2.a.m: Emerging from the water, he mutters: 'Pure and cleansed, I come up from these.'

10.6.4.a.m: Then he gives him a new, unwashed linen garment.

10.6.5.a.s: tatpratigṛhṇāti dīkṣāsi tapaso yonistapo 'si brahmaṇo yonirbrahmāsi kṣatrasya yoniḥ kṣatramasyṛtasya yonirṛtamasi bhūrārabhe śraddhāṃ manasā dīkṣāṃ tapasā viśvasya bhuvanasyādhipatnīṃ sarve kāmā yajamānasya santviti
10.6.5.a.d: तत्प्रतिगृह्णाति दीक्षासि तपसो योनिस्तपो ऽसि ब्रह्मणो योनिर्ब्रह्मासि क्षत्रस्य योनिः क्षत्रमस्यृतस्य योनिरृतमसि भूरारभे श्रद्धां मनसा दीक्षां तपसा विश्वस्य भुवनस्याधिपत्नीं सर्वे कामा यजमानस्य सन्त्विति
10.6.5.a.m: He accepts it with: 'Thou art consecration, the womb of ascetic heat; thou art ascetic heat, the womb of sacred knowledge; thou art sacred knowledge, the womb of the warrior; thou art the warrior, the womb of cosmic order; thou art cosmic order, the earth. I undertake faith with the mind, consecration with ascetic heat, the ruler of the whole universe; may all desires belong to the sacrificer.'

10.6.6.a.s: somasya tanūrasi tanuvaṃ me pāhi dīkṣāsi tanūrasi tāṃ tvāṃ śivāṃ syonāṃ paridhiṣīyeti tatparidhāya somasya nīvirasīti nīvimanuparikalpayate
10.6.6.a.d: सोमस्य तनूरसि तनुवं मे पाहि दीक्षासि तनूरसि तां त्वां शिवां स्योनां परिधिषीयेति तत्परिधाय सोमस्य नीविरसीति नीविमनुपरिकल्पयते
10.6.6.a.m: Having put it on with: 'Thou art the body of Soma, protect my body; thou art consecration, thou art the body; as such, auspicious and comfortable, may I put thee on,' he arranges the tucked fold with: 'Thou art the tuck of Soma.'

10.6.7.a.m: With 'For strength, thee,' he eats food mixed with clarified butter, pouring sour milk over it.

10.6.8.a.m: He eats whatever is pleasing to his heart.

10.6.9.a.m: 'Just that becomes his in yonder world,' it is known [from scripture].

10.6.9.b.s: tathā śitaḥ syādyathā tato dīkṣāsu kanīyaḥkanīyo vratamupeyāt
10.6.9.b.d: तथा शितः स्याद्यथा ततो दीक्षासु कनीयःकनीयो व्रतमुपेयात्
10.6.9.b.m: He should be sated in such a way that from then on, during the consecration days, he may take less and less food.

10.6.10.a.m: Some teachers recite that the eating takes place before the shaving of the hair or before the putting on of the garment.

10.6.11.a.m: With [the formula], “You are the milk of the great ones,” he stirs the fresh butter with two darbha tufts.

10.6.12.a.m: With [the formula], “You are the bestower of brilliance,” [the sacrificer] anoints himself three times away from [the hair's root] (or from head to foot):

10.7.1.a.m: With [the formula], “You are the pupil of Vṛtra's eye,” he anoints [his eyes] with salve from Mount Trikakud.

10.7.2.a.s: yadi traikakudaṃ nādhigacchedyenaiva kena cāñjanenāñjīteti vājasaneyakam
10.7.2.a.d: यदि त्रैककुदं नाधिगच्छेद्येनैव केन चाञ्जनेनाञ्जीतेति वाजसनेयकम्
10.7.2.a.m: “If he should not obtain salve from Mount Trikakud, he may anoint with whatever salve [is available],” so [says] the Vājasaneyaka.

10.7.3.a.s: satūlayā darbheṣīkayā śareṣīkayā darbhapuñjīlena vābhyantaraṃ dvirdakṣiṇamanidhāvamānaḥ /
10.7.3.a.d: सतूलया दर्भेषीकया शरेषीकया दर्भपुञ्जीलेन वाभ्यन्तरं द्विर्दक्षिणमनिधावमानः ।
10.7.3.a.m: With a darbha stalk with its tuft, or a reed stalk, or a darbha tuft, inwards twice the right [eye], not running over;

10.7.4.a.m: Or else twice the right, three times the left;

10.7.5.a.m: Then, to the north outside the prāgvaṃśa hall, he purifies him with darbha tufts.

10.7.6.a.m: “He purifies with two, he purifies with three,” it has been said.

10.7.7.a.m: With twenty-one divided threefold, with seven each, twice he wipes upward from the navel;

10.7.8.a.m: Some say he purifies downward along [the body].

10.7.9.a.m: Whomever he hates, him he should purify crosswise or diagonally.

10.7.10.a.m: With these [formulas], “May Citpati purify you,” and so forth, mantra by mantra.

10.7.11.a.m: He attaches everywhere, “With an unbroken strainer.”

10.7.12.a.s: citpatirmā punātu vākpatirmā punātu devo mā savitā punātviti pāvyamāno japati
10.7.12.a.d: चित्पतिर्मा पुनातु वाक्पतिर्मा पुनातु देवो मा सविता पुनात्विति पाव्यमानो जपति
10.7.12.a.m: While being purified, he mutters: “May Citpati purify me, may Vākpati purify me, may the god Savitṛ purify me,”

10.7.13.a.m: And “Of that you, O lord of the strainer...”

10.7.13.b.m: “May the purifying one, who belongs to heaven, sagacious with the strainer,

10.7.13.d.m: The golden strainer, belonging to Prajāpati, of a hundred stretches,

10.7.13.e.s: tena brahmavido vayaṃ pūtaṃ brahma punīmaha iti ca
10.7.13.e.d: तेन ब्रह्मविदो वयं पूतं ब्रह्म पुनीमह इति च
10.7.13.e.m: With that, we who know sacred lore purify the purified sacred lore;” and so forth.

10.7.14.a.s: yaddevā devaheḍanaṃ tvamagne ayāsīti ca pūtaḥ
10.7.14.a.d: यद्देवा देवहेडनं त्वमग्ने अयासीति च पूतः
10.7.14.a.m: When purified, [he mutters]: “Whatever offense against the gods, O gods...” and “You, O Agni, are unyielding...”

10.7.15.a.m: Or he should offer before the consecratory offering.

10.8.1.a.s: ā vo devāsa īmaha iti pūrvayā dvārā prāgvaṃśaṃ praviśyendrāgnī dyāvāpṛthivī ityapareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramya tvaṃ dikṣāṇāmadhipatirasītyāhavanīyamupopaviśati
10.8.1.a.d: आ वो देवास ईमह इति पूर्वया द्वारा प्राग्वंशं प्रविश्येन्द्राग्नी द्यावापृथिवी इत्यपरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्य त्वं दिक्षाणामधिपतिरसीत्याहवनीयमुपोपविशति
10.8.1.a.m: With [the formula], “We approach you, O gods,” having entered the prāgvaṃśa hall by the eastern door, and having crossed south to the west of the āhavanīya with “Indra-and-Agni, Heaven-and-Earth,” he sits down near the āhavanīya with “You are the overlord of consecrations.”

10.8.2.a.s: eṣa evāta ūrdhvaṃ yajamānasya saṃcaro bhavati
10.8.2.a.d: एष एवात ऊर्ध्वं यजमानस्य संचरो भवति
10.8.2.a.m: This alone, from now on, is the passage-way of the sacrificer.

10.8.3.a.m: Here some teach the consecratory offering.

10.8.4.a.m: Some [teach] the equipment-formulas before the consecration libations.

10.8.5.a.s: yaddīkṣaṇīyāyā dhrauvamājyaṃ tato dīkṣāhutīḥ sruveṇa catasro juhoti /
10.8.5.a.d: यद्दीक्षणीयाया ध्रौवमाज्यं ततो दीक्षाहुतीः स्रुवेण चतस्रो जुहोति ।
10.8.5.a.m: From what is the dhruvā-ghee of the consecratory offering, from that he offers four consecration libations with the sruva spoon,

10.8.5.c.m: With these [formulas], “To the intention, to the impulse, to Agni, svāhā,” mantra by mantra.

10.8.6.a.s: dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā viśve devasya neturiti pūrṇāhutiṃ ṣaṣṭhīm
10.8.6.a.d: द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा विश्वे देवस्य नेतुरिति पूर्णाहुतिं षष्ठीम्
10.8.6.a.m: Having filled the sruc ladle with twelve portions of ghee, [he offers] the full libation as the sixth, with “All [men] of the divine leader...”

10.8.7.a.s: yatrādhvaryuraudgrahaṇāni juhoti tadyajamāno 'dhvaryumanvārabhya pañca juhoti vācā me vāgdīkṣatāṃ svāhā /
10.8.7.a.d: यत्राध्वर्युरौद्ग्रहणानि जुहोति तद्यजमानो ऽध्वर्युमन्वारभ्य पञ्च जुहोति वाचा मे वाग्दीक्षतां स्वाहा ।
10.8.7.a.m: Where the adhvaryu offers the audgrahaṇa libations, there the sacrificer, keeping hold of the adhvaryu from behind, offers five: “Through speech may my speech be consecrated, svāhā;

10.8.7.b.m: Through breath may my breath be consecrated, svāhā;

10.8.7.c.m: Through sight may my sight be consecrated, svāhā;

10.8.7.d.m: Through hearing may my hearing be consecrated, svāhā;

10.8.7.e.m: Through mind may my mind be consecrated, svāhā.”

10.8.8.a.m: Or he recites over the adhvaryu while he is offering.

10.8.9.a.s: vātaṃ prāṇaṃ manasānvārabhāmahe prajāpatiṃ yo bhuvanasya gopāḥ /
10.8.9.a.d: वातं प्राणं मनसान्वारभामहे प्रजापतिं यो भुवनस्य गोपाः ।
10.8.9.a.m: “We take hold with the mind of the wind, the breath, of Prajāpati who is the guardian of the world;

10.8.9.b.s: sa no mṛtyostrāyatāṃ pātvaṃhaso jyogjīvā jarāmaśīmahīti pūrṇāhutiṃ hūyamānāmanumantrayate
10.8.9.b.d: स नो मृत्योस्त्रायतां पात्वंहसो ज्योग्जीवा जरामशीमहीति पूर्णाहुतिं हूयमानामनुमन्त्रयते
10.8.9.b.m: May he protect us from death, protect from distress; long-living, may we attain old age,” with this he recites over the full libation while it is being offered.

10.8.11.a.m: He consecrates the sacrificer with a black antelope skin.

10.8.12.a.m: He should be consecrated with two joined together, flesh sides inwards, hairy sides outwards.

10.8.13.a.m: If there should be one, he should stitch the right fore-foot;

10.8.14.a.s: dve viṣūcī pratimuñceta pādaṃ vā pratiṣīvyedityeke
10.8.14.a.d: द्वे विषूची प्रतिमुञ्चेत पादं वा प्रतिषीव्येदित्येके
10.8.14.a.m: He should fasten on two facing apart, or stitch a foot, say some.

10.8.15.a.m: Inside the altar ground, he spreads out the black antelope skin, with its neck to the east, hairy side up.

10.8.16.a.s: ṛksāmayoḥ śilpe stha iti śuklakṛṣṇe rājī ālabhate /
10.8.16.a.d: ऋक्सामयोः शिल्पे स्थ इति शुक्लकृष्णे राजी आलभते ।
10.8.16.a.m: With [the formula], “You two are the works of art of the Ṛgveda and Sāmaveda,” he touches the white and black stripes;

10.9.1.a.s: indra śākvara gāyatrīṃ prapadye tāṃ te yunajmīndra śākvara triṣṭubhaṃ prapadye tāṃ te yunajmīndra śākvara jagatīṃ prapadye tāṃ te yunajmīndra śākvarānuṣṭubhaṃ prapadye tāṃ te yunajmīndra śākvara paṅktiṃ prapadye tāṃ te yunajmītyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśaṃ kṛṣṇājinamabhimṛśati /
10.9.1.a.d: इन्द्र शाक्वर गायत्रीं प्रपद्ये तां ते युनज्मीन्द्र शाक्वर त्रिष्टुभं प्रपद्ये तां ते युनज्मीन्द्र शाक्वर जगतीं प्रपद्ये तां ते युनज्मीन्द्र शाक्वरानुष्टुभं प्रपद्ये तां ते युनज्मीन्द्र शाक्वर पङ्क्तिं प्रपद्ये तां ते युनज्मीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशं कृष्णाजिनमभिमृशति ।
10.9.1.a.m: With these [formulas], “O mighty Indra, I take refuge in the gāyatrī; that I yoke for you,” “O mighty Indra, I take refuge in the triṣṭubh; that I yoke for you,” “O mighty Indra, I take refuge in the jagatī; that I yoke for you,” “O mighty Indra, I take refuge in the anuṣṭubh; that I yoke for you,” “O mighty Indra, I take refuge in the paṅkti; that I yoke for you,” mantra by mantra, he touches the black antelope skin in each direction,

10.9.2.a.m: Then, facing east, bending his knees, he creeps towards it.

10.9.3.a.s: imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasyeti kṛṣṇājinaṃ bhasatta ārohati
10.9.3.a.d: इमां धियं शिक्षमाणस्येति कृष्णाजिनं भसत्त आरोहति
10.9.3.a.m: With [the formula], “[Desiring the favor] of him who seeks to learn this thought,” he mounts the black antelope skin from the rump side.

10.9.4.a.m: While mounting, he mutters: “The good protector...”;

10.9.4.b.m: Having mounted, “This good ship have I mounted...”

10.9.4.c.s: āhaṃ dīkṣāmaruhamṛtasya patnīṃ gāyatreṇa chandasā brahmaṇā cartaṃ satye 'dhāyi satyamṛte 'dhāyyṛtaṃ ca me satyaṃ cābhūtāṃ jyotirabhūvaṃ suvaragamaṃ suvargaṃ lokaṃ nākasya pṛṣṭhaṃ bradhnasya viṣṭapamagamamiti ca
10.9.4.c.d: आहं दीक्षामरुहमृतस्य पत्नीं गायत्रेण छन्दसा ब्रह्मणा चर्तं सत्ये ऽधायि सत्यमृते ऽधाय्यृतं च मे सत्यं चाभूतां ज्योतिरभूवं सुवरगमं सुवर्गं लोकं नाकस्य पृष्ठं ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपमगममिति च
10.9.4.c.m: And: “I have mounted the consecration, the spouse of truth, through the gāyatrī metre, through sacred lore. Truth has been placed in truth, truth has been placed in order. Both order and truth have become mine. I have become light, I have gone to heaven, I have gone to the heavenly world, the back of the firmament, the highest station of the sun.”

10.9.5.a.m: At this point, the wife puts a head-net and hair-ornament on her head.

10.9.6.a.m: "Black, made of living sheep's wool," says the Vājasaneyaka.

10.9.7.a.m: They explain kumbakurīra as a hair-net.

10.9.8.a.s: viṣṇoḥ śarmāsītyahatena vāsasā dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ yajamānaḥ prorṇute /
10.9.8.a.d: विष्णोः शर्मासीत्यहतेन वाससा दक्षिणमंसं यजमानः प्रोर्णुते ।
10.9.8.a.m: With the formula, "You are Viṣṇu's shelter," the sacrificer covers his right shoulder with an unwashed garment.

10.9.8.b.m: With "Protect me from the shining through of the stars," [he covers] his head.

10.9.9.a.s: uṣṇīṣeṇa pradakṣiṇaṃ śiro veṣṭayata iti vājasaneyakam
10.9.9.a.d: उष्णीषेण प्रदक्षिणं शिरो वेष्टयत इति वाजसनेयकम्
10.9.9.a.m: "He wraps his head sunwise with a turban," says the Vājasaneyaka.

10.9.10.a.m: It is stated: "He should not uncover himself before the buying of soma."

10.9.11.a.m: He consecrates the wife with a garment having its fringes to the east.

10.9.13.a.m: A girdle made of reed grass or of muñja grass, threefold, broad, having a loop at one end.

10.9.13.b.m: With it he consecrates the sacrificer.

10.9.14.a.s: ūrgasīti nābhiṃ prati parivyayati dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
10.9.14.a.d: ऊर्गसीति नाभिं प्रति परिव्ययति द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
10.9.14.a.m: With the formula, "You are sap," he ties it around opposite the navel, contemplating in his mind someone he hates.

10.9.15.a.s: uttareṇa nābhiṃ niṣṭarkyaṃ granthiṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ paryūhya dakṣiṇena nābhimavasthāpayati
10.9.15.a.d: उत्तरेण नाभिं निष्टर्क्यं ग्रन्थिं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं पर्यूह्य दक्षिणेन नाभिमवस्थापयति
10.9.15.a.m: Having made a slipknot north of the navel, and having wound it round sunwise, he lets it rest south of the navel.

10.9.16.a.m: At this point, he girds the wife as in the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

10.9.17.a.s: indrasya yonirasi māmā hiṃsīriti kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ yajamānāya prayacchati
10.9.17.a.d: इन्द्रस्य योनिरसि मामा हिंसीरिति कृष्णविषाणां यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
10.9.17.a.m: With "You are Indra's womb; do not harm me," he gives a black-buck horn to the sacrificer.

10.9.19.a.m: It has three folds or five folds, turned to the right.

10.10.1.a.s: kṛṣyai tvā susasyāyā iti tayā vederloṣṭamuddhanti
10.10.1.a.d: कृष्यै त्वा सुसस्याया इति तया वेदेर्लोष्टमुद्धन्ति
10.10.1.a.m: With "For plowing thee, rich in good crops," he digs up a clod from the altar ground with it.

10.10.2.a.m: With "For the plants rich in good fruit," when an occasion arises, he scratches his head.

10.10.3.a.s: viṣāṇe viṣyaitaṃ granthiṃ yadasya gulphitaṃ hṛdi mano yadasya gulphitam ity aṅgāni
10.10.3.a.d: विषाणे विष्यैतं ग्रन्थिं यदस्य गुल्फितं हृदि मनो यदस्य गुल्फितम् इत्य् अङ्गानि
10.10.3.a.m: With "O horn, untie this knot, whatever in his heart is tangled, whatever mind in him is tangled," [he scratches] his limbs.

10.10.4.a.s: ūrdhvasadasi vānaspatyaḥ sudyumno dyumnaṃ yajamānāya dhehītyaudumbaraṃ dīkṣitadaṇḍaṃ yajamānāya prayacchati /
10.10.4.a.d: ऊर्ध्वसदसि वानस्पत्यः सुद्युम्नो द्युम्नं यजमानाय धेहीत्यौदुम्बरं दीक्षितदण्डं यजमानाय प्रयच्छति ।
10.10.4.a.m: With "You who sit upright, belonging to the tree, of good renown, bestow renown upon the sacrificer," he hands a staff of udumbara wood for the consecrated one to the sacrificer.

10.10.4.b.m: Or whatever sacrificial tree is fruit-bearing.

10.10.5.a.m: It reaches up to the mouth or reaches up to the chin.

10.10.6.a.s: sūpasthā devo vanaspatiriti taṃ yajamānaḥ pratigṛhyoruvyacā asi janadhāḥ svabhakṣo mā pāhīti camasaṃ vratapradānamabhimantrya keśinīṃ dīkṣāṃ japatyagnirdīkṣitaḥ pṛthivī dīkṣā sā mā dīkṣā dīkṣayatu tayā dīkṣayā dīkṣe /
10.10.6.a.d: सूपस्था देवो वनस्पतिरिति तं यजमानः प्रतिगृह्योरुव्यचा असि जनधाः स्वभक्षो मा पाहीति चमसं व्रतप्रदानमभिमन्त्र्य केशिनीं दीक्षां जपत्यग्निर्दीक्षितः पृथिवी दीक्षा सा मा दीक्षा दीक्षयतु तया दीक्षया दीक्षे ।
10.10.6.a.m: Having received it with "A tree is a deity easy to approach," and having addressed the goblet that provides the fast-milk with "You are wide-extending, people-sustaining; partaking of yourself, protect me," the sacrificer whispers the Keśinī-consecration: "Agni is consecrated; the earth is the consecration. May that consecration consecrate me; with that consecration I consecrate myself.

10.10.6.b.s: vāyur dīkṣito 'ntariksāṃ dīkṣā sā mā dīkṣā dīkṣayatu tayā dīkṣayā dīkṣe /
10.10.6.b.d: वायुर् दीक्षितो ऽन्तरिक्सां दीक्षा सा मा दीक्षा दीक्षयतु तया दीक्षया दीक्षे ।
10.10.6.b.m: Vāyu is consecrated; the atmosphere is the consecration. May that consecration consecrate me; with that consecration I consecrate myself.

10.10.6.c.s: ādityo dīkṣito dyaur dīkṣā sā mā dīkṣā dīkṣayatu tayā dīkṣayā dīkṣe /
10.10.6.c.d: आदित्यो दीक्षितो द्यौर् दीक्षा सा मा दीक्षा दीक्षयतु तया दीक्षया दीक्षे ।
10.10.6.c.m: Āditya is consecrated; the sky is the consecration. May that consecration consecrate me; with that consecration I consecrate myself.

10.10.6.d.s: candramā dīkṣitaḥ śrotraṃ dīkṣā sā mā dīkṣā dīkṣayatu tayā dīkṣayā dīkṣe /
10.10.6.d.d: चन्द्रमा दीक्षितः श्रोत्रं दीक्षा सा मा दीक्षा दीक्षयतु तया दीक्षया दीक्षे ।
10.10.6.d.m: The moon is consecrated; the hearing is the consecration. May that consecration consecrate me; with that consecration I consecrate myself.

10.10.6.e.s: prajāpatir dīkṣito mano dīkṣā sā mā dīkṣā dīkṣayatu tayā dīkṣayā dīkṣe /
10.10.6.e.d: प्रजापतिर् दीक्षितो मनो दीक्षा सा मा दीक्षा दीक्षयतु तया दीक्षया दीक्षे ।
10.10.6.e.m: Prajāpati is consecrated; the mind is the consecration. May that consecration consecrate me; with that consecration I consecrate myself.

10.10.6.f.s: vācā me vāg dīkṣatāmagnaye samaṣṭavā u /
10.10.6.f.d: वाचा मे वाग् दीक्षतामग्नये समष्टवा उ ।
10.10.6.f.m: Through speech may my speech be consecrated, so as to attain Agni!

10.10.6.g.s: prāṇena me prāṇo dīkṣatāṃ vāyave samaṣṭavā u /
10.10.6.g.d: प्राणेन मे प्राणो दीक्षतां वायवे समष्टवा उ ।
10.10.6.g.m: Through breath may my breath be consecrated, so as to attain Vāyu!

10.10.6.h.s: cakṣuṣā me cakṣur dīkṣatāṃ sūryāya samaṣṭavā u /
10.10.6.h.d: चक्षुषा मे चक्षुर् दीक्षतां सूर्याय समष्टवा उ ।
10.10.6.h.m: Through sight may my sight be consecrated, so as to attain Sūrya!

10.10.6.i.s: śrotreṇa me śrotraṃ dīkṣatāṃ candramase samaṣṭavā u /
10.10.6.i.d: श्रोत्रेण मे श्रोत्रं दीक्षतां चन्द्रमसे समष्टवा उ ।
10.10.6.i.m: Through hearing may my hearing be consecrated, so as to attain the moon!

10.10.6.j.s: manasā me mano dīkṣatāṃ prajāpataye samaṣṭavā u /
10.10.6.j.d: मनसा मे मनो दीक्षतां प्रजापतये समष्टवा उ ।
10.10.6.j.m: Through mind may my mind be consecrated, so as to attain Prajāpati!

10.10.6.k.s: bhūr bhuvaḥ suvastapo me dīkṣā satyaṃ gṛhapatiriti
10.10.6.k.d: भूर् भुवः सुवस्तपो मे दीक्षा सत्यं गृहपतिरिति
10.10.6.k.m: Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ! Ascetic heat is my consecration; truth is the master of the house."

10.11.1.a.s: pṛthivī dīkṣā tayāgnirdīkṣayā dīkṣito yayāgnirdīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.a.d: पृथिवी दीक्षा तयाग्निर्दीक्षया दीक्षितो ययाग्निर्दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.a.m: [The adhvaryu says:] "The earth is the consecration; with that consecration Agni was consecrated. With which consecration Agni was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.b.s: antarikṣaṃ dīkṣā tayā vāyur dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayā vāyur dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.b.d: अन्तरिक्षं दीक्षा तया वायुर् दीक्षया दीक्षितो यया वायुर् दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.b.m: The atmosphere is the consecration; with that consecration Vāyu was consecrated. With which consecration Vāyu was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.c.s: dyaur dīkṣā tayādityo dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayādityo dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.c.d: द्यौर् दीक्षा तयादित्यो दीक्षया दीक्षितो ययादित्यो दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.c.m: The sky is the consecration; with that consecration Āditya was consecrated. With which consecration Āditya was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.d.s: diśo dīkṣā tayā candramā dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayā candramā dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.d.d: दिशो दीक्षा तया चन्द्रमा दीक्षया दीक्षितो यया चन्द्रमा दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.d.m: The quarters are the consecration; with that consecration the moon was consecrated. With which consecration the moon was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.e.s: āpo dīkṣā tayā varuṇo rājā dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayā varuṇo rājā dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.e.d: आपो दीक्षा तया वरुणो राजा दीक्षया दीक्षितो यया वरुणो राजा दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.e.m: The waters are the consecration; with that consecration King Varuṇa was consecrated. With which consecration King Varuṇa was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.f.s: oṣadhayo dīkṣā tayā somo rājā dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayā somo rājā dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.f.d: ओषधयो दीक्षा तया सोमो राजा दीक्षया दीक्षितो यया सोमो राजा दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.f.m: The plants are the consecration; with that consecration King Soma was consecrated. With which consecration King Soma was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.g.s: vāg dīkṣā tayā prāṇo dīkṣayā dīkṣito yayā prāṇo dīkṣayā dīkṣitastayā tvā dīkṣayā dīkṣayāmi /
10.11.1.g.d: वाग् दीक्षा तया प्राणो दीक्षया दीक्षितो यया प्राणो दीक्षया दीक्षितस्तया त्वा दीक्षया दीक्षयामि ।
10.11.1.g.m: Speech is the consecration; with that consecration breath was consecrated. With which consecration breath was consecrated, with that consecration I consecrate you.

10.11.1.h.m: May the earth follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.i.m: May the atmosphere follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.j.m: May the sky follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.k.m: May the quarters follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.l.m: May the waters follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.m.m: May the plants follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.n.m: May speech follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.o.m: May the Ṛg-verses follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.p.m: May the Sāman-chants follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.q.m: May the Yajus-formulas follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated!

10.11.1.r.s: ahaś ca rātriś ca kṛṣiś ca vṛṣṭiś ca tviṣiścāpacitiścāpaścauṣadhayaścork ca sūnṛtā ca tās tvā dīkṣamāṇam anudīkṣantām iti
10.11.1.r.d: अहश् च रात्रिश् च कृषिश् च वृष्टिश् च त्विषिश्चापचितिश्चापश्चौषधयश्चोर्क् च सूनृता च तास् त्वा दीक्षमाणम् अनुदीक्षन्ताम् इति
10.11.1.r.m: Day and night, agriculture and rain, splendor and reverence, waters and plants, strength and gracious speech—may they follow in consecration after you as you are being consecrated."

10.11.2.a.m: And the adhvaryu makes him recite the Saṃbhāra-yajus formulas.

10.11.4.a.m: With "Svāhā to the sacrifice through mind," two [fingers].

10.11.4.d.m: With "Svāhā from the broad atmosphere!" [he makes] two [oblations].

10.11.4.e.s: svāhā yajñaṃ vātādārabha iti muṣṭīkaroti vācaṃ ca yacchati
10.11.4.e.d: स्वाहा यज्ञं वातादारभ इति मुष्टीकरोति वाचं च यच्छति
10.11.4.e.m: With "Svāhā! I seize the sacrifice from the wind!" he clenches his fists and restrains his speech.

10.11.5.a.s: athainaṃ trirupāṃśvāvedayati triruccairadīkṣiṣṭāyaṃ brāhmaṇo 'sāvamuṣya putro 'muṣya pautro 'muṣya naptāmuṣyāḥ putro 'muṣyāḥ pautro 'muṣyā napteti
10.11.5.a.d: अथैनं त्रिरुपांश्वावेदयति त्रिरुच्चैरदीक्षिष्टायं ब्राह्मणो ऽसावमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्य पौत्रो ऽमुष्य नप्तामुष्याः पुत्रो ऽमुष्याः पौत्रो ऽमुष्या नप्तेति
10.11.5.a.m: Then [the adhvaryu] announces him three times silently and three times aloud: "This brahmin has undergone consecration: so-and-so, son of so-and-so, grandson of so-and-so, great-grandson of so-and-so; son of such-and-such a woman, grandson of such-and-such a woman, great-grandson of such-and-such a woman!"

10.11.6.a.s: brahmaṇo vā eṣa jāyate yo dīkṣate /
10.11.6.a.d: ब्रह्मणो वा एष जायते यो दीक्षते ।
10.11.6.a.m: He who undergoes consecration is indeed born from the brahman.

10.11.6.b.m: Therefore, even in the case of a rājanya or a vaiśya, he announces him merely as: "A brahmin!"

10.12.2.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta tapasvī syād iti taṃ pūrvāhṇe
10.12.2.a.d: यं कामयेत तपस्वी स्याद् इति तं पूर्वाह्णे
10.12.2.a.m: One whom he desires to become ascetic, him [he should consecrate] in the forenoon.

10.12.3.a.m: Restraining his speech and practicing ascetic fervor, he sits until the stars rise.

10.12.4.a.s: vatsasyaikaṃ stanamavaśiṣyetarānvrataṃ dohayitvā yāḥ paśūnāmṛṣabhe vācastāḥ sūryo agre śukro agre tāḥ prahiṇvo yathābhagaṃ vo atra śivā nastāḥ punarāyantu vāca iti japitvā vrataṃ kṛṇuteti vācaṃ visṛjate
10.12.4.a.d: वत्सस्यैकं स्तनमवशिष्येतरान्व्रतं दोहयित्वा याः पशूनामृषभे वाचस्ताः सूर्यो अग्रे शुक्रो अग्रे ताः प्रहिण्वो यथाभगं वो अत्र शिवा नस्ताः पुनरायन्तु वाच इति जपित्वा व्रतं कृणुतेति वाचं विसृजते
10.12.4.a.m: Having left one teat for the calf and milked the other [teats] for the fast-milk, he recites softly: "The voices of the animals in the bull, which were at the forefront of the sun, at the forefront of the bright [soma], I send them forth according to your share here; may those auspicious voices return to us!" and releases his speech with: "Prepare the fast-food!"

10.12.5.a.m: With "You are seekers," he releases four fingers:

10.12.5.b.m: two on one [hand], two on the other.

10.12.7.a.m: He adds "Canasita" or "Vicakṣaṇa" at the end of the names.

10.12.8.b.m: "Vicakṣaṇa" for a rājanya and a vaiśya.

10.12.10.a.m: He should not converse with a woman, nor with a śūdra.

10.12.12.a.s: yadyenaṃ śūdreṇa saṃvāda upapadyeta brāhmaṇarājanyavaiśyānāmekaṃ brūyādimamitthaṃ brūhīti vājasaneyakam
10.12.12.a.d: यद्येनं शूद्रेण संवाद उपपद्येत ब्राह्मणराजन्यवैश्यानामेकं ब्रूयादिममित्थं ब्रूहीति वाजसनेयकम्
10.12.12.a.m: If a conversation with a śūdra occurs, he should tell one among the brahmins, rājanyas, or vaiśyas: "Tell this man in this manner"—this is the Vājasaneyaka view.

10.12.13.a.s: kāmaṃ śūdreṇa saṃbhāṣeta yaḥ pāpena karmaṇānabhilakṣitaḥ syāditi śaṭyāyanakam
10.12.13.a.d: कामं शूद्रेण संभाषेत यः पापेन कर्मणानभिलक्षितः स्यादिति शट्यायनकम्
10.12.13.a.m: At will, he may converse with a śūdra who is not marked by an evil deed—this is the Śāṭyāyanaka view.

10.12.14.a.s: abhivadati nābhivādayate 'pyācāryaṃ śvaśuraṃ rājānam iti śāṭyāyanakam
10.12.14.a.d: अभिवदति नाभिवादयते ऽप्याचार्यं श्वशुरं राजानम् इति शाट्यायनकम्
10.12.14.a.m: He salutes, but does not allow himself to be saluted, even by a teacher, a father-in-law, or a king—this is the Śāṭyāyanaka view.

10.13.1.a.s: agnir vai dīkṣitas tasmād enaṃ nopaspṛśet
10.13.1.a.d: अग्निर् वै दीक्षितस् तस्माद् एनं नोपस्पृशेत्
10.13.1.a.m: The consecrated one is indeed Agni; therefore one should not touch him.

10.13.3.a.m: He should not untie the black-antelope horn before the sacrificial gifts are led away.

10.13.5.a.m: Covering [his mouth] with his hand, he smiles.

10.13.6.a.s: madhu māṃsaṃ striyamanṛtamupariśayyāṃ ṣṭhīvanaṃ vikāle niṣkramaṇaṃ dīkṣitavimitātpravāsamiti varjayet
10.13.6.a.d: मधु मांसं स्त्रियमनृतमुपरिशय्यां ष्ठीवनं विकाले निष्क्रमणं दीक्षितविमितात्प्रवासमिति वर्जयेत्
10.13.6.a.m: He should avoid honey, meat, women, falsehood, sleeping on an elevated bed, spitting, going outside at an improper time, and being absent from the enclosure of the consecrated.

10.13.7.a.m: He should not pass urine or feces by day.

10.13.9.a.s: mūtraṃ cikīrṣanniyaṃ te yajñiyā tanūriti tṛṇaṃ loṣṭaṃ vāpādāyāpo muñcāmi na prajāmaṃhomucaḥ svāhākṛtāḥ pṛthivīmāviśateti mūtraṃ visṛjyācamya pṛthivyā saṃbhavetyapāttaṃ pratinidadhāti
10.13.9.a.d: मूत्रं चिकीर्षन्नियं ते यज्ञिया तनूरिति तृणं लोष्टं वापादायापो मुञ्चामि न प्रजामंहोमुचः स्वाहाकृताः पृथिवीमाविशतेति मूत्रं विसृज्याचम्य पृथिव्या संभवेत्यपात्तं प्रतिनिदधाति
10.13.9.a.m: Intending to urinate, having taken up a blade of grass or a clod of earth with "This is your sacrificial body," having discharged urine with "I release the waters, not offspring; releasers from distress, consecrated by svāhā, enter the earth!" and having sipped water, he replaces the taken [grass or clod] with "Be united with the earth!"

10.13.10.a.m: "Whatever of my milk went from the fullness there, that you have caused to settle;

10.13.10.b.s: agnihotramiva somena tadahaṃ punarādada iti retaḥ saknnamanumantrayate
10.13.10.b.d: अग्निहोत्रमिव सोमेन तदहं पुनरादद इति रेतः सक्न्नमनुमन्त्रयते
10.13.10.b.m: like the agnihotra with soma, that I take back to myself"—with this he recites over semen that has been discharged.

10.13.11.a.m: "Whatever sap of mine has been spat out here unremembered,

10.13.11.b.s: agniṣṭatsomahā pṛthivī punarātmandadhātu ma iti charditvā ṣṭhutvā vā //
10.13.11.b.d: अग्निष्टत्सोमहा पृथिवी पुनरात्मन्दधातु म इति छर्दित्वा ष्ठुत्वा वा ॥
10.13.11.b.m: may Agni, the slayer of Soma, may the earth place that back into myself"—[he recites this] having vomited or spat.

10.13.11.c.s: yadannamadya te naktaṃ na tatprātaḥ kṣudho 'vati /
10.13.11.c.d: यदन्नमद्य ते नक्तं न तत्प्रातः क्षुधो ऽवति ।
10.13.11.c.m: "Whatever food is eaten by you tonight, that does not ward off hunger in the morning;

10.13.11.d.s: sarvaṃ tadasmānmā hiṃsīrnahi taddadṛśe diveti svapne 'nnaṃ bhuktvā //
10.13.11.d.d: सर्वं तदस्मान्मा हिंसीर्नहि तद्ददृशे दिवेति स्वप्ने ऽन्नं भुक्त्वा ॥
10.13.11.d.m: do not injure us from all that, for that was not seen by day"—[he recites this] having eaten food in a dream.

10.13.11.e.m: With "Svāhā to the Rudrian waters!" [he recites] having seen blood gushing out.

10.14.1.a.s: bībhatsā nāma sthāpaḥ svāhākṛtāḥ pṛthivīmāviśateti snūhānam /
10.14.1.a.d: बीभत्सा नाम स्थापः स्वाहाकृताः पृथिवीमाविशतेति स्नूहानम् ।
10.14.1.a.m: With "You are waters named Disgusting; consecrated by svāhā, enter the earth!" [he addresses] nasal mucus.

10.14.1.b.m: With "You are waters named Compassion; consecrated by svāhā, enter the earth!" [he addresses] a tear.

10.14.1.c.s: tapasyā nāma sthāpaḥ svāhākṛtāḥ pṛthivīmāviśateti svedam
10.14.1.c.d: तपस्या नाम स्थापः स्वाहाकृताः पृथिवीमाविशतेति स्वेदम्
10.14.1.c.m: With "You are waters named Austere; consecrated by svāhā, enter the earth!" [he addresses] sweat.

10.14.2.a.m: He does not go out by the western door.

10.14.3.a.m: He does not make an oblation that is unconnected with the sacrificial rite.

10.14.5.a.m: He does not sacrifice with the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

10.14.8.a.m: He remains consecrated for twelve days at least.

10.14.8.b.s: māsaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yadā vā kṛśaḥ syād ity aparam
10.14.8.b.d: मासं संवत्सरं यदा वा कृशः स्याद् इत्य् अपरम्
10.14.8.b.m: For a month, for a year, or "whenever he becomes lean"—this is another [view].

10.14.9.b.s: yadā vai dīkṣitaḥ kṛśo bhavatyatha medhyo bhavati /
10.14.9.b.d: यदा वै दीक्षितः कृशो भवत्यथ मेध्यो भवति ।
10.14.9.b.m: "Indeed, when the consecrated one becomes lean, then he becomes fit for sacrifice.

10.14.9.c.m: When there is nothing inside him, then he becomes fit for sacrifice.

10.14.9.d.d: यदास्य त्वचास्थि संधीयते ऽथ मेध्यो भवति ।
10.14.9.d.m: When his skin and bones are joined together, then he becomes fit for sacrifice.

10.14.9.e.m: When the black of his eyes disappears, then he becomes fit for sacrifice.

10.14.10.c.m: Whatever of his limbs diminishes, he just offers that as oblation"—so it is known [from scripture].

10.15.1.a.s: ekā dīkṣā tisra upasadaḥ pañcamīṃ prasutaḥ /
10.15.1.a.d: एका दीक्षा तिस्र उपसदः पञ्चमीं प्रसुतः ।
10.15.1.a.m: One consecration [day], three upasad [days], pressed on the fifth [day].

10.15.1.b.s: tisro vā dīkṣāstisra upasadaḥ saptamīṃ prasutaḥ /
10.15.1.b.d: तिस्रो वा दीक्षास्तिस्र उपसदः सप्तमीं प्रसुतः ।
10.15.1.b.m: Or three consecration [days], three upasad [days], pressed on the seventh [day].

10.15.1.c.d: चतस्रो वा दीक्षास्तिस्र उपसदो ऽष्टमीं प्रसुतः
10.15.1.c.m: Or there are four consecration days and three Upasads; on the eighth day the pressing takes place.

10.15.2.a.m: The consecration takes place on the new moon day or on the day of sacrifice.

10.15.2.b.m: The pressing day falls on the full moon day or on the day of sacrifice.

10.15.4.a.m: The consecration takes place on the new moon day or on the day of sacrifice;

10.15.4.b.m: the pressing day falls on the new moon day or on the day of sacrifice.

10.15.4.c.m: The consecration takes place on the full moon day or on the day of sacrifice;

10.15.4.d.m: the pressing day falls on the full moon day or on the day of sacrifice.

10.15.5.a.m: The sun should not set or rise upon him anywhere else than inside the consecrated person's hut.

10.15.6.a.m: If set upon by the sun, he should whisper verses addressed to Varuṇa;

10.15.7.a.m: Having seen something impure, he whispers: 'My mind is unfettered...'

10.15.8.a.m: Rained upon, he whispers: 'O wetting waters, bestow strength...'

10.15.9.a.s: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ prāṅ śete na nyaṅnottāno nāgnerapaparyāvarteta
10.15.9.a.d: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं प्राङ् शेते न न्यङ्नोत्तानो नाग्नेरपपर्यावर्तेत
10.15.9.a.m: To the south of the āhavanīya fire, he lies facing east, neither face down nor on his back, and he must not turn away from the fire.

10.15.10.a.s: yadyapaparyāvarteta viśve devā abhi māmāvavṛtrānniti japet
10.15.10.a.d: यद्यपपर्यावर्तेत विश्वे देवा अभि मामाववृत्रान्निति जपेत्
10.15.10.a.m: If he should turn away, he should whisper: 'May all the gods turn toward me...'

10.15.11.a.m: He should not sit anywhere other than on the black antelope skin.

10.15.11.b.m: If he should sit elsewhere, he should whisper: 'The sacrifice has gone to the divine folk...'

10.15.12.a.m: He must not become separated from the staff or from the black antelope skin.

10.15.12.b.m: Having put down both, he may pass urine and feces.

10.15.13.a.m: The insignia of the consecrated person belong to the wife only to the extent stated.

10.15.15.a.m: [Another] should not put on the garment of the consecrated person.

10.15.16.a.m: Or, once the portion for the sacrifice has been set aside, they may eat from the remainder;

10.15.16.b.m: or when the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma has been completed;

10.16.1.a.m: He should not release his speech before the stars [appear].

10.16.1.b.s: yadi visṛjedidaṃ viṣṇustvamagne vratapā asīti japitvā vācaṃ yacchet
10.16.1.b.d: यदि विसृजेदिदं विष्णुस्त्वमग्ने व्रतपा असीति जपित्वा वाचं यच्छेत्
10.16.1.b.m: If he should release it, he should restrain his speech after having whispered: 'Through this, Viṣṇu...' [and] 'You, O Agni, are the guardian of vows...'

10.16.3.b.m: speech is to be restrained after reciting a verse to Viṣṇu, one to Agni-Viṣṇu, one to Sarasvatī, and lastly one to Bṛhaspati.

10.16.4.a.m: Ālekhana says: He should release speech only over the milked [vow-drink].

10.16.5.a.m: It has been stated: 'Barley gruel is for a rājanya.'

10.16.6.a.m: Some teach without reference to caste that one should take as vow-drink either barley gruel or pure milk.

10.16.7.a.m: Some indeed take milk as that vow-drink.

10.16.7.c.m: Having cooked barley gruel in the milk itself, he should consume it as the vow-drink.

10.16.8.a.m: If the cow that yields the vow-drink yields little, one should milk another.

10.16.9.a.m: If there is no other, he should cook it mixed with water.

10.16.10.a.s: yadi payo na syādapsveva yavāgūṃ śrapayitvā vratayet
10.16.10.a.d: यदि पयो न स्यादप्स्वेव यवागूं श्रपयित्वा व्रतयेत्
10.16.10.a.m: If there is no milk, having cooked barley gruel in water alone, he should consume it as the vow-drink.

10.16.11.b.m: He should certainly not abstain from consuming the vow-drink, so that the agnihotra is not interrupted.

10.16.12.a.m: If he desires curds, they should prepare just curds for him.

10.16.13.a.s: yadyannīyāddhānā asmā anvāvapeyuḥ saktūnasmā anvāvapeyurghṛtamasmā anvānayeyuḥ
10.16.13.a.d: यद्यन्नीयाद्धाना अस्मा अन्वावपेयुः सक्तूनस्मा अन्वावपेयुर्घृतमस्मा अन्वानयेयुः
10.16.13.a.m: If he desires food, they should throw parched grains into it for him, throw groats into it for him, or pour clarified butter into it for him.

10.16.14.a.m: He may even consume as the vow-drink any one among the agnihotra oblations, with the exception of meat.

10.16.15.a.d: सो ऽयं दैक्षो वादो भवतीति खल्वाहुः ।
10.16.15.a.m: Indeed they say: 'This is the rule regarding the consecration.'

10.16.15.b.m: In the case of all [sacrifices], the procedure for taking the vow-drink during the Upasads has been handed down without specific initiation.

10.16.16.a.d: अपराह्णे ऽधिवृक्षसूर्ये वा व्रतप्रदो वाचं यमयति ।
10.16.16.a.m: In the afternoon, or when the sun is at the level of the tree tops, the one who brings the vow-drink causes [the sacrificer] to restrain his speech.

10.16.16.b.s: agnīñjyotiṣmataḥ kuruta dīkṣita vācaṃ yaccha patni vācaṃ yaccheti saṃpreṣyati
10.16.16.b.d: अग्नीञ्ज्योतिष्मतः कुरुत दीक्षित वाचं यच्छ पत्नि वाचं यच्छेति संप्रेष्यति
10.16.16.b.m: He gives the ritual call: 'Make the fires luminous! Consecrated one, restrain your speech! Wife, restrain your speech!'

10.17.1.a.m: When the stars have risen, speech is released as before.

10.17.2.a.m: In this manner he restrains [speech] towards sunrise;

10.17.3.a.m: He consumes the vow-drink at midday and at midnight;

10.17.4.a.m: or after having passed the human mealtime.

10.17.5.a.m: Some say: [he consumes] the evening milk in the latter part of the night, and the morning milk in the afternoon.

10.17.6.a.m: He boils the vrata [milk] of the consecrated [sacrificer] on the gārhapatya;

10.17.7.a.m: Whatever is the expiation for spilled agnihotra, that is [the expiation] for the vrata.

10.17.8.a.s: agnihotravattūṣṇīmunnīyāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ vratamatyāhṛtya prayacchannāha vratya vrataya vratamupehīti
10.17.8.a.d: अग्निहोत्रवत्तूष्णीमुन्नीयापरेणाहवनीयं व्रतमत्याहृत्य प्रयच्छन्नाह व्रत्य व्रतय व्रतमुपेहीति
10.17.8.a.m: Having scooped it out silently, just as [for] the agnihotra, and having brought the vrata around to the west of the āhavanġya, handing it over, he says: 'O consecrated one, partake of the vrata; approach the vrata.'

10.17.9.a.s: daivīṃ dhiyaṃ manāmaha iti hastāvavanijya ye devā manojātā manoyuja iti dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ pariśrite vratayati
10.17.9.a.d: दैवीं धियं मनामह इति हस्ताववनिज्य ये देवा मनोजाता मनोयुज इति दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं परिश्रिते व्रतयति
10.17.9.a.m: Having washed his hands with: 'We contemplate divine thought...', he partakes of the vrata south of the āhavanġya, in an enclosed space, with: 'Which gods are mind-born, mind-yoked...'

10.17.10.a.m: Unconsecrated persons do not see him partaking of the vrata.

10.17.11.a.s: śivāḥ pītā bhavatha yūyamāpo 'smākaṃ yonāvudare suśevāḥ /
10.17.11.a.d: शिवाः पीता भवथ यूयमापो ऽस्माकं योनावुदरे सुशेवाः ।
10.17.11.a.m: 'Favorable when drunk may you waters become, very kindly in our womb, the belly;

10.17.11.b.s: irāvatīranamīvā anāgasaḥ śivā no bhavatha jīvasa iti vratayitvā nābhideśamabhimṛśate
10.17.11.b.d: इरावतीरनमीवा अनागसः शिवा नो भवथ जीवस इति व्रतयित्वा नाभिदेशमभिमृशते
10.17.11.b.m: rich in nourishment, free from disease, sinless, favorable may you become to us for living' — having partaken of the vrata with this [mantra], he touches the region of his navel,
