10.17.13.a.m: The wife partakes of the vrata silently in her own place.

10.18.1.a.m: When about to sleep, he addresses the āhavanġya with: 'O Agni, watch well!'

10.18.2.a.s: tvamagne vratapā asīti prabudhya muṣṭī vācaṃ vā visṛjyādīkṣitavādaṃ voditvā
10.18.2.a.d: त्वमग्ने व्रतपा असीति प्रबुध्य मुष्टी वाचं वा विसृज्यादीक्षितवादं वोदित्वा
10.18.2.a.m: Having awakened, if he has opened his fists or speech, or has spoken words improper for the consecrated, [he addresses it] with: 'O Agni, you are the guardian of vows.'

10.18.3.a.s: viśve devā abhi māmāvavṛtranniti prabudhya japati /
10.18.3.a.d: विश्वे देवा अभि मामाववृत्रन्निति प्रबुध्य जपति ।
10.18.3.a.m: Having awakened, he murmurs: 'May all the gods turn toward me;

10.18.3.b.m: Mind has come again, life-span has come again, breath has come again, purpose has come again;

10.18.3.c.d: वैश्वानरो ऽदब्धस्तनूपा अवबाधतां दुरितानि विश्वेति च
10.18.3.c.m: and may unbeguiled Vaiśvānara, protector of the body, ward off all distress.'

10.18.4.a.m: Therefore, the consecrated [sacrificer] should beg for maintenance for twelve days.

10.18.4.b.m: 'He thereby indeed gathers the sacrifice together,' so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

10.18.5.a.m: He instructs the bringers of gifts with: 'Pūṣan is with the gift...'

10.18.6.a.m: He receives [them] according to their characteristics with: 'You are Candramas...'

10.18.7.a.m: [He receives] others with: 'The divine Savitṛ, giver of wealth from wealth...'

10.18.8.a.m: Among them, he assigns one that is lost with: 'To Vāyu thee!'

10.18.9.a.m: one that has died in the waters with: 'To Varuṇa thee!'

10.18.10.a.m: one that has collapsed or is shattered with: 'To Nirṛti thee!'

10.19.1.a.m: one struck by lightning, struck by a sheep-slayer, or drowned in water with: 'To the Maruts thee!'

10.19.2.a.m: one killed by Mahādeva with: 'To Rudra thee!'

10.19.3.a.s: indrāya tvā prashvana iti yāṃ senābhītvarī vindeta
10.19.3.a.d: इन्द्राय त्वा प्रस्ह्वन इति यां सेनाभीत्वरी विन्देत
10.19.3.a.m: one which an attacking army has seized with: 'To Indra the conqueror thee!'

10.19.4.a.m: one that died of an unknown illness with: 'To Yama thee!'

10.19.5.a.m: He should not pasture among cattle [any animal] obtained from those assigned away.

10.19.6.a.m: Having mounted the fires into separate churning sticks, he sets forth in a chariot.

10.19.7.a.m: In its absence, taking a chariot-part.

10.19.8.a.m: The departure is made with: 'From the auspicious unto the better...'

10.19.9.a.m: He wades across water with: 'O divine waters...'

10.19.10.a.s: acchinnaṃ tantuṃ pṛthivyā anugeṣamiti hastena loṣṭaṃ vimṛdnātyā pārāt
10.19.10.a.d: अच्छिन्नं तन्तुं पृथिव्या अनुगेषमिति हस्तेन लोष्टं विमृद्नात्या पारात्
10.19.10.a.m: He crushes a clod of earth with his hand until the other shore, with: 'May I follow the unbroken thread of the earth.'

10.19.11.a.s: pṛthivyā saṃbhaveti sikatā loṣṭaṃ vā madhye pāre ca nyasyati
10.19.11.a.d: पृथिव्या संभवेति सिकता लोष्टं वा मध्ये पारे च न्यस्यति
10.19.11.a.m: With: 'Be united with the earth,' he throws sand or a clod of earth into the middle and on the farther shore.

10.19.13.a.m: With two churning sticks [or] with churning sticks, according to some.

10.19.14.a.m: He should not be separated from the chariot or from the chariot-part.

10.19.15.a.m: Here, some prescribe settling upon the sacrificial ground.

10.19.16.a.m: Whoever would settle here should set out;

10.20.1.a.m: Elevated to the south, sloped down to the north, sloping toward the east, or sloping toward the northeast is the sacrificial ground.

10.20.2.a.m: Or where many brāhmaṇas would agree.

10.20.3.a.m: 'The fires indeed are the sacrificial ground;

10.20.3.b.s: yatra kvacāgnīnādhāya yajate devayajana eva yajata iti vijñāyate
10.20.3.b.d: यत्र क्वचाग्नीनाधाय यजते देवयजन एव यजत इति विज्ञायते
10.20.3.b.m: wherever having established the fires he sacrifices, he sacrifices on the sacrificial ground indeed,' so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

10.20.4.a.m: 'The sacrificial gifts indeed are the sacrificial ground;

10.20.4.b.s: dakṣiṇāścetkalyāṇīrdadāti devayajana eva yajata ity eke
10.20.4.b.d: दक्षिणाश्चेत्कल्याणीर्ददाति देवयजन एव यजत इत्य् एके
10.20.4.b.m: if he gives fine sacrificial gifts, he sacrifices on the sacrificial ground indeed,' so say some.

10.20.6.a.m: Practicing sorcery, he should sacrifice on a clearing [in the forest].

10.20.7.a.m: From which tree [or] ant-hills they would remove [material], and also dig up [earth].

10.20.8.a.m: He should cause one who is accused of sin to sacrifice secretly, in a hiding-place, in a forest.

10.20.9.a.m: They should undertake the pṛṣṭha chants out of sight;

10.20.10.a.s: yaḥ kāmayetobhayeṣāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ prakāśaṃ gaccheyamiti na prācīnaṃ devayajanāddevayajanamātramucchiṃṣet
10.20.10.a.d: यः कामयेतोभयेषां देवमनुष्याणां प्रकाशं गच्छेयमिति न प्राचीनं देवयजनाद्देवयजनमात्रमुच्छिंषेत्
10.20.10.a.m: One who desires: 'May I become manifest to both gods and men,' should not leave behind [ground] the size of a sacrificial ground to the east of the sacrificial ground.

10.20.11.a.s: yatrāpo devayajanaṃ cāntareṇa panthā abhividhāvettasminyājayedyaṃ kāmayeta nainamuttaro yajña upanamediti
10.20.11.a.d: यत्रापो देवयजनं चान्तरेण पन्था अभिविधावेत्तस्मिन्याजयेद्यं कामयेत नैनमुत्तरो यज्ञ उपनमेदिति
10.20.11.a.m: Where a path runs across between the water and the sacrificial ground, upon that he should cause him to sacrifice whom he would wish: 'May a further sacrifice not fall to his lot.'

10.20.12.a.m: Having said: 'He should purchase the king [Soma] from a descendant of Kutsa or from another brāhmaṇa,' he says: 'even from a non-brāhmaṇa.'

10.20.13.a.s: uttaravedideśa uparavadeśe vā lohitaṃ carmānaḍuhaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya dkṣiṇe carmapakṣe rājānaṃ nivapati /
10.20.13.a.d: उत्तरवेदिदेश उपरवदेशे वा लोहितं चर्मानडुहं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य द्क्षिणे चर्मपक्षे राजानं निवपति ।
10.20.13.a.m: Having spread a red ox-hide, with its neck pointing east and the hair upward, in the place of the uttaravedi or in the place of the uparavas, he pours out the king [Soma] upon the southern half of the hide;

10.20.13.b.m: the soma-seller sits down on the northern [half].

10.20.14.a.s: udakumbhaṃ rājānaṃ somavikrayiṇamiti sarvataḥ pariśrityottareṇa dvāraṃ kṛtvā vicityaḥ somā3 ityuktam
10.20.14.a.d: उदकुम्भं राजानं सोमविक्रयिणमिति सर्वतः परिश्रित्योत्तरेण द्वारं कृत्वा विचित्यः सोमा3 इत्युक्तम्
10.20.14.a.m: Having enclosed all around the water-jar, the king [Soma], and the soma-seller, and having made an entrance to the north, it is said: 'Is the Soma to be inspected?'

10.20.15.a.m: Having said: 'O soma seller, cleanse the soma,' he turns away.

10.20.16.b.m: The sacrificer should not sort out the soma.

10.20.17.a.m: Neither his man, nor the adhvaryu, nor the adhvaryu's man.

10.20.18.a.m: They should be onlookers while the King [Soma] is being picked out.

10.20.19.a.m: With the two [verses], "I am from you...", "Being summoned...", the sacrificer attends upon the āhavanīya.

10.21.1.a.m: He sets in motion the procedure of the introductory offering (prāyaṇīyā).

10.21.2.a.m: Having made the broom and strewn [grass] around the fires, he proceeds to the rites beginning with the washing of hands.

10.21.3.a.m: He arranges the vessels according to need,

10.21.3.b.m: a pot in place of the potsherds.

10.21.4.a.m: At the time of pouring out [the oblation-materials], the introductory offering is a boiled rice oblation for Aditi in milk.

10.21.5.a.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the ritual call, he issues the ritual call omitting the [sacrificer's] wife.

10.21.6.a.s: yāḥ kṛtāyāṃ vedyāṃ codyante saiva tāsāṃ vediḥ /
10.21.6.a.d: याः कृतायां वेद्यां चोद्यन्ते सैव तासां वेदिः ।
10.21.6.a.m: For those [rites] that are prescribed [to be performed] on a prepared altar ground, that very altar ground serves for them;

10.21.6.b.s: yāḥ stīrṇe barhiṣi tadeva tāsāṃ barhiḥ
10.21.6.b.d: याः स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि तदेव तासां बर्हिः
10.21.6.b.m: for those [prescribed to be performed] on strewn sacrificial grass, that very sacrificial grass serves for them.

10.21.7.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, in the introductory offering, which has no after-offerings, he takes four [ladlefuls] in the juhū

10.21.7.b.m: and four in the upabhṛt, for the sake of combining them.

10.21.8.a.m: In the concluding offering (udayanīyā), which has no fore-offerings, he does not take [any] in the juhū,

10.21.8.b.m: [but takes] four in the upabhṛt for the sake of the after-offerings.

10.21.9.a.m: With the six-hotṛ formula, he sets down the introductory offering.

10.21.10.a.m: It has already been stated: "having fore-offerings, [but] without after-offerings".

10.21.11.a.m: He offers four butter portions facing each direction:

10.21.11.b.s: pathyāṃ svastiṃ purastādagniṃ dakṣiṇataḥ somaṃ paścātsavitāramuttarataḥ /
10.21.11.b.d: पथ्यां स्वस्तिं पुरस्तादग्निं दक्षिणतः सोमं पश्चात्सवितारमुत्तरतः ।
10.21.11.b.m: to Pathyā Svasti in the east, to Agni in the south, to Soma in the west, to Savitṛ in the north,

10.21.12.a.m: Having offered to Aditi and recited the verse addressed to the Maruts, he fills the pot with clarified butter and offers to these deities,

10.21.13.a.m: Or [the rite] may be concluded ending with the śaṃyu [formula].

10.21.14.a.m: However, he should not perform the offerings to the wives of the gods.

10.21.15.a.m: He should perform them at the concluding offering.

10.21.17.a.m: He preserves the clarified butter of the dhruvā ladle.

10.21.18.a.m: In the hall with eastward-pointing rafters, he puts down the sacrificial grass, the unscraped cooking pot, and the stirring stick for the sake of the concluding offering.

10.22.1.a.s: prāyaṇīyāyā dhrauvādaṣṭau juhvāṃ caturo vā gṛhītvā tasmindarbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ niṣṭarkyaṃ baddhvāvadadhātīyaṃ te śukra tanūriti
10.22.1.a.d: प्रायणीयाया ध्रौवादष्टौ जुह्वां चतुरो वा गृहीत्वा तस्मिन्दर्भेण हिरण्यं निष्टर्क्यं बद्ध्वावदधातीयं ते शुक्र तनूरिति
10.22.1.a.m: Having taken eight or four [ladlefuls] into the juhū from the dhruvā of the introductory offering, having tied a piece of gold in a knot that can be loosened with darbha grass, he puts it in [the juhū with the formula]: "This is your bright body..."

10.22.2.a.s: purastāt pratīcī somakrayaṇyavasthitā bhavatyekahāyanī dvihāyanī varṣīyasī vā
10.22.2.a.d: पुरस्तात् प्रतीची सोमक्रयण्यवस्थिता भवत्येकहायनी द्विहायनी वर्षीयसी वा
10.22.2.a.m: The Soma-purchasing cow stands in the east facing west, either one year old, two years old, or older.

10.22.3.a.m: Its marks are: [it is described] with "not hornless, not cropped-eared..."

10.22.4.a.s: yā rohiṇī babhrulomnī pṛśnavālā pṛśniśaphā śucyakṣī śvitropakāśā tayā krīṇīyād ity eke
10.22.4.a.d: या रोहिणी बभ्रुलोम्नी पृश्नवाला पृश्निशफा शुच्यक्षी श्वित्रोपकाशा तया क्रीणीयाद् इत्य् एके
10.22.4.a.m: Some say: "One should buy with one that is reddish, brown-haired, with a speckled tail, speckled hooves, clear eyes, and white-spotted."

10.22.6.a.m: for the Ṣoḍaśin, with a tailless one whose ears are pierced.

10.22.7.a.m: Looking at the Soma-purchasing cow, he offers that clarified butter with the formula: "You are swift..."

10.22.8.a.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā śukramasīti hiraṇyaṃ paścāduddhṛtya vaiśvadevaṃ havirityājyamavekṣya sūryasya cakṣurāruhamityādityamupasthāya cidasi manāsīti somakrayaṇīmabhimantrayate
10.22.8.a.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा शुक्रमसीति हिरण्यं पश्चादुद्धृत्य वैश्वदेवं हविरित्याज्यमवेक्ष्य सूर्यस्य चक्षुरारुहमित्यादित्यमुपस्थाय चिदसि मनासीति सोमक्रयणीमभिमन्त्रयते
10.22.8.a.m: Having taken another four ladlefuls, having lifted out the gold behind [the fire] with the formula "You are bright...", having looked at the clarified butter with the formula "The oblation belonging to All-gods...", having attended upon the sun with the formula "I have mounted the eye of the sun...", he addresses the Soma-purchasing cow with the formula: "You are thought, you are mind..."

10.22.9.a.m: She is not seized by the ear and her foot is not bound.

10.22.10.a.s: mitrastvā padi badhnātviti dakṣiṇaṃ pūrvapādaṃ prekṣate /
10.22.10.a.d: मित्रस्त्वा पदि बध्नात्विति दक्षिणं पूर्वपादं प्रेक्षते ।
10.22.10.a.m: With the formula "May Mitra bind you by the foot", he looks at her right forefoot;

10.22.10.b.m: with the formula "May Pūṣan protect the paths", he recites after her as she walks eastward.

10.22.11.a.s: ṣaṭ padānyanunikrāmati dakṣiṇena padā dakṣiṇāni vasvyasi rudrāsītyetaiḥ pratimantram
10.22.11.a.d: षट् पदान्यनुनिक्रामति दक्षिणेन पदा दक्षिणानि वस्व्यसि रुद्रासीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
10.22.11.a.m: He steps along six footprints with his right foot along the right [footprints], each with its formula: "You are Vasvī", "You are Rudrā"...

10.22.12.a.s: ekamiṣe viṣṇustvānvetu dve ūrje viṣṇustvānvetu trīṇi vratāya viṣṇustvānvetu catvāri mayobhavāya viṣṇustvānvetu pañca paśubhyo viṣṇustvānvetu ṣaḍrāyaspoṣāya viṣṇustvānvetu sapta saptabhyo hotrābhyo viṣṇustvānvetv iti nikramyamāṇeṣu yajamāno 'nuvartayitvā
10.22.12.a.d: एकमिषे विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु द्वे ऊर्जे विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु त्रीणि व्रताय विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु चत्वारि मयोभवाय विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु पञ्च पशुभ्यो विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु षड्रायस्पोषाय विष्णुस्त्वान्वेतु सप्त सप्तभ्यो होत्राभ्यो विष्णुस्त्वान्वेत्व् इति निक्रम्यमाणेषु यजमानो ऽनुवर्तयित्वा
10.22.12.a.m: While they are being stepped along with the formulas, "One for sap, may Viṣṇu follow you; two for strength, may Viṣṇu follow you; three for the vow, may Viṣṇu follow you; four for happiness, may Viṣṇu follow you; five for cattle, may Viṣṇu follow you; six for increase of wealth, may Viṣṇu follow you; seven for the seven hotrās, may Viṣṇu follow you", the sacrificer, having followed after,

10.23.1.a.s: sakhāya saptapadā abhūma sakhyaṃ te gameyaṃ sakhyātte mā yoṣaṃ sakhyān me mā yoṣṭhā iti saptame pade japati
10.23.1.a.d: सखाय सप्तपदा अभूम सख्यं ते गमेयं सख्यात्ते मा योषं सख्यान् मे मा योष्ठा इति सप्तमे पदे जपति
10.23.1.a.m: mutters at the seventh footprint: "Friends having walked seven steps have we become; may I attain your friendship; may I not fall away from your friendship; may you not fall away from my friendship."

10.23.2.a.s: bṛhaspatistvā sumne raṇvatviti sapatamaṃ padamadhvaryurañjalinābhigṛhya pade hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya pṛthivyāstvā mūrdhannājigharmīti hiraṇye hutvāpādāya hiraṇyaṃ devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti sphyamādāya parilikhitaṃ rakṣaḥ parilikhitā arātaya iti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ padaṃ parilikhati yāvadghṛtamanuvisṛtaṃ bhavati
10.23.2.a.d: बृहस्पतिस्त्वा सुम्ने रण्वत्विति सपतमं पदमध्वर्युरञ्जलिनाभिगृह्य पदे हिरण्यं निधाय पृथिव्यास्त्वा मूर्धन्नाजिघर्मीति हिरण्ये हुत्वापादाय हिरण्यं देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति स्फ्यमादाय परिलिखितं रक्षः परिलिखिता अरातय इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं पदं परिलिखति यावद्घृतमनुविसृतं भवति
10.23.2.a.m: The adhvaryu, having grasped around the seventh footprint with folded hands with the formula "May Bṛhaspati delight you in comfort", having placed the piece of gold in the footprint, having offered on the piece of gold with the formula "I sprinkle you on the head of the earth", having picked up the piece of gold, having taken the wooden sword with the formula "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...", traces around the footprint three times from left to right as far as the clarified butter has spread, with the formula: "Traced around is the demon; traced around are the enemies."

10.23.3.a.s: kṛṣṇaviṣāṇyā cānuparilikhyāsme rāya iti sthālyāṃ yāvattmūtaṃ samopya tve rāya iti yajamānāya prayacchati
10.23.3.a.d: कृष्णविषाण्या चानुपरिलिख्यास्मे राय इति स्थाल्यां यावत्त्मूतं समोप्य त्वे राय इति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
10.23.3.a.m: And having traced around it with the black antelope horn, having gathered as much [dust] as fits into a bowl with the formula "In us is wealth", he gives it to the sacrificer with the formula: "In you is wealth."

10.23.5.a.s: māhaṃ rāyaspoṣeṇa viyoṣamiti patnī padaṃ pradīyamānamanumantrayate
10.23.5.a.d: माहं रायस्पोषेण वियोषमिति पत्नी पदं प्रदीयमानमनुमन्त्रयते
10.23.5.a.m: The wife recites after [the dust of] the footprint being handed over: "May I not be separated from the increase of wealth."

10.23.6.a.s: saṃ devi devyorvaśyā paśyasveti somakrayaṇyā patnīṃ saṃkhyāpayati
10.23.6.a.d: सं देवि देव्योर्वश्या पश्यस्वेति सोमक्रयण्या पत्नीं संख्यापयति
10.23.6.a.m: He causes the wife to look at the Soma-purchasing cow with the formula: "Look together, O goddess, with the divine Urvaśī."

10.23.7.a.s: tvaṣṭīmatī te sapeyeti patnī somakrayaṇīm abhimantrayate
10.23.7.a.d: त्वष्टीमती ते सपेयेति पत्नी सोमक्रयणीम् अभिमन्त्रयते
10.23.7.a.m: The wife addresses the Soma-purchasing cow with the formula: "Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, may I serve you."

10.23.8.a.m: The sacrificer [addresses it] with: "Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, may we serve you."

10.23.9.a.s: yataḥ padamapāttaṃ tasminsahiraṇyau pāṇī prakṣālyonnambhaya pṛthivīmaityadbhirupaninīya padaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya tṛtīyamuttarto gārhapatyasya śīte bhasmanyupavapati /
10.23.9.a.d: यतः पदमपात्तं तस्मिन्सहिरण्यौ पाणी प्रक्षाल्योन्नम्भय पृथिवीमैत्यद्भिरुपनिनीय पदं त्रैधं विभज्य तृतीयमुत्तर्तो गार्हपत्यस्य शीते भस्मन्युपवपति ।
10.23.9.a.m: At the place from where the [dust of the] footprint was taken, having washed his hands together with the gold, having poured water on it with the formula "Moisten the earth...", having divided the [dust of the] footprint into three parts, he scatters a third in the cool ashes north of the gārhapatya,

10.23.9.c.m: and hands a third to the wife.

10.23.10.a.m: She deposits it in the house.

10.24.1.a.m: Here, some prescribe the attendance on the sun and the rites of pouring out and so on of the King [Soma].

10.24.2.a.s: api panthāmagasmahītyuddhṛtapūrvaphalakenānasā pariśritena chadiṣmatā prāñcaḥ somamaccha yānti
10.24.2.a.d: अपि पन्थामगस्महीत्युद्धृतपूर्वफलकेनानसा परिश्रितेन छदिष्मता प्राञ्चः सोममच्छ यान्ति
10.24.2.a.m: With the formula "We have reached the path...", they go facing east toward the Soma, with a cart that has its front plank removed, is enclosed on all sides, and is roofed.

10.24.3.a.m: They carry on the head what was purchased on the mountain.

10.24.4.a.s: apareṇottareṇa vā rājānaṃ prāgīṣamudagīsaṃ vā naddhayugaṃ śakaṭaṃ cubukapratiṣṭhitam
10.24.4.a.d: अपरेणोत्तरेण वा राजानं प्रागीषमुदगीसं वा नद्धयुगं शकटं चुबुकप्रतिष्ठितम्
10.24.4.a.m: Behind or to the north of the King [Soma], the cart has its yoke tied, its pole pointing eastward or northward, resting upon its support.

10.24.5.a.s: aṃśunā te aṃśuḥ pṛcyatāmiti yajamāno rājānamabhimantrayate
10.24.5.a.d: अंशुना ते अंशुः पृच्यतामिति यजमानो राजानमभिमन्त्रयते
10.24.5.a.m: The sacrificer addresses the King [Soma] with the formula: "May your stalk be united with stalk..."

10.24.6.a.m: It has already been stated: "For him whom he might wish, 'May he be without cattle', [he should take] from a withered [plant]..."

10.24.7.a.s: kṣaumaṃ vāso dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vā prāgdaśamuttaradaśaṃ carmaṇyāstṛṇāti /
10.24.7.a.d: क्षौमं वासो द्विगुणं त्रिगुणं वा प्राग्दशमुत्तरदशं चर्मण्यास्तृणाति ।
10.24.7.a.m: He spreads a linen cloth, two-layered or three-layered, with its fringes pointing eastward or northward, upon the skin.

10.24.8.a.s: tasminharaṇyapāṇiraṅguṣṭhena kaniṣṭhikayā cāṅgulyāṃśūnsaṃgṛhyānyacannabhi tyaṃ devaṃ savitāramityaticchandasarcā mimīte
10.24.8.a.d: तस्मिन्हरण्यपाणिरङ्गुष्ठेन कनिष्ठिकया चाङ्गुल्यांशून्संगृह्यान्यचन्नभि त्यं देवं सवितारमित्यतिच्छन्दसर्चा मिमीते
10.24.8.a.m: Holding gold in his hand, seizing the soma shoots with the thumb and little finger [while leaving] the other [fingers] bent, he measures [them] out on it with the over-metered verse: 'Towards that divine Savitṛ...'

10.24.9.a.m: In this way, [he measures] each [time] releasing [one finger].

10.24.10.a.m: He presses the thumb against each of them.

10.24.11.a.s: yayā prathamaṃ na tayā pañcamaṃ tayaivottamam
10.24.11.a.d: यया प्रथमं न तया पञ्चमं तयैवोत्तमम्
10.24.11.a.m: With whichever [finger] he measures first, not with that does he measure the fifth; with that very [finger] he measures the last.

10.24.12.a.m: He measures five times with a yajus formula,

10.24.13.a.m: Thus [he repeats] twice, thrice, or an unmeasured number of times.

10.24.14.a.s: prajābhyastvetyavaśiṣṭānaṃśūnupasamūhya kṣaumeṇa vāsasopasaṃgṛhya prāṇāya tveti dviguṇenoṣṇīṣeṇopanahya vyānāya tveti visrasyāvekṣate prajāstvamanuprāṇihi prajāstvāmanuprāṇantviti
10.24.14.a.d: प्रजाभ्यस्त्वेत्यवशिष्टानंशूनुपसमूह्य क्षौमेण वाससोपसंगृह्य प्राणाय त्वेति द्विगुणेनोष्णीषेणोपनह्य व्यानाय त्वेति विस्रस्यावेक्षते प्रजास्त्वमनुप्राणिहि प्रजास्त्वामनुप्राणन्त्विति
10.24.14.a.m: Gathering together the remaining shoots with 'For offspring thee,' gathering [them] up with the linen cloth, tying [them] up with 'For out-breathing thee' with a double turban, and loosening [it] with 'For diffusive breathing thee,' he looks [at them] with: 'Breathe along with the offspring; may the offspring breathe along with thee.'

10.24.15.a.s: eṣa te gāyatro bhāga ity etair yajamāno rājanamupatiṣṭhate
10.24.15.a.d: एष ते गायत्रो भाग इत्य् एतैर् यजमानो राजनमुपतिष्ठते
10.24.15.a.m: With [the formulas beginning]: 'This is thy Gāyatra portion...', the sacrificer waits upon the king (Soma).

10.25.1.a.s: deva sūrya somaṃ kreṣyāmastaṃ te prabrūmastsaṃ tvaṃ viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ kratūnkalpaya dakṣiṇāḥ kalpaya yathartu yathādevatamityādityam upasthāya somavikrayiṇe rājānaṃ pradāya paṇate
10.25.1.a.d: देव सूर्य सोमं क्रेष्यामस्तं ते प्रब्रूमस्त्सं त्वं विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः क्रतून्कल्पय दक्षिणाः कल्पय यथर्तु यथादेवतमित्यादित्यम् उपस्थाय सोमविक्रयिणे राजानं प्रदाय पणते
10.25.1.a.m: Having waited upon the sun with: 'O divine Sūrya, we are about to purchase Soma; we announce him to thee; arrange the rites for the All-gods, arrange the sacrificial gifts, according to the season, according to the deity,' [and] having handed the king (Soma) to the soma-seller, he bargains:

10.25.2.a.m: 'O soma-seller, is thy soma for sale?'

10.25.3.a.m: 'It is for sale,' the other replies.

10.25.4.a.s: somaṃ te krīṇāmyūrjasvantaṃ payasvantamityuktvā kalayā te krīṇānīty enam āha
10.25.4.a.d: सोमं ते क्रीणाम्यूर्जस्वन्तं पयस्वन्तमित्युक्त्वा कलया ते क्रीणानीत्य् एनम् आह
10.25.4.a.m: Having said: 'I purchase thy soma, rich in food, rich in sap,' he says to him: 'Let me purchase it for a sixteenth part (kalā).'

10.25.5.a.s: bhūyo vā ataḥ somo rājārhatīti sarveṣu paṇaneṣu somavikrayī pratyāhā saṃpadaḥ
10.25.5.a.d: भूयो वा अतः सोमो राजार्हतीति सर्वेषु पणनेषु सोमविक्रयी प्रत्याहा संपदः
10.25.5.a.m: 'King Soma is worth more than that,' the soma-seller replies at every bargaining, up to the completion.

10.25.6.a.m: 'Let me purchase it for an eighth part (kuṣṭhā),' [he says] a second time.

10.25.6.b.m: 'Let me purchase it for a quarter (śapha),' [he says] a third time.

10.25.6.c.m: 'Let me purchase it for a half (pad),' [he says] a fourth time.

10.25.9.a.m: 'Let me purchase it for a cow,' [he says] finally.

10.25.10.b.s: eṣeti nirdiśya japati tasyā ātmā tasyā ātmā tasyā rūpaṃ tasyāḥ prajā tasyāḥ payastasyā bandhuriti
10.25.10.b.d: एषेति निर्दिश्य जपति तस्या आत्मा तस्या आत्मा तस्या रूपं तस्याः प्रजा तस्याः पयस्तस्या बन्धुरिति
10.25.10.b.m: Pointing to it, he murmurs: 'She is its self, she is its self, she is its form, she is its offspring, she is its milk, she is its kin.'

10.25.11.a.s: śukraṃ te śukreṇa krīṇāmīti japitvā hiraṇyena krīṇāti
10.25.11.a.d: शुक्रं ते शुक्रेण क्रीणामीति जपित्वा हिरण्येन क्रीणाति
10.25.11.a.m: Having murmured: 'Bright with bright I purchase thee,' he purchases with gold.

10.25.12.a.m: Having murmured: 'Thou art the body of austerity,' he purchases with a she-goat.

10.25.14.a.m: If he should purchase with a bull, he would purchase with Prajāpati.

10.25.14.b.m: In its place is an uncastrated young bull.

10.25.15.a.m: [With the formula]: 'With a pair,' [it means] a young bull and a heifer.

10.25.16.a.m: Having purchased with those two together, he completes [the purchase] finally with a cloth.

10.26.1.a.m: [The purchase is made] with ten [articles] for a sacrifice with a sacrificial gift of one hundred and twelve [cows];

10.26.3.a.m: or with four: with a cow, with gold, with cloth, [and] with a she-goat, according to some.

10.26.4.a.m: With one [article] for [a sacrifice] with a sacrificial gift of twenty-one [cows];

10.26.4.b.m: with three for [a sacrifice] with a sacrificial gift of sixty [cows];

10.26.4.c.m: with an unmeasured number for [a sacrifice] with an unmeasured sacrificial gift;

10.26.5.a.m: with twenty-four for a thousand [cows] or for an all-property sacrifice;

10.26.6.a.m: or with thirty for [a sacrifice] with a thousand sacrificial gift:

10.26.7.a.s: saptaviṃśatirgā hiraṇyaṃ chāgā vāsa iti triṃśat
10.26.7.a.d: सप्तविंशतिर्गा हिरण्यं छागा वास इति त्रिंशत्
10.26.7.a.m: twenty-seven cows, gold, a she-goat, [and] a cloth—thus thirty;

10.26.9.a.m: with a thousand for an Aśvamedha.

10.26.10.a.m: With 'To us radiant things,' he takes back the gold from the soma-seller.

10.26.11.a.m: With 'To us light,' he hands a tuft of white wool to the sacrificer.

10.26.11.b.s: tāṃ sa kāle daśāpavitrasya nābhiṃ kurute
10.26.11.b.d: तां स काले दशापवित्रस्य नाभिं कुरुते
10.26.11.b.m: At the proper time, he makes that into the navel of the fringed filter.

10.26.12.a.m: The filter is of white [wool] from a white sheep, unwoven.

10.26.13.a.s: yaṃ dviṣyāttasya kṛṣṇāṃ lohinīṃ ca pavitre kuryāt
10.26.13.a.d: यं द्विष्यात्तस्य कृष्णां लोहिनीं च पवित्रे कुर्यात्
10.26.13.a.m: For him whom he hates, he should make a black and a reddish [wool tuft] in the filter.

10.26.14.a.s: kṛṣṇāmūrṇāstukāmadbhiḥ kledayitvedamahaṃ sarpāṇaṃ dandaśūkānāṃ grīvā upagrathnāmītyupagrathya tayā somavikriyiṇaṃ vidhyati somavikrayiṇi tama iti
10.26.14.a.d: कृष्णामूर्णास्तुकामद्भिः क्लेदयित्वेदमहं सर्पाणं दन्दशूकानां ग्रीवा उपग्रथ्नामीत्युपग्रथ्य तया सोमविक्रियिणं विध्यति सोमविक्रयिणि तम इति
10.26.14.a.m: Having moistened a tuft of black wool with water and tied it up with: 'Here do I tie up the necks of the biting snakes,' he strikes the soma-seller with it, [saying]: 'Darkness in the soma-seller!'

10.26.15.a.s: svāna bhrājeti somakrayaṇānanudiśya svajā asi svabhūrasyasmai karmaṇe jāta ṛtena tvā gṛhṇāmyṛtena mā pāhīti somavikrayiṇo rājānamapādatte
10.26.15.a.d: स्वान भ्राजेति सोमक्रयणाननुदिश्य स्वजा असि स्वभूरस्यस्मै कर्मणे जात ऋतेन त्वा गृह्णाम्यृतेन मा पाहीति सोमविक्रयिणो राजानमपादत्ते
10.26.15.a.m: Having addressed the articles used for purchasing soma with 'O Svāna, Bhrāja...', he takes the king (Soma) away from the soma-seller with: 'Thou art self-born, thou art self-existent, born for this rite; by truth I take thee, by truth protect me.'

10.26.16.a.m: If he should make difficulties, he should simply take it away.

10.27.2.a.s: sīkṣitadaṇḍaṃ ca maitrāvaruṇāya prayacchati mitrāvaruṇayostvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā prayacchāmyavakro 'vidhuro bhūyāsamiti
10.27.2.a.d: सीक्षितदण्डं च मैत्रावरुणाय प्रयच्छति मित्रावरुणयोस्त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा प्रयच्छाम्यवक्रो ऽविधुरो भूयासमिति
10.27.2.a.m: And he hands the staff of the consecrated one to the maitrāvaruṇa with: 'By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, I hand thee over; may I be upright and unbroken.'

10.27.3.a.s: mitro na ehīti yajamāno rājānamādāyendrasyorumāviśeti dakṣiṇa ūrāvāsādya hastābhyāṃ nigṛhyāste
10.27.3.a.d: मित्रो न एहीति यजमानो राजानमादायेन्द्रस्योरुमाविशेति दक्षिण ऊरावासाद्य हस्ताभ्यां निगृह्यास्ते
10.27.3.a.m: With 'Come as a friend to us,' the sacrificer, taking the king (Soma) and placing him on his right thigh with 'Enter Indra's thigh,' sits holding [him] with both hands.

10.27.4.a.m: Some teach here the waiting upon the sun, the handing over of the staff, and the addressing of the articles used for purchasing soma.

10.27.5.a.s: rudrastvāvartayatviti pradakṣiṇaṃsomakrayaṇīmāvartyānyayā gavā niṣkrīya yajamānasya goṣṭhe visṛjati
10.27.5.a.d: रुद्रस्त्वावर्तयत्विति प्रदक्षिणंसोमक्रयणीमावर्त्यान्यया गवा निष्क्रीय यजमानस्य गोष्ठे विसृजति
10.27.5.a.m: Having turned the cow used for purchasing soma around clockwise with 'May Rudra turn thee back,' and redeemed her with another cow, he releases [her] into the sacrificer's cow-pen.

10.27.6.a.s: yadi somavikrayī prativivadeta pṛṣatainaṃ vratrākāṇḍenāvakṣāyaṃ nāśayeyuḥ
10.27.6.a.d: यदि सोमविक्रयी प्रतिविवदेत पृषतैनं व्रत्राकाण्डेनावक्षायं नाशयेयुः
10.27.6.a.m: If the soma-seller should dispute, they should drive him away, blinding [him] with a spotted piece of cane.

10.27.7.a.m: 'They beat him with clubs,' say some.

10.27.8.a.m: Some teach the beating as an obligatory rule.

10.27.9.a.m: Taking the king (Soma) and rising with 'Up with life, with good life,' the sacrificer walks towards the cart with: 'Traverse the wide mid-space.'

10.27.10.a.s: adityāḥ sado 'sītyadhvaryuḥ śakaṭanīḍe kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīryādityāḥ sada āsīdeti tasminrājānamāsādya vaneṣu vyantarikṣaṃ tatāneti vāsasā paryānahyodu tyaṃ jātavedasamiti sauryarcā kṛṣṇājinaṃ purastātpratyānahyatyūrdhvagrīvaṃ bahiṣṭādviśasanam
10.27.10.a.d: अदित्याः सदो ऽसीत्यध्वर्युः शकटनीडे कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्यादित्याः सद आसीदेति तस्मिन्राजानमासाद्य वनेषु व्यन्तरिक्षं ततानेति वाससा पर्यानह्योदु त्यं जातवेदसमिति सौर्यर्चा कृष्णाजिनं पुरस्तात्प्रत्यानह्यत्यूर्ध्वग्रीवं बहिष्टाद्विशसनम्
10.27.10.a.m: With the formula 'You are the seat of Aditi,' the adhvaryu, having spread a black antelope skin with the neck to the east and the hair side up in the seat of the cart, having set the King [Soma] upon it with 'Sit upon the seat of Aditi,' having wrapped him around with a cloth with 'He stretched the atmosphere across the trees,' ties up the black antelope skin in front with the solar verse, 'Upward the knowledgeable one…' with its neck turned upward and the cut side facing out.

10.28.1.a.s: atra darśapūrṇamāsavaddhurāvabhimṛśya vāruṇamasīti śakaṭamākhidya varuṇastvottabhnātvityupastabhya varuṇasya skambhanamasīti śamyāṃ pratimucyosrāvetaṃ dhūrṣāhāvityanaḍvāhāvupājya vāruṇamasīti yoktrapāśaṃ parihṛtya pratyasto varuṇasya pāśa ityabhidhānīṃ pratyasyati
10.28.1.a.d: अत्र दर्शपूर्णमासवद्धुरावभिमृश्य वारुणमसीति शकटमाखिद्य वरुणस्त्वोत्तभ्नात्वित्युपस्तभ्य वरुणस्य स्कम्भनमसीति शम्यां प्रतिमुच्योस्रावेतं धूर्षाहावित्यनड्वाहावुपाज्य वारुणमसीति योक्त्रपाशं परिहृत्य प्रत्यस्तो वरुणस्य पाश इत्यभिधानीं प्रत्यस्यति
10.28.1.a.m: Here, having touched the two yoke-pins as in the New and Full Moon sacrifices, having pulled down the cart with 'You belong to Varuṇa,' having propped it up with 'May Varuṇa prop you up,' having fastened the yoke-peg with 'You are the prop of Varuṇa,' having driven up the two draft oxen with 'Come, you two bulls bearing the yoke,' having slipped around the yoke-strap loop with 'You belong to Varuṇa,' he fastens the halter with 'Cast away is the halter of Varuṇa.'

10.28.2.a.m: In the same manner, he yokes the northern ox.

10.28.3.a.m: Holding two green branches, the subrahmaṇya crawls between the two shafts,

10.28.3.b.m: or two palāśa branches, or two śamī branches.

10.28.4.a.s: athādhvaryuḥ śakaṭamanvārabhya saṃpreṣyati somāya rājñe krītāya prohyamāṇāyānubrūhi subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti
10.28.4.a.d: अथाध्वर्युः शकटमन्वारभ्य संप्रेष्यति सोमाय राज्ञे क्रीताय प्रोह्यमाणायानुब्रूहि सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति
10.28.4.a.m: Then the adhvaryu, holding onto the cart, issues the ritual call: 'Recite for King Soma, who has been purchased and is being conveyed forward; subrahmaṇya, call the subrahmaṇyā [litany]!'

10.28.5.a.s: sarvāsu subrahmaṇyāsu subrahmaṇyamanvārabhya yajamāno japati sāsi subrahmaṇye tasyāste pṛthivī pādaḥ /
10.28.5.a.d: सर्वासु सुब्रह्मण्यासु सुब्रह्मण्यमन्वारभ्य यजमानो जपति सासि सुब्रह्मण्ये तस्यास्ते पृथिवी पादः ।
10.28.5.a.m:
Holding onto the subrahmaṇya at all subrahmaṇyā [recitations], the sacrificer mutters: 'Such are you, O subrahmaṇyā; of you, the earth is a foot.

Such are you, O subrahmaṇyā; of you, the atmosphere is a foot.

10.28.5.b.m: Such are you, O subrahmaṇyā; of you, the sky is a foot.

10.28.5.c.m: Such are you, O subrahmaṇyā; of you, the directions are a foot.

10.28.5.e.m: Beyond the realm of space is your fifth foot.

10.28.5.f.s: sā na iṣamūrjaṃ dhukṣva teja indriyaṃ brahmavarcasamannādyam iti
10.28.5.f.d: सा न इषमूर्जं धुक्ष्व तेज इन्द्रियं ब्रह्मवर्चसमन्नाद्यम् इति
10.28.5.f.m: As such, milk out for us food and sap, fiery vigor, sensory faculty, spiritual luster, and consumable food.'

10.28.6.a.m: In this way, [he recites this] each time she is called three times.

10.28.7.a.m: When the first [litany] has been recited thrice,

10.29.1.a.d: प्रच्यवस्व भुवस्पत इति प्राञ्चो ऽभिप्रयाय प्रदक्षिणमावर्तन्ते
10.29.1.a.m: having stepped forward toward the east with 'Advance, O Lord of the world,' they turn around sunwise.

10.29.2.a.s: śyeno bhūtvā parāpatety adhvaryū rājānam abhimantrayate
10.29.2.a.d: श्येनो भूत्वा परापतेत्य् अध्वर्यू राजानम् अभिमन्त्रयते
10.29.2.a.m: With 'Becoming a falcon, fly away,' the two adhvaryus address the King [Soma].

10.29.3.a.m: With 'We have reached the path,' the adhvaryu and the sacrificer walk across past the King [Soma] on the south or on the north.

10.29.4.a.s: ajenāgnīṣomīyeṇa karṇagṛhītena yajamāno rājānamohyamānaṃ pratīkṣate namo mitrasyeti
10.29.4.a.d: अजेनाग्नीषोमीयेण कर्णगृहीतेन यजमानो राजानमोह्यमानं प्रतीक्षते नमो मित्रस्येति
10.29.4.a.m: With the goat meant for Agni and Soma held by its ear, the sacrificer looks at the King being conveyed, with 'Homage to the eye of Mitra…'

10.29.7.a.m: There is a chair made of udumbara wood, with headpieces and side-rails of a cubit's length, legs reaching up to the navel, woven with muñja grass;
